12623922.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12623922.value: 社會工作價值和倫理觀（側重於促進人權和社會義）乃社會工作專業的基石。然而，這些價值和道德倫理觀被認為已被全球轉向占主導地位的政治經濟意識形態，即新自由主義，通過過去幾十年在社會福利服務中實施管理主義和新公共管理而受到影響。市場競爭不但改變了福利服務行業，對社會工作行業固有的傳統價值觀更是一大挑戰。在短期合同、注重靈活性和流動性的管理文化中，同工也可能被塑造為一個關注自我的策略者，對社會工作價值觀有所妥協。 儘管有大量關於新自由主義的困境和影響的文獻，但對社會工作者所面臨的實際情況和道德困境、他們如何處理這些困境以及促成道德決策的具體因素的實證分析卻很少。首先，沒有定量研究研究過全球的情況。另外，世界各地的社會工作者認證機構發布的職業道德規範雖然能夠規範社會工作者的職業操守，但它能否抵消管理主義在提供社會服務方面的影響也仍然是一個疑問。 擬議的研究將會考量新自由主義價值觀，通過管理主義，對提供社會服務的影響，並測量道德守則作為確保職業操守的作用。以香港為案例研究，本研究將採用準實驗研究設計，並以混合方法研究途徑進行。主要目的是根據新自由主義管理主義的特點，分析社會工作者在面臨倫理困境時的專業決策過程，發掘影響其倫理判斷的各種因素，並探討各因素之間的相互作用。計劃初期會先進行一項德爾福研究，以 (1) 辨識社會工作者面臨的相關道德困境以及影響他們作出道德判斷和決定的因素；(2) 組成不同的簡短情景描述（小插曲）。第二階段將會採用羅西 (1974) 的析因調查法，通過在線平台，邀請至少900名參與者進行問卷調查，探討他們對以上的簡短情景描述（小插曲）所作出的回應。其後，本研究會進行多級（邏輯）回歸分析，以尋找影響其道德判斷的因素。

12624122.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12624122.value: 看見不可見：近現代歐洲（1400-1700）對殘障的視覺呈現

12624122.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12624122.value: Abstract: The proposed project is the first study that comprehensively analyses how disability and impairment were represented in western art, focusing on the period 1400–1700. Situated at the crossroads between art history, social history and disability studies, it locates understandings of disability in the context of history, medicine, literature and visual culture. By looking at a wide range of visual and written sources, it maps the different attitudes that early modern societies had towards disability and analyses the intellectual framework within which disability was positioned. Furthermore, it examines how impairment affected the everyday life of people and highlights the presence of artists with disabilities in the history of art, using their artworks, notebooks, letters and documents pertaining to their life to describe how through art practice they asserted their own profession, identity and even citizenship. The study investigates visual sources that relate to and/or portray disability and impairment by dividing them into five categories: i) religious images portraying miraculous and charitable actions; ii) scientific illustrations related to medical conditions; iii) genre paintings detailing scenes of daily life; iv) portraits of people with disabilities; v) artworks created by artists with disabilities. These images are not considered as historical documents in the narrow sense but rather as records that reflect personal and social reactions and interpretations of impairment. They highlight that disability as we understand it today did not fully exist in the early modern period and demonstrate that the consideration of intersectional factors such as age, gender and social status were essential to how people responded to impairment. Aside from investigating historical constructs of disability, the project retraces the personal and professional stories of early modern artists. Some, such as the celebrated Dutch printmaker Hendrick Goltzius, took advantage of their disability achieving unprecedented technical virtuosity. Others, such as the Italian sculptor Giovanni Gonnelli, have almost completely been forgotten. Responding to recent calls in the fields of art history, social history and disability studies, the proposed project looks for the very first time at art practice, visual culture and disability in the early modern period, addressing a major research gap in contemporary scholarly literature. 摘要： 此研究項目將首次全面分析西方藝術界於1400-1700年間對殘障的呈現，它將結合藝術史、社會史及殘障研究，在歷史、醫藥史、文學和視覺藝術的語境下來重新認識殘障。通過研究大量的視覺和書面資料，該項目系統地呈現出近現代社會對殘障的各種態度，並分析殘障被置於的知識框架。並且，此研究將探討殘障如何影響了人們的日常生活，並著重指出藝術史中殘障藝術家一直存在，通過研究他們的作品、筆記、書信以及其他生活相關的材料，描繪出他們是如何通過藝術實踐來堅持和維護自己的職業、身份甚至國籍。此研究把與殘障相關的視覺藝術資料分成五類：1）描繪神跡和慈善活動的宗教圖像，2）與疾病相關的科學圖解，3）描繪生活細節的類型繪畫，4）包含殘障人士的繪畫，5）殘障藝術家創作的作品。這些圖像並不是狹義的歷史檔案，而是記錄並反映了個人及社會對殘障的認知和態度，它們體現了我們今天所認知的殘障在當時還未完全存在，以及人們對殘障的態度取決於年齡、性別以及社會階層等各種因素。除了研究殘障的歷史構建，此研究還追蹤了近現代藝術家的個人和職業發展經歷，其中有的人，比如著名的荷蘭版畫家亨德裏克·霍爾奇尼斯，巧用自己的殘障取得了空前的精湛技藝；有的人，比如意大利雕塑家喬瓦尼·貢內裏，則被完全遺忘了。響應藝術史、社會史以及殘障研究近期的需求，該研究將首次聚焦近現代藝術實踐和視覺藝術中對殘障的呈現，彌補當代學術界的一大研究空缺。

12624322.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12624322.value: 從電視到數字媒體：家長調節範式的轉變

12624322.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12624322.value: Dr Chen, Liang Prof Lwin, May Oo

12624322.label: Project Objectives
12624322.value: The project’s first objective is to explore how Asian parents (in Hong Kong, Mainland China, and Singapore) mediate their children’s digital media use in a rapidly changing digital media landscape. That objective will be addressed by answering the following research questions via in-depth interviews with parent-child dyads: Research Question 1: How is parental mediation of digital media practiced in the Asian context to balance the risks and benefits of digital media use among children? The second objective is to understand and develop a clear typologies of Asian parents’ parental mediation strategies of digital media. The objective will be addressed by analyzing data from mixed methods of in-depth interviews as well as cross-national surveys with parent-child dyads conducted in Hong Kong, Mainland China, and Singapore. Research Question 2: What are the typologies of parental mediation strategies for children’s digital media use in Asian contexts? The third objective is to investigate the effects of each parental mediation strategy on the risks and benefits of children’s digital media use and to compare findings from the three Asian locations. Digital media have posed several types of risk to young users, such as stealing personal information, introducing cyberbullying, perpetuating ideologies (e.g., being obsessed with physical perfection, and rise of materialism among children), and keeping children addicted to smartphones or video games. Nevertheless, the digital media has also provided children with tremendous opportunities to improve digital skills, engage in learning activities, socialize with peers, and reach people beyond their own communities. Thus, the third objective is to examine the effects of parental mediation on the various outcomes of digital media use. Research Question 3a: How does each type of parental mediation strategy of digital media affect the risks of digital media encountered by children in Hong Kong, Mainland China, and Singapore? Research Question 3b: How does each type of parental mediation strategy of digital media affect the benefits of digital media utilized by children in Hong Kong, Mainland China, and Singapore? The fourth objective is to provide theory-driven recommendations on parental mediation of digital media for parents, educators, policy makers, and the digital media industry, especially in the Asian context. Such recommendations may include instrumental guidance on how parents could better mediate their children’s digital media use to balance risks and benefits. Such enhancement of digital skills can enable children to become more adapt in their digital learning and countering of risks in. The project also aims to offer insights on education and policy making to improve digital media skills and literacy for both parents and children, regardless of background, to help users become more resilient and to address digital divides in society. Findings from the proposed project will also offer recommendations for the digital media industry for their technology (e.g. application and software developments) to facilitate parental mediation practices, reduce user risks, and enhance parent-child joint digital media engagement.

12625122.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12625122.value: While playing a video game such as, say, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998), players might notice that their gameplay directly affects the musical output of the game. For example, Ocarina-players might notice that the game’s music becomes more tense, exciting and dramatic in thematic content as they direct Link, the series protagonist, toward an enemy monster. Video game music composers, or “game scorers” design and program musical changes such as these, with the aim of elucidating gaming activity as it happens in real-time, and so they undertake compositional activities that do not inhere in scoring for non-interactive media, or traditional compositional modes. Despite this fact, little research is done to explain how game scores are composed differently from other forms of music. The proposed project examines game scoring from a compositional perspective. Musicians and composers need to understand game scoring’s differences from traditional modes of composition, in order to see it not only as a lucrative venue for their musical practice, but also as an inspiring and creatively fulfilling one. The main questions that will inform the proposed project are: (a) How is game scoring different from scoring for other media, and from traditional composition?; (b) what types of compositional strategies do game scorers adopt in musically responding to an interactive art form?; and (c) how can aspiring game scorers without any programming background practice the design and creation of interactive music systems? I will explore how modern game scorers are designed and programmed, through (i) interviews with game scorers, designers and programmers working for both corporate and independent developers; (ii) case studies of interactive music systems for games; and (iii) a critical analysis of current game music programming software. More than two billion people worldwide play computer and video games at least an hour a day. Each of these games has a soundtrack, and every gameplay experience is accompanied by a score. Very little research is done, however, to explain how the music these gamers hear every day is designed differently from other forms of music, and how game scorers devise and undertake entirely different musical and compositional methods to accommodate those differences. The proposed project is intended to begin the process of addressing this gap in scholarship, facilitate a proper understanding of this musical practice to aspiring game scorers, and provide musicians and composers with an avenue to practice skills that are fundamental to game scoring activity. 12626622.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12626622.value: 出土文獻《反淫 》與《妄稽》背景下的早期哲學著作中的「淫」概念

12626622.label: Project Objectives
12626622.value: During the current project, the PI first intends to translate the Fan yin and Wang Ji into English. This is a challenging task, considering the highly sophisticated language of the two works. However, the PI is experienced in dealing with texts couched in poetic form (Daoist and otherwise). An analysis of the philosophical ideas contained in the two texts will be provided. To this end, different stages in the respective processes leading to the healing or the outbreak of sickness will be investigated. The philosophical ideas underlining the depictions of the resulting states will also be explored. The relationship between the Fan yin and Mei Sheng’s Qi fa will be investigated. The PI intends to look into the relationship between the Fan yin and the Wang Ji and other manuscripts from the same text corpus with philosophical and literary content. Their parallels need to be addressed as they might be suggestive of certain textual practices in early China and reveal more information about the philosophical views of their owner. The present study intends to investigate the philosophical underpinnings of the notion of “immoderation” in the Daoist classics. Its appearance in Daoist works will be compared to the Confucian critique of the notion yin. The project aims to investigate the early Chinese philosophical and medical works regarding their approach to “immoderation”. The main question to be answered here is whether there is evidence that political, philosophical, and medical handling of immoderation, its causes and effects was based on similar principles. To reach this goal, a comparison with medical literature will be carried out. Early stages of the development of the literary genre of fu will be investigated.

12626622.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12626622.value: This project aims to investigate the philosophical significance of the notion of “immoderation” (yin 淫) in early Chinese philosophy and poetry. As a starting point for this investigation, the PI has chosen the newly discovered manuscript Fan yin 反淫 (Contra Immoderation), which belongs to the corpus of bamboo manuscripts donated to Peking University in 2009. The Fan yin is structured as a dialogue between the “ethereal soul” (hun 魂) and “corporeal soul” (po 魄): the former depicts several enticing scenes of pleasant activities such as listening to music, hunting, fishing etc. to facilitate healing of the ailing “corporeal soul”. In the end, the po shows signs of convalescence only after being instructed in what comes very close to a poetic representation of the Way (dao 道) especially as it was promulgated in the Zhuangzi 莊子 and Huainanzi 淮南子. The next manuscript to be investigated is the Wang Ji 妄稽, likewise part of the Peking University collection. Here, the eponymous protagonist is portrayed as an utterly repulsive woman who, driven by jealousy (du 妒) towards her husband’s beautiful concubine, adopts increasingly desperate and brutal measures. In the end, she develops a serious disease and succumbs to it. On her deathbed, she realizes that her jealousy was caused by her ignorance of the “decree of heaven” (tian ming 天命). Therefore, in both cases, the decisive factor for convalescing or developing a sickness is determined as the realization of higher principles, which preclude “immoderate” actions. Following this, the two manuscripts will be compared to other texts of the same collection, such as the Laozi and Zhou xun, in which notions belonging to medical discourse serve as a means to address political issues. The investigation of the common philosophical features of this collection might help shed more light onto the intellectual and political views of their unknown owner. In the final step, the PI will proceed to examine the earliest examples for the notion of “immoderation” in Daoist texts. While the notion is absent in the Laozi, it plays an important role in the Zhuangzi, the Huainanzi and the Wenzi. This analysis will be carried out against the background of the Confucian understanding of yin and will be informed by the correspondence between the medical and political discourses in early China. 本項目旨在分析中國早期哲學和詩歌中「淫」概念的哲學意義。 作為研究的起點，PI選擇了出土文獻《反淫》。該文獻屬於2009年捐贈給北京大學的西漢竹書。《反淫》描述的是一場「魂」與「魄」的對話。前者描繪了幾個令人愉快的活動，如聽音樂、打獵、釣魚等，以促進生病的「魄」的治愈。最後，讓「魄」顯示恢復的跡象是「魂」對「道」的描述。它非常接近《莊子》和《淮南子》中相關的思想。 下一部要分析的文獻是同樣屬於北大西漢竹書的《妄稽》。在此，同名的主人公被描繪為一位完全令人厭惡的女人。在嫉妒的驅使下，她對丈夫美麗的妃子採取了越來越殘酷的措施。最後，她患上了嚴重的疾病。臨終前，她意識到自己的嫉妒是由於她對「天命」的無知造成的。因此，在這兩部作品當中，康復或得病的決定性因素都被確定為對「道」或「天」的把握。 在此之後，PI蔣要把這兩部文獻與其他的北大西漢竹書進行比較，例如《老子》和《周訓》等。其中某些本來屬於醫學範圍的概念被用來描述政治策略與手段。這種調查可能有助於更好地了北大西漢竹書的主人的政治觀點。 在最後一步中，PI 將繼續研究道家作品中最早的「淫」概念的例子。雖然《老子》沒有這個概念，但它在《莊子》、《淮南子》和《文子》中發揮了重要作用。此研究項目將以儒家對「淫」的理解為背景，並以中國早期醫學和政治術語之間的對應關係為依據。

13500022.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13500022.value: 了解眾籌項目的視頻內容： 視頻處理和特徵提取的深度學習方法

13500022.label: Co - Investigator(s)
13500022.value: Prof CUI, Geng Prof Jia, Jianmin Prof PENG, Ling

13500022.label: Project Objectives
13500022.value: Conduct one of the first empirical studies to examine how pitch video and its design contents are related to video content engagement and project outcomes (e.g., funding success and fundraising amount). Prior work has identified a wide range of factors that influence fundraising success. These factors can be categorized as those related to (1) the characteristics of creators, (2) the characteristics of backers, and (3) the characteristics of crowdfunding projects. Although prior work has considered different project-specific factors and their effect on the amount pledged and the success of crowdfunding (Hong, Hu, and Burtch 2018; Kuppuswamy and Bayus 2017; Mollick 2014), only a limited amount of research has considered the influence of video content design, which is a key component of a crowdfunding project. In particular, we propose a novel Video Analytical Framework (VAF) by integrating the recent advance of computer vision technologies and deep learning methodologies to help marketers understand video consumption from a content analysis. Specifically, the proposed framework can be used to automatically extract the various types of video features (BEST) in the pitch videos and analyze how these features are related to the project outcomes (e.g., project success and funding amount). Examine the relationship between video content design and financial outcome by examining the four major aspects of video features. Although previous work has explored the roles of video features in different contexts (e.g., standard commercial TVs), most studies have been conducted in small-scale laboratory settings or artificial conditions (Baumgartner, Sujan, and Padgett 1997; Polsfuss and Hess 1991; Teixeira, Wedel, and Pieters 2010). We will study the video features in an empirical setting with over 69,000 Kickstarter videos. Additionally, we employ a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model and transfer learning approach to analyze unstructured video data in a more scalable and automatic manner. [methodological] Examine the influence of various video features on different types of crowdfunding projects. The crowdfunding platform offers a wide range of projects from product-driven products (e.g., creating an early product prototype for presell) to prosocial causes (e.g., building a primary school in a rural area). Research suggests that backers may have different goal pursuits for backing the product-driven projects and prosocial projects, which are the two major project categories in crowdfunding (Dai and Zhang 2019; Hong, Hu, and Burtch 2018). In this study, we expect that Brand and Technology scores will exert disproportionally greater influence on product-driven projects, whereas Social and Emotional scores will exert disproportionally greater influence on prosocial projects. [theoretical] Provide advice on the management, planning, and design of pitch video and its contents. Prior work has not clearly provided practical implications describing how to create an interesting and engaging pitch video. Before launching the crowdfunding project, a project creator should focus on the four key aspects of video features (i.e., brand, emotion, social, and technology) to increase video content engagement. This study will provide a strategic roadmap for designing video content. [practical] Inform researchers, project creators, and crowdfunding operators about the importance of video content design in affecting a project’s pledged amount and crowdfunding success. [practical]

13500022.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13500022.value: 視頻作為有效的品牌故事講述和消費者聯繫的重要性不斷增長。根據 Hubspot（2021 年）最近的一份報告指出，視頻已取代博客和信息圖表，成為內容營銷中最流行的使用格式。人們對視頻分析、機器學習和計算機視覺領域的興趣與日俱增。然而，當前的大部分研究和開發工作主要集中在各種監控視頻應用的運動檢測和對象跟踪上。在線視頻共享平台（如 YouTube）和直播應用平台（如 抖音）中海量的視頻內容為營銷人員更好地了解和與客戶溝通提供了新的機會。雖然在收集和處理視頻消費數據方面取得了很大進展，但從非結構化視頻數據中分析和處理仍然是一項重大的技術和方法挑戰。視頻是富媒體內容，需要多模態處理；現有的研究大多是僅對視頻數據的一個方面進行零散分析：文本（腳本）、圖像、聲音或語音，並且通常在視頻級別進行匯總。提取有價值的特徵和對豐富的視頻數據進行系統分析一直困擾著研究人員和從業者，並且仍然是視頻研究的一項重大挑戰。 在這項研究中，我們提出了一種新穎的視頻分析框架，結合計算機視覺技術和深度學習方法的最新進展，對來自 Kickstarter 上 69,000 多個項目的獨特視頻數據集進行實證分析。我們構建和開發新的視頻功能，命名為 BEST（品牌、情感、社交和技術）分數，以評估視頻內容參與度，並分析這些功能與眾籌項目成果（例如，籌款成功和眾籌金額）的關係。我們還研究了社交和情感得分如何對親社會項目產生不成比例的更大影響，以及品牌和技術得分如何對產品驅動的項目產生不成比例的更大影響。我們將採用遷移學習方法來訓練和驗證我們的捲積神經網絡 (CNN) 模型，並提取視頻幀中的顯著圖像特徵。這種方法不僅提高了模型解釋和特徵提取能力，防止了模型過度擬合的風險，而且提高了計算效率和可擴展性。 這項研究將加深我們過去通常只關注的視頻是否存在，從而擴展我們對視頻內容設計的理解。 結果的影響相關性也將是深遠的，因為營銷人員和客戶每天都會創建大量用戶生成的視頻。 例如，每天有數千個新的推介視頻上傳到眾籌平台（如 Kickstarter）。 快速了解視頻內容並準確預測客戶行為的能力可以為營銷人員提供非常有用的知識，以提高客戶參與度。 此外，這項研究將提供有關視頻內容設計的寶貴信息，以促進戰略規劃並提供實用指導。項目創建者可以通過提高他們的宣傳視頻的製作能力來吸引支持者的注意力，並提高籌款成功率，從而從這項研究中受益。

13500322.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13500322.value: This project will establish an axiomatically founded robust smooth ambiguity model by integrating an exogenously given background risk into the model of KMM. 13500322.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500322.value: We explore how introducing background risk (BR) alters ambiguity aversion. The proposed model extends the KMM model by accounting for independent BR and introduces an additional effect on ambiguity aversion due to incomplete separation between risk and ambiguity attitudes. The relationship between risk aversion and ambiguity aversion is further explored, addressing concerns about incorporating BRs directly into the KMM framework. The Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization is presently reviewing one paper, while two others have undergone revisions and resubmitted to Management Science and Insurance: Mathematics and Economics

13500322.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13500322.value: We will try to dig deeper into the applications of this model.

13500322.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500322.value: The key observation is that introducing an unfair background risk to wealth makes the decision-maker exhibit increased risk aversion confronting other independent risks. This effect is termed risk vulnerability. Specifically, we demonstrate that two competing elements determine ambiguity attitudes in light of background risk. On one side, standard ambiguity aversion engenders an aversion to ambiguity in the decision-maker. Conversely, risk vulnerability triggers a stronger tendency towards seeking ambiguity. Consequently, in the presence of background risk, the decision-maker must have an adequately high degree of standard ambiguity aversion to retain an ambiguity-averse stance.

13500622.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13500622.value: 内幕信息与公司披露和融资政策：来自卫星数据和田野实验的证据

13500622.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13500622.value: Firm managers possess private information about their firms that outside investors do not have access to (i.e., insider information). Such information asymmetry affects a wide range of corporate decisions. However, insider information is difficult to observe, impeding efforts to detect selective disclosure and prove that some insiders misuse nonpublic information. In this project, we will use a novel measure of insider information and examine its effects on corporate disclosure and financial policies. Specifically, we will exploit satellite data to identify the thermal infrared radiation (TIR) emitted during firms’ operation and production processes. Firms facing increased demand expand their operation and production activities, thus emitting stronger TIR. Unlike indicators of performance used in the literature, such as stakeholders’ reviews and other satellite-imagery-based indicators (e.g., car counts), TIR is anchored to insiders’ operation decisions but unobservable by outsiders, as it is not visible to the human eye. The level of TIR thus measures insiders’ private information about firms’ fundamentals. We will use TIR to test whether insiders have an incentive to hide bad news and disclose good news. To this end, we will conduct a field experiment by exploiting a unique disclosure mechanism in China, namely company site visits, which are investors’ field trips to corporate production facilities to obtain firm-specific information. Specifically, we will randomize firms into two groups, focal and control. We will contact each firm in the focal group and request visits to the firm’s randomly selected factories that have either high or low TIR. Similar requests will be made to firms in the control group, for which factories will be randomly selected (independent of TIR). If our hypothesis is true, focal group firms would be more (less) likely to grant visits to factories with high (low) TIR while control group firms will show indistinctive responses to the visit requests. To generalize our results, we will use archival data to examine whether TIR is positively related to the intensity of company site visits and voluntary managerial forecasts. We will also examine how our findings vary with managerial career concerns and equity incentives. Moreover, we will examine whether managers are more likely to buy (sell) their firms’ stock and reduce (increase) equity issuance when TIR is high (low). The preliminary results of the experimental and archival analysis suggest that managers indeed disclose corporate information strategically. This project will provide direct evidence of the influence of insiders’ private information on corporate decision-making. 公司经理拥有外部投资者无法获得的公司信息（即内幕信息）。这种信息不对称对公司的决策有广泛影响。然而，内幕信息很难被观察到，这让发现公司存在选择性披露和证明其滥用公司内幕信息的行为变的异常困难。在这个项目中，我们将使用一种全新的衡量内幕信息的方法，并借以检查内幕信息对公司披露和财务政策的影响。 具体来说，我们将利用卫星数据来识别企业运营和生产过程中发出的热红外辐射（TIR）。公司在面临需求增加的时候会扩大其经营和生产活动，从而产生更强的 TIR。不同于现有文献中使用的指标，例如公司利益相关者对公司的评论和其他基于卫星图像的指标（例如汽车数量），TIR 直接和公司高管的运营决策挂扣并且无法被外面的人观察到因为TIR对人类的肉眼是不可见的。因此，TIR 的水平可以衡量公司高管关于公司基本面的私人信息。 我们将使用 TIR 来测试公司高管是否有隐瞒坏消息和披露好消息的动机。具体地，我们将利用中国独特的披露机制进行一个田野试验。投资者经常通过实地调研企业生产设施来去获取公司的信息。为此，我们将公司随机分为两组，实验组和控制组。我们将联系实验组中的每家公司，并申请调研该公司的两家工厂。这两家工厂是随机选择的但保证一个的TIR 高一个的TIR低。我们也将向控制组中的公司提出类似的申请。控制组组里的工厂是随机的他们的选择和TIR无关。如果我们的假设是正确的，实验组公司将更有（更少）可能接受我们访问其具有TIR高（低）工厂的请求，而控制组公司对访问其工厂的请求平均而言将没有明显差别。 为了证明我们的结果具有一般性，我们将使用历史数据来检验 TIR 是否与公司实地调研和公司的自愿披露的强度有正相关。我们还将研究我们的发现如何随着经理人的职业担忧和股权激励变化而变化。此外，我们将研究公司管理层是否更有可能在 TIR 高（低）时购买（出售）其公司的股票并减少（增加）股票发行。 实验和历史分析的初步结果表明，公司高管确实会进行战略性的披露公司信息。该项目将提供公司高管私人信息对公司决策影响的直接证据。

13500722.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13500722.value: The question of how female business leadership affects business outcomes is of increasing interest as women’s representation has grown in recent years (Matsa and Miller 2011). It is well argued in the literature that female leadership has the potential to influence firm financial performance and risk taking (e.g., Francis et al., 2013; Huang and Ksigen, 2013) and financial reporting (e.g., Fan et al., 2019; García Lara et al., 2017) among other corporate policies; however, a very limited number of studies have been undertaken to examine whether this also applies to non-financial performance including CSR (e.g., Bear et al., 2010; Jia and Zhang, 2013; McGuinness et al., 2017; Liu 2018). Specifically, to the best of our knowledge, there is no literature on the relationship between female leadership and customers. We intend to fill in this gap by studying how female leadership affects the welfare of customers, an important stakeholder group. Female leaders have heightened sensitivity to ethical issues and are more stakeholder-oriented than their male counterparts (Adams and Ferreira, 2009; Adams and Funk, 2012; Adams et al., 2011). We posit that female leadership improves the firm-customer relationship. We proxy customer treatment using a unique dataset on consumer complaints in insurance and adjudicated outcomes to state regulators. Next, we analyze the possible channels through which female leadership affects customer treatment: underwriting services or claim settlement. To assess whether this complaint gap stems from complaint-prone customers in insurers with male leadership, we assess state-adjudicated complaint success. To further delineate between customer selection or treatment explanations, we exploit within insurer complaints around natural disasters. Tests of complaints within insurers before and after random shocks allow us to hold the profiles of the insurers’ consumers and mix of insurance products constant. We further investigate whether female leadership helps improve the firm-customer relationship potentially at the cost to shareholder interests in the short term but to the benefit of shareholders in the long term, due to enhanced customer loyalty. We then study under what conditions the relationship between female leadership and complaints is mitigated or enhanced by regulation or market pressures on firm reputation. Finally, we test our analyses on the relationship between female CEOs and customer complaints using alternative definition of female leadership, i.e., female presence on board. We further study whether the aforementioned female-complaint relationship is mainly driven by female CEO, or female board membership, or both, due to synergy effects related to the critical mass theory.

13500722.label: Realisation of objectives
13500722.value: Generally, we follow the original plan and realize all project objectives. We found some interesting results that were counterintuitive, revealing a surprising relationship between female leadership and customer satisfaction that deviated from our original hypotheses. More specifically. expanding upon the burgeoning field of research that explores the role of CEO gender, the question of whether specific circumstances grant female CEOs a unique advantage remains unaddressed. In pursuit of a deeper understanding, we developed and examined three hypothesis sets relating to female CEOs and their management of regulatory compliance processes. Initially, our findings show a higher prevalence of female CEOs in insurers subject stringent regulation than in lax-regulated ones. This finding regarding the first hypothesis addresses Project Objective 4. Subsequently, our inquiry delves into regulatory adherence within the insurance sector by examining customer complaints to officials of over 1,750 firms. We scrutinize the frequency and success rates of customer grievances in companies helmed by female CEOs, contrasting these with firms led by their male counterparts. Contrary to widespread assumptions, the data reveals that insurance companies under female leadership receive more customer complaints than firms headed by men. Evidence on the second hypothesis satisfies Project Objective 1. However, the adjudication success rates are strikingly similar for male and female CEO firms. Interestingly, the increased number of complaints does not result in heightened reputational damage for female-led firms in the eyes of regulators. Evidence on Hypothesis 3 advances Project Objective 3 and implies that the consumer welfare effects of female CEO leadership may be durable, provided it does not trigger regulatory intervention or reputational harm. We probe customer-facing mechanisms—underwriting and claims—using the NAIC’s detailed complaint taxonomy by type and reason. Relative to male-led counterparts, insurers with women CEOs receive significantly more complaints in claim handling (+9%), marketing and sales (+13%), and policyholder service (+17%), with no difference in underwriting. By reason, they attract more complaints about claim issues (+18%), policy termination (+9%), pricing/terms (+7%), and customer care (+8%), with no difference in misconduct. These patterns are consistent with stricter claims management and cost containment, potentially at the expense of service quality. This evidence helps address project objective 2. We conducted a battery of robustness tests, including the PSM matched sample and Entropy matched sample, IV method, and DiD analyses. The results consistently showed that insurers with female CEOs had more complaints than those with male CEOs. We also used the staggered implementation of the ACA Medicaid Expansion among states as a source of exogenous claim shocks to insurers. The findings supported our interpretation that insurers with female CEOs provided poorer service to their customers and suggested a causal effect of CEO gender on customer satisfaction. We posit that female CEOs' resilience and adept reputation management skills empower them to navigate regulatory scrutiny and cultivate favorable stakeholder relations. At first glance, it may seem surprising that the higher number of complaints does not translate into greater reputational damage for female-led firms in the eyes of regulators. We interpret these findings as evidence supporting the hypothesis that female managers possess superior communication skills when engaging with insurance regulators. Note that we are not suggesting that female CEOs allocate resources to communicate directly with individual insurance customers. Given the vast number of individual insurance consumers—in contrast to the limited number of state regulators—it is improbable that the personal efforts of female CEOs would significantly reduce complaints. To fulfil project object 5, we next examine the relationship between the disparity in complaints against insurers led by female versus male CEOs and the strength of the regulatory environment. Insurance firms face state-level regulation, with each state operating independently; stricter regimes may enhance consumer protection oversight. Although most insurers operate across multiple states, primary regulatory responsibility falls to the domicile state to avoid duplicative efforts. Notably, states with more regulatory staff or larger budgets exhibit greater complaint disparities between female- and male-led insurers. We find no evidence that market competition attenuates the association between female leadership and consumer complaints. Furthermore, our findings on the impact of female board representation on insurer complaints are inconsistent, thereby addressing objective 6. We conduct supplementary analyses employing alternative proxies for regulatory favoritism toward female executives. The property and casualty (P&C) insurance sector is subject to state-level regulation, necessitating that firms submit applications to regulators for product modifications—including rates, forms, and rules—in each state of operation. For example, more than 1,100 insurers provide private passenger automobile coverage in the United States and filed over 57,000 rate submissions for price adjustments between 2007 and 2021. The approval procedure is frequently onerous and protracted, with standard filings surpassing 1,000 pages and entailing substantial iterative correspondence between insurers and regulators. Regulatory decisions exhibit variation across jurisdictions: certain authorities grant full approval to rate applications, whereas others may deny or grant partial approval. Should female CEOs demonstrate superior communicative proficiency with regulators, we posit that their rate-increase submissions would yield more advantageous outcomes. Empirical evidence confirms that female CEOs attain higher approval rates for such submissions relative to their male counterparts. Our findings bear implications for selecting and grooming leaders within the insurance industry. They offer valuable insights into the significance of gender in executive leadership and illuminate the capabilities of female CEOs in managing regulators.

13500722.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500722.value: This study examines how CEO gender influences regulatory management in the highly regulated insurance industry by analyzing customer complaints and regulatory outcomes. We posit that women CEOs' resilience and reputation management skills empower them to navigate regulatory scrutiny, allowing their firms to choose more aggressive customer claims and handling strategies. While prior research has explored gender differences in CEO performance, the role of gender in managing regulatory relationships remains understudied. Using state-level insurance data, we find three patterns: women CEOs are more prevalent in states with stringent oversight; their firms experience more customer complaints; yet they achieve similar success rates in regulatory adjudication as male-led firms. These findings illuminate how gender shapes executive leadership in regulated industries. The paper has been presented at the 2024 China International Conference on Insurance and Risk Management, IIRM Conference on Risk and Uncertainty, Lingnan University, National Chengchi University, National Taiwan University, Renmin University of China, and Shanghai University of Finance and Economics.

13500722.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13500722.value: We observe a significant impact of female CEOs on the quality of insurance loss reserves and financial ratings. Two additional papers have been developed on these topics. We are formulating further hypotheses to investigate how insurers' regulatory arbitrage leads to inconsistent consumer protections across states.

13500722.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500722.value: Women CEOs are increasingly recognized for their unique leadership capabilities, but how do they perform in highly regulated industries? Our study of the insurance industry reveals interesting insights for boards and executives. We find that women CEOs are particularly effective at managing regulatory relationships, enabling their firms to pursue more aggressive claims-handling strategies without suffering negative consequences. While insurance companies led by women receive more customer complaints, they maintain similar success rates in regulatory proceedings as firms led by men. This suggests women CEOs excel at building and maintaining strong relationships with regulators - a crucial skill in today's complex regulatory environment. For boards seeking leaders in regulated industries, these findings highlight the strategic advantage women CEOs can bring to regulatory management.

13500822.label: Project Title(Chinese)
13500822.value: 是否应在在线市场上披露交货时间评级？具有经验数据支持的理论模型的最优定价和承诺交货时间决策

13500822.label: Project Objectives
13500822.value: We will investigate whether or not online retailing firms should disclose on their websites the delivery-time ratings provided by their customers. In a survey of 18,430 online shoppers across more than 50 countries [22], 43% of those shoppers reported that delivery service is the most important attribute of online offerings (second only to price at 57%). The survey also revealed that delivery time is by far the most influential aspect of delivery service. Another survey focusing on different aspects of delivery service [4] exposed that 74% of U.S. consumers are willing to pay more for fast delivery, and 75% care about on-time delivery (a.k.a. delivery-time conformance). Prior to receiving products, consumers are not sure if the deliveries can be completed within the times promised by online retailing firms. To predict the likelihood of delivery-time conformance, consumers usually refer to the delivery-time ratings posted online (if allowed by online retailing firms). When such ratings are available, the actual delivery time has a significant impact on customer satisfaction [19] as well as delivery ratings and sales [12]. As the disclosure of delivery ratings has its pros and cons, it behooves us to explore under what conditions online retailing firms benefit from posting the delivery-time rating information online. We will explore the roles of pricing and delivery-time ratings disclosure policies in the manifestation of the trade-off between promised delivery times and delivery-time conformance. A shorter promised delivery time can entice more consumers to buy, but can also result in a lower delivery-time conformance and discourage consumers from buying. It is thus necessary to trade off the delivery-time promise and conformance. We learn from Cosgrove [11] and Hodgson [21] that, in practice, some firms prioritize a high delivery-time conformance over a short promised delivery time whereas others grant a higher priority to short promised times. As consumer demand decreases with retail price, a lower price could mitigate the negative effects of a longer delivery time promised by those online firms who treat delivery time conformance with a higher priority. Similarly, a lower price may allow those online firms prioritizing a shorter delivery time to accept a smaller delivery-time conformance. In addition, the delivery-time ratings affect consumer expectations of delivery-time conformance, thus influencing consumers’ purchase intentions. [41]) perform a consumer-choice utility analysis. A natural question is whether analyses with these two different approaches will generate similar implications or not. We will first consider a single-firm setting in which the firm is responsible for retail pricing and shipping, similar to, e.g., Ho and Zheng [20] who used queuing theory to investigate the promised delivery time decision. rows: We will investigate whether or not online retailing firms should disclose on their websites the delivery-time ratings provided by their customers. In a survey of 18,430 online shoppers across more than 50 countries [22], 43% of those shoppers reported that delivery service is the most important attribute of online offerings (second only to price at 57%). The survey also revealed that delivery time is by far the most influential aspect of delivery service. Another survey focusing on different aspects of delivery service [4] exposed that 74% of U.S. consumers are willing to pay more for fast delivery, and 75% care about on-time delivery (a.k.a. delivery-time conformance). Prior to receiving products, consumers are not sure if the deliveries can be completed within the times promised by online retailing firms. To predict the likelihood of delivery-time conformance, consumers usually refer to the delivery-time ratings posted online (if allowed by online retailing firms). When such ratings are available, the actual delivery time has a significant impact on customer satisfaction [19] as well as delivery ratings and sales [12]. As the disclosure of delivery ratings has its pros and cons, it behooves us to explore under what conditions online retailing firms benefit from posting the delivery-time rating information online.

We will explore the roles of pricing and delivery-time ratings disclosure policies in the manifestation of the trade-off between promised delivery times and delivery-time conformance. A shorter promised delivery time can entice more consumers to buy, but can also result in a lower delivery-time conformance and discourage consumers from buying. It is thus necessary to trade off the delivery-time promise and conformance. We learn from Cosgrove [11] and Hodgson [21] that, in practice, some firms prioritize a high delivery-time conformance over a short promised delivery time whereas others grant a higher priority to short promised times. As consumer demand decreases with retail price, a lower price could mitigate the negative effects of a longer delivery time promised by those online firms who treat delivery time conformance with a higher priority. Similarly, a lower price may allow those online firms prioritizing a shorter delivery time to accept a smaller delivery-time conformance. In addition, the delivery-time ratings affect consumer expectations of delivery-time conformance, thus influencing consumers’ purchase intentions. 13500822.label: Realisation of objectives
13500822.value: For objective 1, we have investigated the conditions under which online retailing firms should disclose on their websites the delivery-time ratings provided by their customers. We have delivered two major outputs for this project, which includes one publication at Manufacturing & Service Operations Management (M&SOM) and the other under the second-round review at Production and Operations Management (POM). In the M&SOM paper, our findings imply that it is optimal for an online merchant to spend either full effort or no effort to improve the precision of consumer perceptions of delivery reliability. That is, the firm should not consider a partial effort. Whether it is optimal to make the full effort or no effort depends on many factors but mainly on the cost of information quality and the dispersion of consumer valuations. The higher these two main factors are, the less likely the firm should make a full effort. This suggests that the estimation of cost and consumer characteristics should receive especial attention from managers. In our POM paper, we have found that, for both the drop-shipping and the retailer fulfillment models, the supplier's and the retailer's incentives to disclose the ratings information depend on the system-wide value (i.e., the sum of consumers' total utility increase and the supply chain's unit shipping-cost reduction). Because making delivery-time ratings available can shorten the optimal delivery times, this strategy may not be profitable for online marketplaces that lack affordable access to a high delivery-speed infrastructure (e.g., marketplaces that operate in remote geographic areas and that lack capital to develop the capability in-house). Likewise, making delivery-time ratings available may not be profitable when short delivery times are cost-prohibitive and pricing restrictions are enforced (i.e., prices are exogenous or capped). These two possible scenarios could explain why some online retailers make delivery-time ratings available while others do not. For objective 2, we have explored the roles of pricing and delivery-time ratings disclosure policies in the manifestation of the trade-off between promised delivery times and delivery-time conformance. In our M&SOM paper, we concluded that the firm cannot simultaneously increase both delivery reliability and consumer demand by changing the information quality level. This interesting result indicates that the consumer who is more likely to trust the delivery-time information is not more likely to buy, because the consumer's purchase also depends on other factors such as price, promised delivery time, etc. Hence, the results suggest that online merchants may need to determine whether profits or market share are more important before deciding on their delivery-time information efforts. In our POM paper, we find that optimal promised delivery times are decreasing in the consumer sensitivity to delivery time, no matter whether prices are endogenous or exogenous and no matter whether delivery-time ratings are available or not. Optimal promised delivery times are increasing in the consumer sensitivity to delivery-time conformance, unless pricing is endogenous and delivery-time ratings are available. If these two conditions hold, optimal promised delivery times are decreasing in the consumer sensitivity to delivery conformance, and there is no trade-off between delivery times and delivery-time conformance. For objective 3, we have examined whether different consumer utility specifications result in similar or different managerial implications. We considered different consumer utility functions in our M&SOM paper and our POM paper. In our M&SOM paper, our proposed model abstracts the different degrees of information quality observed in practice by regarding the error in delivery reliability information as a continuous random variable. The distribution of this random variable depends on a continuous measure of the firm's information quality effort. To incorporate this additional source of uncertainty into the standard random utility model, we capitalize on the special properties of the C distribution. This methodological innovation allows us to solve the model analytically and characterize the optimal decisions as well as the optimal reliability and profit. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to incorporate the C distribution into analytic models in the operations management field. In our POM paper, we relied on the data from the T-mall supply chain to model and analyze consumer utility and to derive expected demand functions for both the case of the availability of delivery-time ratings and the case of the unavailability of ratings. We allowed the promised delivery time to affect consumer utility directly through its effect on expected waiting times and also indirectly through the effect of delivery-time ratings on expected delivery-time conformance. For objective 4, we have analyzed the single-firm (non-supply chain) in our M&SOM paper and supply-chain channel structures in our POM paper to identify differences and similarities between the two structures and to assess the consequences of platformization. We have obtained some similar results and also found some differences. For objective 5, we have discussed the impacts of competition on optimal pricing, delivery-time, and rating information disclosure decisions. That is, we have investigated the duopoly competition between two online retailers who compete with their prices and promised delivery times. In our POM paper, we found that when a supplier sells through both a retailer that offers the delivery-time ratings and a retailer that does not, the optimal promised delivery time decreases both with the consumer sensitivity to delivery time and with the consumer sensitivity to delivery conformance. When incorporating an additional channel without delivery-time ratings alongside the existing channel with available ratings, we can mitigate the trade-off between promised delivery time and delivery-time conformance through coordinating the prices and promised delivery times.

13500822.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500822.value: In the M&SOM paper, we have obtained a number of managerial insights that can be helpful to managers of digital businesses. The five main insights are summarized as follows. First, our results imply that it is optimal for an online merchant to spend either full effort or no effort to improve the precision of consumer perceptions of delivery reliability. Second, the factors that influence the firm's profit the most are consumer sensitivity to delivery trust and the correlation between consumer inferences of delivery reliability and actual delivery reliability. Third, the firm cannot simultaneously increase both delivery reliability and consumer demand by changing the information quality level. Fourth, a higher service rate could help simultaneously raise delivery reliability, consumer demand, as well as the firm's profit. Fifth, high heterogeneity in consumer valuations of the firm's offerings harms profits. This suggest that, ceteris paribus, online merchants should favor markets in which consumer valuations of their products are as uniform as possible. In the POM paper, we summarize the main implications of our analyses as follows. First, optimal promised delivery times are decreasing in the consumer sensitivity to delivery time, no matter whether prices are endogenous or exogenous and no matter whether delivery-time ratings are available or not. Second, optimal promised delivery times are increasing in the consumer sensitivity to delivery-time conformance, unless pricing is endogenous and delivery-time ratings are available. Third, regardless of whether the supply chain uses the drop-shipping model or the retailer-fulfillment model, the optimal promised shipping time when the ratings information is disclosed is always shorter than that in the case of no disclosure. Fourth, for both the drop-shipping and the retailer fulfillment models, the supplier's and the retailer's incentives to disclose the ratings information depend on the system-wide value (i.e., the sum of consumers' total utility increase and the supply chain's unit shipping-cost reduction). Fifth, because making delivery-time ratings available can shorten the optimal delivery times, this strategy may not be profitable for online marketplaces that lack affordable access to a high delivery-speed infrastructure (e.g., marketplaces that operate in remote geographic areas and that lack capital to develop the capability in-house). In addition, we have published another paper in Naval Research Logistics. In this paper, we considered a multinational firm that needs to determine a local content rate for its products made and sold in a foreign country. We investigated the impact of a government's local content requirement (LCR) on the local content rate and pricing decisions of a multinational firm who competes with a local firm in a market.

13500822.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13500822.value: In this research project, we considered delivery-time information disclosure and pricing decisions for a single-firm case and a supply-chain case. We focused on the disclosure of the delivery-time information only. As in practice, online firms may also release the information of quality to consumers. This behooves us to investigate the quality and delivery-time information disclosure in future, for which it is important to find optimal quality and delivery-effort decisions. Moreover, it would be interesting to examine the optimal decision on shipping options in addition to the delivery-effort and pricing decisions.

13500822.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500822.value: The proliferation of online offerings increases search costs for consumers and leads them to rely on ratings from other customers to infer the attributes of offerings, such as quality, delivery time, and after-sale service. We investigated how the characteristics of consumers and a service firm influence the firm's optimal pricing and promised delivery-time decisions as well as the optimal investment in the quality of delivery reliability information available to consumers. We found that the optimal strategy is to disclose either error-free delivery reliability information or no information at all. We also delineated conditions for each of the two strategies to dominate. Moreover, the disclosure of ratings can reduce delivery times but is profitable only if the rating availability can increase system-wide value. These results hold for both drop-shipping and retailer-managed fulfillment models and also suggest when and how the supply chains of online marketplaces can use pricing to make the offering of shorter delivery times a dominant strategy.

13500922.label: Major findings and research outcome
13500922.value: This study examines how wealth disclosure influences the tax strategies of businesses controlled by wealthy owners in China. We find that public disclosure of entrepreneurs’ wealth deters aggressive tax strategies due to heightened social and political scrutiny. Enhanced tax-centric media coverage and enforcement following disclosure are key pathways driving this effect. The impact is more pronounced in regions with substantial wealth gaps and lower average income, and firms with lower pre-disclosure tax payments respond more intensely. This research broadens corporate behavior analysis by examining how nontax social and political factors influence firms’ tax decisions. It enriches discussions on social and governance issues, highlighting tax as a key element of corporate sustainability and social responsibility. The results had been presented to the Canadian Academic Accounting Association Annual Conference 2024, the feedback from which had been incorporated into the paper.

13500922.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13500922.value: The original study, though focused on China, has global relevance. The universal question of whether the wealthy pay their fair share of taxes suggests its findings on "wealth disclosure" could apply elsewhere. Future research could test this in different countries, such as European nations debating transparency laws or by analyzing the global impact of leaks like the "Panama Papers." Comparing these contexts would reveal if social and political pressures drive tax compliance everywhere, validating the original findings and advancing our understanding of transparency as a tool for corporate responsibility and equity.

13500922.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13500922.value: When wealthy business owners in China are required to publicly disclose their fortunes, their companies become less likely to aggressively avoid taxes. This happens because the public disclosure subjects them to greater social and political scrutiny, making them more concerned about their reputation and attracting increased media attention and stricter enforcement from tax authorities. The effect is strongest in regions with large wealth gaps and lower incomes, and for firms that were previously paying the least in taxes. Ultimately, this research shows that beyond just financial rules, social pressure and public opinion are powerful forces that can shape corporate behavior and encourage businesses to act more responsibly.

13501122.label: Project Objectives
13501122.value: This research project aims to explore the role of boards of directors in shaping firms’ disclosure of climate risks. Climate change increasingly imposes non-negligible risks on business operations. As risk oversight is the primary responsibility of boards, a growing number of firms emphasize the environmental experiences of directors in their proxy statements. Hence, this project can provide a timely evaluation of whether appointing directors with relevant experiences is effective in addressing a firm’s climate risks and improving corporate disclosure of these risks. More specifically, this research will examine whether and how directors’ climatic disaster experiences affect corporate climate risk disclosure. As the climatic disaster experience may alter a director’s ability and/or incentive to supply climate risk information, the effect of director climatic disaster experience on climate risk disclosure is not clear-cut and worth exploring. Prior studies have typically investigated how past experiences of financial events (e.g., acquisitions or bankruptcies) influence directors in carrying out their advisory roles (e.g., Field and Mkrtchyan, 2017; Gopalan, Gormley, and Kalda, 2021). The tests in this research will show whether directors learn from their firsthand experiences of climatic disasters and improve corporate climate risk disclosure. By focusing on directors’ climatic disaster experiences, this research will fill the void and shed light on the importance of nonfinancial experiences that may enhance a director’s ability to produce and supply information for nonfinancial disclosure. This research will inspect a potential drawback of the emerging governance practice appointing directors with adverse environmental experiences, which might intensify the directors’ career concerns and weaken their incentive to facilitate climate risk disclosure that harms firm performance. As such, this research will provide evidence on whether directors’ incentives play a role in firms’ climate risk reporting, adding to the literature arguing that directors’ incentives (e.g., arising from electoral or reputational concerns) affect board effectiveness and corporate decisions (Fahlenbrach, Low, and Stulz, 2017; Jiang, Wan, and Zhao 2016; Masulis and Mobbs 2014). In this research, I will further consider firm-specific costs and benefits of climate risk disclosure and investigate the heterogeneity in the effect of directors’ climatic disaster experiences. The possible benefits of disclosing climate risks include meeting the information demand of large investors (Flammer, Toffel, and Viswanathan, 2021; Ilhan, Krueger, Sautner, and Starks, 2021) and avoiding litigation due to non-disclosure of material climate risks (Wasim, 2019). The possible costs of climate risk disclosure include developing new structures or processes to collect and compile the information (Christensen, Hail, and Leuz, 2019) and potentially revealing proprietary information to competitors (Verrecchia, 1983; Griffin and Jaffe, 2016), among others. Hence, the effect of directors’ climatic disaster experiences on firms’ voluntary disclosure of climate risks should vary across firms, depending on each firm’s disclosure cost and/or benefit. In addition to the costs and benefits of climate risk disclosure inherent in firm characteristics, I will also examine how directors’ perceived costs and benefits of reporting climate risks influence the baseline effect. Directors having experienced climatic disasters may have also observed the consequences of climate risk disclosure at disaster firms and thereby have developed their own estimates of the costs and benefits of such disclosures. Thus, I conjecture that the effect of directors’ climatic disaster experiences on the voluntary disclosure of climate risks varies with the directors’ perceived costs and/or benefits of climate risk disclosure.

13501322.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13501322.value: The expression of feigned emotions to conform with organizational display norms is very common in marketing and effective in engaging and influencing customers. Unlike genuine expressions, acted expressions are produced and perceived asymmetrically. While asymmetric expressions provide significant clues about the spontaneity, valence, and intensity of emotions, previous studies have generally treated them as being negative and lacking trustworthiness in social interactions. Moreover, despite the dynamic nature of facial expressions, extant studies of facial asymmetry have mainly used static images in experimental settings, an approach that lacks external validity and accuracy in reflecting observer perceptions. We propose that the asymmetry effect is more complicated and contingent upon the timing of display and emotional labor strategies. Facial asymmetry has unforeseen benefits in video marketing, which is less subject to the influence of social pressure than face-to-face interactions. To bridge the gap between facial asymmetry research and emotional labor theory in a video marketing context, we posit that: 1) the negative effect of asymmetry is reversed when the displayer performs deep acting (vs. surface acting) due to enhanced perceptions of acting competence; and 2) onset facial asymmetry (especially in negative expressions) is weighted more heavily in consumer judgments and subsequent actions. We propose a machine learning approach to face-detection and facial-expression-recognition using a convolutional neural network (CNN) to measure targets’ dynamic facial expressions and facial asymmetry. To test the main effect of facial asymmetry as well as the effect of timing and emotional labor, we will empirically analyze 9,000+ videos from Kickstarter and 30+ live commerce videos from an apparel retailer. Finally, to test the causal impact of facial asymmetry on consumer perceptions, we will manipulate facial asymmetry in controlled experiments using dynamic video stimuli. The proposed project will make three main contributions. First, it will add to emotion research by demonstrating the complex effect of facial asymmetry on consumer perceptions. It will be the first work to link facial asymmetry, emotional labor, and video marketing, concepts that previous research has examined separately, despite their close relation to emotional expression (its appearance, production method, and natural setting). Second, we will contribute to video analysis by proposing a novel approach to measuring visual features at scale, thus opening new avenues for future research. Third, the findings will inform research on the social psychology of emotions and enable practitioners to leverage the effect of dynamic facial expressions to improve video marketing effectiveness. 公司要求员工情绪的表达符合行业规范在业界非常普遍，目的是为了更有效地吸引和影响客户。与自然真实表达的表情不同，刻意的表情会造成脸部表情的不对称并且被消费者感知。脸部表情的对称与不对称的表征是判断情绪是否自发、正面还是负面，以及强度的重要线索。已有的研究通常将脸部表情的不对称视为消极和缺乏可信度的。尽管面部表情具有动态特性，但现有研究在实验环境中主要使用静态图像进行测试，因此在测量观察者感知方面缺乏外部有效性和准确性。我们认为脸部表情的不对称效应取决于表情展示的时机和情绪劳动策略。与面对面的互动相比，面部不对称在视频营销中可能具有正面效应，源于视频营销的受社会压力的影响更小。 在未来的研究中，我们假设：1）当展示者进行深度表演（相对于表面表演）时，表情不对称的负面影响被逆转，由于消费者对其表演能力的肯定; 2）初见阶段的面部不对称（尤其是在负面表情中）对消费者判断和后续行动中的权重更大。我们提出了一种使用卷积神经网络 (CNN) 进行面部检测和面部表情识别的机器学习方法来测量目标的动态面部表情和面部不对称性。我们将对来自 Kickstarter 的 9,000 多个视频和来自服装零售商的 30 多个直播带货视频进行实证分析。我们还将使用动态视频操纵面部表情不对称，以测试其对消费者感知的影响。 该项目有三个主要贡献。首先，它通过研究面部表情的不对称表征对消费者认知的影响，来丰富情感研究的文献。面部表情的不对称，情绪劳动策略，和视频营销这三个概念已经被分别研究过，尽管它们与情绪表达的外观、产生方法，和产生背景密切相关，但被联系起来研究还是第一次。其次，我们提出适用于大数据测量视觉特征的新方法，为视频分析的方法开辟新的途径。第三，研究结果将为情绪的社会心理学研究提供信息，并使从业者能够利用动态面部表情的效果来提高视频营销的有效性。

13501322.label: Realisation of objectives
13501322.value: The proposed research aims to complete the following five objectives: 1. Bridge the gap between facial asymmetry research and emotional labor theory and adopt a multi-method approach to assess the asymmetrical effect on communication outcomes in video marketing - We successfully integrated these two theories in the proposed research to understand Duchenne and non-Duchenne facial expressions in video marketing. This involved an extensive review of literature in both fields and the development of a comprehensive framework that delineates the relationship between facial asymmetry and emotional labor in the context of video marketing. We finally develop a temporal-spatial framework to analyze both the morphological and dynamic features of facial expressions (take smiling as an example). 2. Propose a novel machine learning approach to measuring the dynamic facial expressions and asymmetries displayed in videos - A significant achievement of our project was the development and implementation of a novel machine-learning algorithm designed to measure dynamic facial expressions and asymmetries in video content accurately. This tool has demonstrated remarkable precision in detecting subtle facial movements and has potential applications beyond our initial research scope. 3. Provide empirical evidence for the facial asymmetry effect on communication outcomes across different platforms, as well as the time dynamics of facial asymmetry and the effect of emotional labor strategies - We have provided substantial empirical evidence of how facial asymmetry influences communication outcomes on the Udemy.com (an online learning platform). Our findings offer intriguing insights into the role of facial expressions in video marketing, particularly regarding viewer perceptions of spontaneity, trustworthiness, and competence. 4. Test the causal impact of facial asymmetry on consumer perception of spontaneity, trustworthiness, competence, and other traits - Through controlled experiments, we have tested and confirmed the causal impact of facial asymmetry on consumer perceptions. These experiments have significantly contributed to our understanding of the psychological mechanisms underlying viewer responses to video marketing content. 5. Highlight the implications of facial asymmetry for the social psychology of emotions, video analysis, and video marketing strategies - Our research highlights several practical implications for marketers, video content creators, and social psychologists. We have outlined strategies that leverage the nuances of facial expression (morphological features such as facial asymmetry and temporal features such as duration and timing) to enhance communication effectiveness in video marketing. Addressing the Partial Completion of Objective 3: While we have made significant strides in most of the research objectives, it's important to note that our analysis across different platforms is not yet complete. Our initial plan was to conduct comparative analyses across Kickstarter and Weimob platforms. However, due to unforeseen challenges, including data access issues and the need for a more nuanced approach to analyzing video content, we have only completed our analysis on the Udemy platform to date. Additionally, we have collected a substantial dataset from another platform, italki, which offers a unique opportunity to explore facial asymmetry effects in a new context. This dataset is poised for analysis, and we anticipate that it will provide valuable insights that complement and enhance our findings from Udemy. Our immediate plan is to leverage the data collected from italki to replicate and extend our analysis. This will not only fulfill our original objective of comparing facial asymmetry effects across platforms but will also enrich our understanding of the dynamics of emotional labor strategies in video marketing. We now prioritize the analysis of the italki dataset, employing the same machine learning tools and analytical frameworks developed for the Udemy platform. This will ensure the robustness of our analysis on a whole.

13501322.label: Major findings and research outcome
13501322.value: Existing research on smiles often relies on pre-selected or digitally manipulated portrayals in laboratory settings. While these examples are easily recognizable, they may not accurately capture the nuances of real-life smiles. Previous studies, despite their rich findings, have been limited in capturing both the morphological and dynamic features of smiles at granular levels, leading to fragmented insights and inconsistent conclusions. To address these gaps, our research proposes a spatiotemporal framework for analyzing smiles in marketing videos, emphasizing both the spatial and temporal characteristics of smiles displayed by video presenters. This approach examines the asymmetry, duration, and timing of smiles, along with their interactions, to decode their impact on consumer reactions. Our analytics pipeline encompasses face detection, emotion extraction, and the construction of relevant metrics. In a practical application of our framework, we conducted an empirical study analyzing a substantial dataset of promotional videos for online courses hosted on Udemy. Our empirical analysis of 12,298 Udemy videos reveals that asymmetric and prolonged smiles may deter student enrollments, an effect moderated by the smile's timing. The findings consistently indicate that an excessively large smile itself does not affect student enrollments, whereas prolonged smiles positively impact them. However, these positive effects are reversed by factors such as facial asymmetry and the timing of the smile's display, especially when the smiles occur in the middle or at the end of the videos, compared to their appearance at the beginning. Highlighting the intricate influence of smiles, our study advocates comprehensive and sensitive measures to detect subtle changes in facial expressions. It showcases the viability of automated methods in extracting dynamic properties of facial expressions, marking a significant advancement in smile analytics and video marketing research. The manuscript has been completed and was presented at the INFORMS Marketing Science Conference in Sydney in June 2024. It received considerable feedback from the academic audience. We are currently fine-tuning the model and plan to submit it to the Journal of Marketing by the summer of 2025.

13501322.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13501322.value: The current study highlights several limitations that pave the way for future research. Firstly, while we found a link between the characteristics of smiles in Udemy videos and sales success, this does not confirm a cause-and-effect relationship. Our methods also did not gauge average consumer perceptions accurately. To address these issues, future research could explore the causal mechanisms in a lab setting, such as how the perceived authenticity of a smile affects its persuasiveness. Secondly, gender differences in the use and impact of smiles in communication are evident, with women smiling more frequently and potentially facing penalties for not smiling, whereas men's smiles are seen as more significant due to their infrequency. Future studies should investigate how gender influences the effectiveness of smiles in marketing communications. Lastly, our research focused on one-to-many communications without direct interaction, as seen in video-based persuasion. Future work could examine face-to-face interactions in settings like live-stream e-commerce, where viewers can interact with presenters in real-time. This could offer insights into how two-way communication influences the persuasive power of smiles.

13501322.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
13501322.value: Our project dives into understanding smiles better than ever before. In the past, when researchers wanted to study smiles, they mostly showed people pictures of different smiles and asked what they thought about them. This approach helped figure out how certain types of smiles make us feel or react. But, it had its drawbacks. For one, it couldn't capture all the tiny details and variations of smiles that we see in real life, and it was hard to mix and match different smile features in these studies. Now, thanks to new tech in computer vision and analysis, we can study smiles more closely and accurately. We can pick up on the tiny changes in a smile that happen in real life but were too subtle for older methods to catch. This means we can understand not just any smile, but the full range of smiles people make in day-to-day life and what these smiles mean. Our research is a big step forward in figuring out how smiles work and their impact. It's especially exciting for areas like marketing, where understanding the nuances of a smile can make a big difference in how we communicate and connect with each other.
