To use pressure to tune these superconductors and to use the pressure evolution of the self-field critical current density to detect a quantum phase transition hidden beneath the superconducting dome

To extract the superfluid density from the self-field critical current density in the limiting case that the sample is thinner than the penetration depth; to use the temperature dependence of the superfluid density to infer the superconducting gap symmetry and to probe the pressure evolution of the superconducting gap, thereby helping us understand the nature of the superconducting phase.

14300722.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300722.value: Making superconductors that can work at practical temperatures is the holy grail of modern condensed matter research. Their optimization requires a deep understanding of their fundamental physics. This proposal seeks to contribute to this endeavour via a detailed investigation of the superfluid density through the usage of pressure as a controlled tuning parameter. The superfluid density is a quantity that is of central importance for a superconductor, determining for example the strength of the superconducting state. While this quantity can be determined accurately for most superconductors, its measurement is not straightforward for materials that superconduct under pressure. This is because the devices used for generating high pressure are incompatible with most traditional techniques that probe the superfluid density. This proposal aims to tackle the challenge of measuring the superfluid density under pressure through a novel route. The superfluid density has recently been theoretically shown to be related to the self-field critical current density, i.e. critical current density in the absence of an external magnetic field. When the thickness of the superconducting sample is much smaller than the London penetration depth, the self-field critical current density is directly proportional to the superfluid density. Therefore, this proposal seeks to develop a unique methodology to measure the self-field critical current of thin flakes with a diamond anvil cell in a dilution refrigerator. Superconductors that feature interesting temperature-pressure phase diagrams will be studied, allowing us to determine the pressure-evolution of the superconducting gap and to assess if there is a quantum phase transition hidden beneath the superconducting dome. The CUHK group has the existing capability to conduct electrical transport measurements on thin flakes of quantum materials under pressure. The Wellington group is responsible for the theoretical model that unravels the relationship between the superfluid density and the self-field critical current density. Considering the research background of both groups, the joint CUHK-Wellington team is highly qualified for executing this project.

14300822.value: 生物啟發的納米馬達作為高效多功能治療劑的研究進展

14300822.label: Project Objectives
14300822.value: To construct and characterize newly developed MnO2-FA NSs for cancer theranostics. To integrate copper (Cu) nanoparticles onto MnO2-FA NSs to increase the effect of chemodynamic therapy. rows: To construct and characterize newly developed MnO2-FA NSs for cancer theranostics.
To integrate copper (Cu) nanoparticles onto MnO2-FA NSs to increase the effect of chemodynamic therapy.

14300822.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300822.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT), ultrasound-assisted sonodynamic therapy (SDT) and chemodynamic therapy (CDT) have emerged as effective strategies for cancer treatment. However, the effectiveness of PDT and SDT is limited by tumor hypoxia while the anticancer efficacy of CDT is limited by low penetration capability of passive CDT agents. In this proposed project, we will fabricate MnO2-based nanomotors with a variety of cancer-targeting curing agents to improve their treatment efficacy. We will design a new class of magnetic resonance (MR) active, folic acid fabricated MnO2 nanosheets (MnO2-FA NSs) with low toxicity and optimal biocompatibility using a facile method. MnO2-FA NSs can target cancer cells via folate receptor-mediated endocytosis. To a certain extent, MnO2-FA NSs alleviate hypoxia and deplete GSH in response to the tumor microenvironment (TME), specifically inducing cancer cell death and causing minimal damage to healthy cells. Furthermore, MnO2-FA NSs are smart nanocarriers for the precise delivery and release of anticancer drugs to tumor sites. Additionally, taking advantage of the significantly high Fenton-like catalytic activity and the capability of glutathione depletion of copper nanoparticles, we will fabricate MnO2-FA NSs with copper nanoparticles as a highly promising cancer theranostic nanoplatform for further medical applications. Lastly, we will incorporate novel self-destroying and self-propelling nanomotors onto targeting nanosheets of Cu@MnO2-FA to significantly increase the tumor penetration for effective killing of cancer cells. All the above newly developed nanoagents will be systematically studied in-vitro and in-vivo. This will open a new avenue for the development of biocompatible and biodegradable multimodal nanoagents for disease sensing, imaging, and, drug delivery and release. 光動力療法(PDT)、超聲輔助聲動力療法(SDT)和化學動力療法(CDT)已成為治療癌症的有效方法。然而，PDT和SDT的有效性受腫瘤缺氧環境的限制，CDT的抗癌效果受CDT藥物被動運輸穿透能力低的限制。在本課題中，我們將合成基於MnO2的帶有多種腫瘤靶向治療藥物的納米馬達，以提高其治療功效。首先，我們將設計一種新型的具有核磁共振活性的、葉酸修飾的MnO2納米片(MnO2-FA NSs)，這種納米材料具有低毒性、理想的生物相容性且易於合成。MnO2-FA NSs可通過葉酸受體介導的胞吞作用靶向癌細胞，且能在一定程度上響應腫瘤微環境，減輕缺氧、消耗穀胱甘肽、特異性誘導癌細胞死亡，並對健康細胞的損傷最小。此外，MnO2-FA NSs是一種智能的納米載體，可以將抗癌藥物精確地傳遞和釋放到腫瘤部位。並且，利用銅納米顆粒顯著的類芬頓催化活性和穀胱甘肽消耗能力，我們可以制備帶有銅納米顆粒的MnO2-FA NSs作為一種極具前景的癌症治療納米平台，用于進一步的醫療應用。最後，我們將在靶向納米薄片Cu@MnO2-FA上加入新型自毀自推進的納米馬達，以顯著提高腫瘤穿透能力，有效殺傷癌細胞。上述所有新開發的納米製劑都將在體外和體內進行系統地研究。這將為開發用於疾病感測、成像和藥物輸送與釋放的生物兼容和可生物降解的多模式納米制劑開辟一條新的途徑。

14300822.label: Realisation of objectives
14300822.value: The project objectives were successfully realized through innovative nanomaterial designs, comprehensive characterizations, and rigorous in vitro and in vivo evaluations. Each objective was achieved, resulting in manuscript preparations and a peer-reviewed publication, demonstrating significant advancements in cancer theranostics. Objective 1: To construct and characterize newly developed MnO₂-FA NSs for cancer theranostics. This objective was fully achieved by developing a novel heterostructured TiO₂@Pt-MnO₂ nanoplatform in a 1:1 ratio, which incorporates MnO₂ nanosheets (NSs) functionalized for targeted cancer therapy and diagnostics. The platform was constructed via advanced synthesis methods and thoroughly characterized for structural integrity, catalytic activity, oxygen generation, and glutathione (GSH) depletion capabilities. It addresses key challenges in sonodynamic therapy (SDT) by enhancing reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, alleviating tumor hypoxia, and remodeling the suppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). In vitro studies confirmed superior ROS generation, TME modulation, and apoptotic cell death induction, while in vivo evaluations demonstrated remarkable tumor suppression and durable therapeutic outcomes. A manuscript detailing these findings is ready for submission. (Attached in Part C) Objective 2: To integrate copper (Cu) nanoparticles onto MnO₂-FA NSs to increase the effect of chemodynamic therapy. Inspired by the work published in Smart Materials in Medicine 4 (2023) 286–293 (attached in part C), indicating the strong evidence of therapeutic efficacy of Cu(+) ions via Fenton like reaction, this objective was accomplished by integrating CuO₂ nanoparticles onto a mesoporous TiO₂-based structure (analogous to MnO₂-FA NSs), creating a TiO₂@CuO₂ nanoplatform that synergistically boosts chemodynamic therapy (CDT) efficacy. The Cu integration modulated the energy bandgap for amplified ROS production under SDT, catalyzed a self-sustaining H₂O₂ cascade, depleted GSH, and generated O₂ to mitigate hypoxia. The nanoplatform was characterized for structural stability and multifunctional performance, with in vitro assessments showing enhanced ROS generation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cytotoxicity against cancer cells. In vivo studies validated potent anti-tumor effects, reduced resistance, and improved survival. Although initially framed around MnO₂-FA NSs, the Cu integration was adapted to this heterostructure for optimal CDT enhancement, with a manuscript ready for submission. (Attached in Part C) Objective 3: To analyze nitric oxide-driven nanomotor with higher tissue penetration for inflammation/cancer treatment. This objective was exceeded through the development and analysis of a multifunctional hybrid membrane-coated nanomotor (RM-GDL-MF), comprising mesoporous silica-coated iron oxide nanoparticles loaded with doxorubicin (DOX), L-arginine (L-arg), and glucose oxidase (GOx), camouflaged with red blood cell and cancer cell membranes. The nanomotor utilizes a cascade reaction where GOx produces H₂O₂, oxidizing L-arg to release nitric oxide (NO) for self-propelled motion, enhancing tissue penetration and extracellular matrix (ECM) traversal. It was analyzed for tumor targeting, immune evasion, ROS-induced immunogenic cell death (ICD), dendritic cell maturation, macrophage reprogramming, and overall anti-tumor efficacy. In vitro and in vivo experiments confirmed significant tumor accumulation, penetration, and therapeutic outcomes. This work has been published in ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces (2025, 17, 51643–51658), underscoring its impact on inflammation and cancer treatment. (Attached in Part C)

14300822.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300822.value: This project delivered three innovative nanoplatforms that overcome key barriers in cancer therapy—hypoxia, GSH resistance, poor penetration, and immune suppression—via ROS amplification, TME remodeling, and multimodal synergy. 1. TiO₂@Pt-MnO₂ Nanoplatform (Objective 1). A heterostructured system combining TiO₂ (sonosensitizer) with Pt-MnO₂ in a 1:1 ratio dramatically enhances sonodynamic therapy (SDT) and chemodynamic therapy (CDT). Under ultrasound, it generates abundant ROS while MnO₂ decomposes H₂O₂ to produce O₂ (relieving hypoxia) and depletes GSH to block antioxidant defense. This dual modulation amplifies oxidative stress and induces robust apoptosis. In vitro: superior ROS yield, mitochondrial damage, and cell death. In vivo: significant tumor suppression was demonstrated. Manuscript ready for submission. 2. TiO₂@CuO₂ Nanoplatform (Objective 2). A mesoporous TiO₂ core with CuO₂ shell forms a bandgap-tuned heterostructure for synergistic sono-chemodynamic therapy. CuO₂ narrows TiO₂’s energy gap for enhanced SDT efficiency, self-supplies H₂O₂ via cascade catalysis, depletes GSH, and generates O₂ to reverse hypoxia. This creates a self-reinforcing ROS storm. In vitro: exceptional ROS production, hypoxia relief, and cytotoxicity under ultrasound. In vivo: potent tumor ablation, reduced resistance, and improved survival. Manuscript ready for submission. 3. RM-GDL-MF Hybrid Nanomotor (Objective 3). A self-propelled, biomimetic nanomotor built on mesoporous silica-coated iron oxide (MF), loaded with DOX, L-arginine, and glucose oxidase (GOx), and cloaked in red blood cell and cancer cell hybrid membranes. It uses tumor glucose to trigger a GOx, then H₂O₂ and NO cascade, generating NO bubbles for autonomous propulsion. This enables deep ECM penetration and high tumor accumulation. The hybrid coating ensures immune evasion and tumor targeting. ROS from the cascade induces immunogenic cell death (ICD), recruiting CD8⁺ TILs, maturing dendritic cells, and shifting macrophages to M1 phenotype—transforming immunosuppressive tumors into immunologically active ones. In vitro/in vivo: excellent targeting, penetration, and synergistic chemo-immunotherapy. Published in Applied Materials & Interfaces 2025, 17, 51643–51658. Overall Impact. These platforms integrate TME reprogramming, enhanced ROS therapy, self-propulsion, and immune activation into single, intelligent systems. They achieve deep tumor delivery, overcome resistance, and enable durable responses with minimal invasiveness—setting new alternatives for precision, multimodal cancer nanomedicine.

14300822.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300822.value: The three nanoplatforms offer strong clinical potential through deep penetration, TME reprogramming, and multimodal synergy. TiO₂@Pt-MnO₂ & TiO₂@CuO₂: Enhance with targeting ligands for specific cancers and integrate real-time ultrasound imaging for precision therapy. Combine with immunotherapy to amplify anti-tumor immunity. RM-GDL-MF Nanomotor: Use patient-derived membranes for personalized targeting and co-load immune checkpoint inhibitors. Proposed Course of Action: Apply for future financial support to, 1 Conduct large scale-animal (canine/primate) safety and efficacy studies. 2 Optimize the synthesis protocol and biodistribution for regulatory approval. 3 Initiate Phase I clinical trials in accessible tumors (e.g., skin, head & neck). These steps will fast-track safe, personalized, and powerful next-generation cancer therapies.

14300822.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300822.value: This project created three smart nanoparticle systems to fight cancer more effectively by fixing the tumor’s defenses. Two Ultrasound-Activated Killers nanoparticles (TiO₂@Pt-MnO₂ and TiO₂@CuO₂) use safe ultrasound waves to trigger cancer-killing oxygen bursts. They fix the tumor’s low-oxygen problem, drain its antioxidant shield (GSH), and load it with toxic molecules—killing cancer cells from within. Lab and mouse tests showed strong tumor shrinkage. Self-Driving “Cancer-Seeking” Nanomotor. A nanorobot wrapped in real cell membranes coats sneaks past the immune system and homes in on tumors. It uses tumor glucose to power its movement deeper into the cancer mass. Inside, it releases a chemotherapy drug and triggers immune cells to attack the tumor, turning a cold tumor “hot” for better immune response. Tests in mice showed strong tumor control and killing effect. Significance & Value. These systems reach deep tumors, break their resistance, and combine multiple treatments (ultrasound, chemo-, immuno-) in one dose. With less side effects and harm to healthy tissue, they offer safer, stronger, and smarter cancer treatments. One study is published in a top journal; two are ready for submission.
