17500522.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500522.value: COVID-19疫情与数字平台上的品牌绩效：信号理论视角

17500522.label: Project Objectives
17500522.value: To understand how the COVID-19 pandemic influences the effect of name versus non-name brands in product performance on digital platforms. Reasons Whereas the COVID-19 pandemic has resulted in severe challenges for economic activities due to its global scale and unpredictable duration (Ivanov 2021; Xiong et al. 2021), our knowledge of how it influences business operations remains limited (Das et al. 2021). One critical element of marketing strategy is to create and maintain a strong brand (Erdem et al. 2006; Nguyen and Feng 2021). Prior studies have suggested that branding can foster performance in increasingly competitive markets (Madden et al. 2006; Worm and Srivastava 2014). Recent development further indicates that the salience of branding may become weaker on digital platforms (Mu and Zhang 2021). However, little is known about how the COVID-19 pandemic affects brand performance on digital platforms. Solutions This project will draw on signaling theory to examine how the COVID-19 pandemic influences the effect of name versus non-name brands on product performance in the digital platform. We plan to use weekly product sales data from a digital platform in China from 2018 to 2020. We will leverage the exogenous pandemic shock to use a difference-in-differences approach. We will compare the difference in product performance between name and non-name brands before and after the COVID-19 pandemic (i.e., 2019-2020). We will also examine the same effect in a parallel time window before the pandemic (i.e., 2018-2019) for a falsification test (cf. Cui et al. 2021). This approach will offer strong evidence for whether differences between name and non-name brands are driven by the pandemic shock. To understand how platform signals (i.e., live streaming use and platform competition) moderate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on brand performance. Reasons While the digital platform has dramatically reshaped the shopping landscape, the COVID-19 pandemic has made its role even more salient. Although a name brand has been a critical firm asset, recent development cautions about its declining role on digital platforms (Mu and Zhang 2021). On the digital platform, firms can rely on their product signals (e.g., price and features) or platform-based functions to enhance their credibility (Jean et al. 2021; Taeuscher 2019). According to signaling theory, firms can use multiple signals to mitigate information asymmetry (Ozmel et al. 2013). However, prior studies have investigated the roles of platform-based functions and firm-based signals separately, leaving their interplay underexplored (Jean et al. 2021; Jean and Kim 2021). Thus, it is necessary to discuss how the simultaneous use of platform signals and firms’ branding signals affect product performance during the COVID-19 pandemic. Solutions This project will investigate the moderating roles of platform signals for the interaction effect between the COVID-19 pandemic and brands. We will consider two important platform signals: live streaming use and platform competition. The former reflects how the focal product uses the digital platform to convey information, and the latter captures the competition among products in each category. The findings will show how platform signals and branding signals jointly affect the challenges from the COVID-19 pandemic. To understand how product characteristics (i.e., countries of origin (foreign versus local) and exchange history) moderate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on brand performance. Reasons A given product can be evaluated along different characteristics (Kushwaha and Shankar 2013), which may lead to different information availability. Given that a brand is a salient signal, prior studies have primarily investigated the contingent roles of industrial environments and supplier characteristics in brand performance (Nguyen and Feng 2021). However, prior studies have been silent on how product characteristics affect the role of branding during the COVID-19 pandemic. Solutions This project will investigate the moderating roles of product characteristics in the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on brand performance. Buyers may implicitly categorize products based on their origin and prior experience (Mandler et al. 2021). Thus, we consider two critical product characteristics: country of origin (foreign versus local) and exchange history. Examining their moderating effects can enrich the branding literature by showing the interplay between brands and product features during the COVID-19 pandemic.

17500522.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500522.value: The COVID-19 pandemic has rapidly engulfed the world and irreversibly changed the way people live, work, and interact. It has disrupted business operations and constrained supply and demand in the market. Health concerns and government stringency policies restrict suppliers’ ability to produce and deliver products. Constraints on mobility and high uncertainties also reduce buyers’ consumption intentions and purchase expenditures. While the economic and health consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic are well-documented, how it has impacted business performance is under-researched. Meanwhile, the COVID-19 outbreak brings new opportunities for digital platforms to address health concerns and facilitate business transactions. Thus, it is crucial for firms to enhance their performance on digital platforms. Given the central role brand plays in marketing strategy, prior studies have focused primarily on its value in offline markets and demonstrated its importance for performance. However, recent studies warn that the digital environment may diminish the role of brands, because digital platforms provide detailed product information that enables buyers to do a side-by-side comparison. Since the pandemic has led to significant changes in the external market environment, it is important to understand how the COVID-19 pandemic affects brand performance on digital platforms. To address these research gaps, our project will investigate how the COVID-19 pandemic affects the product performance of name versus non-name brands on digital platforms. Specifically, we aim to answer the following questions: 1) How does the COVID-19 pandemic affect the impact of name versus non-name brands on product performance on the digital platform? 2) How do platform signals (e.g., live streaming use and platform competition) influence the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on brand performance? 3) How do product characteristics (e.g., country of origin and exchange history) influence the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on brand performance? Given the possible continual occurrence of pandemics in the future, we anticipate that our research will provide fresh insights in understanding the impact of pandemics on firms’ marketing activities, especially their branding strategy. The findings will provide important managerial implications for firms to address the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic and understand how to achieve better brand performance on digital platforms. COVID-19 大流行迅速席卷全球，不可逆转地改变了人们的生活、工作和互动方式。 它扰乱了商业运转并限制了市场的供需。 健康问题和政府严格的政策限制了供应商生产和交付产品的能力。 流动性的限制和高度的不确定性也降低了购买者的消费意愿和购买支出。 虽然 COVID-19 大流行的经济和健康后果有众多研究，但它如何影响公司绩效的研究不足。 同时，COVID-19 的爆发为数字平台解决健康问题和促进商业交易带来了新的机会。 因此，对于企业而言，提高其在数字平台上的表现至关重要。 鉴于品牌在营销策略中的核心作用，之前的研究主要集中在其在线下市场的价值上，并证明了其对绩效的重要性。 然而，最近的研究警告说，数字环境可能会削弱品牌的作用，因为数字平台提供了详细的产品信息，使买家能够进行并排比较。 由于大流行导致外部市场环境发生重大变化，因此了解 COVID-19 大流行如何影响数字平台上的品牌表现非常重要。 为了解决这些研究空白，我们的项目将调查 COVID-19 大流行如何影响数字平台上知名品牌与非知名品牌的产品绩效。 具体而言，我们旨在回答以下问题： 1) COVID-19 大流行如何改变数字平台上知名品牌与非知名品牌对产品绩效的影响？ 2) 平台信号（例如，直播使用和平台竞争）如何影响 COVID-19 大流行对品牌绩效的影响？ 3) 产品特性（例如，原产国和交往历史）如何影响 COVID-19 大流行对品牌绩效的影响？ 鉴于未来COVID-19的可能持续，我们预计我们的研究将为了解流行病对公司营销活动，特别是品牌战略的影响提供新的见解。 这些发现将为公司应对 COVID-19 大流行的挑战并了解如何在数字平台上实现更好的品牌表现提供重要的管理意义。

17500722.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500722.value: 个人信贷市场的信息溢出及逆向选择效应

17500722.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500722.value: 在近年的消费市场中，金融机构越来越多的加强对自有信息源的使用并逐渐减少对征信评级等公共信息源的依赖。这使得不同金融机构的信用评估模型和借款决策差异化逐步加大，从而可能导致当前信贷市场的逆向选择问题变得更加严重。 本课题的目标是识别信贷市场中不同类型借贷者的信息持有状况，并了解其信息差异带来的逆向选择问题。本研究预计将通过整合多个关于消费者金融活动的微观数据对相应的逆向选择问题提供直接证据。 本研究将从两个维度考虑信息不对称的问题：一是同一消费者的其他金融活动如何对现有金融机构产生信息溢出，以及该消费者的逆向选择如何影响其未来对金融机构的选择。二是不同消费者的金融活动信息如果通过社群网络进行传导，从而影响掌握相关信息的金融机构对其他消费者的借贷决策。 整体而言，这些潜在的逆向选择问题意味着即使当下金融科技和大数据正在快速发展和广泛应用于金融行业，不同金融机构之间的信息壁垒仍然可能使得特定消费者群体面临更高的借贷成本甚至信贷约束。因此，我们预期该研究可以为监管方对于某些金融机构和科技公司的信息垄断对市场的影响提供更多的线索。

17500922.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500922.value: 學校支出的收益是否大於成本？對（淨）稅收的長期影響

17500922.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500922.value: In countries rich and poor, chronic underinvestment in primary and secondary education shocks the conscience. In the United States, students in poor urban and rural districts take tests based on textbooks their schools cannot buy; in China, a third of rural middle schoolers may have books but don’t have eye glasses to read them. Failures to invest in education have social and fiscal externalities: students who are not taught may one day rely on welfare, and may not earn enough to pay their share of taxes. But who will internalize the externality? In decentralized school systems like the United States or China, thousands of local governments share funding responsibility. In the corresponding, centralized fiscal systems, the central government collects most revenue. Perhaps, then, it is no surprise that education is undersupplied. But central policy makers in Washington and Beijing alike have begun to ask whether the responsibility to finance education should be theirs. Are the fiscal externalities from education spending large enough to justify central government intervention? How large? We propose direct evidence on fiscal externalities (and fiscal returns) to elementary and secondary education spending in the United States. We are the first to study the effect of education spending on federal revenue and transfers (welfare), in population-scale administrative data. We observe cohorts born in 1950-1998, exiting college in 1972-2020, and exposed to six decades of spending variation covering the entire history of school finance reforms where state governments massively increased education spending. Our latest-born cohorts are just starting their careers, and our earliest-born are already retired, so we observe key fiscal externalities throughout the whole lifecycle. To isolate the causal effect of education spending, we rely on a well-tested instrumental variables strategy using major reforms across the United States. Unusual detail in the administrative data also allows us to bolster the credibility of estimates by controlling for unobservables, addressing known sources of measurement error, and carrying out an analysis of heterogeneity across children that may be relevant for policy targeting. Our evidence will be timely. In the U.S., the Biden administration's proposals would expand federal education spending by forty percent, the most in half a century. In China, centrally-funded education expansion is a top-line goal in the 14th Five Year Plan. In follow-up work, we may examine fiscal externalities and incentives to fund education at the state and local level. 在富裕和貧窮的國家，初等和中等教育的長期投資不足有悖於人們的良知。在美國，身處貧困市區和農村的學生參加基於他們學校無法購買的教科書的考試；在中國，三分之一的農村中學生可能擁有書本卻沒有用以閱讀的眼鏡。 對教育投資的缺失有著社會與財政外部性：未受教育的學生也許有一天會靠福利生活，也可能賺不到足夠的錢來足額支付他們的稅款。但誰會將這種外部性內部化呢？在像美國或中國這樣分散的學校系統中，數千個地方政府分擔資助責任。而在相應的中央集權的財政體系中，中央政府收取大部分稅收收入。因此，教育供應不足也許並不奇怪。但是，華盛頓和北京的中央政策制定者都已開始思考他們是否應該承擔資助教育的責任。教育支出的財政外部性是否大到足以證明中央政府的干預是合理的？這個外部性有多大？ 我們提議提供關於美國中小學教育支出的財政外部性（和財政回報）的直接證據。 我們首創性地運用涵蓋全美國人口的行政數據來研究教育支出對聯邦稅收收入和（福利）轉移支付的影響。我們觀察的隊列出生於1950至1998年，在1972至2020年離開大學。這些隊列經歷了六十年的支出變化，跨越了州法院命令學校財政改革的整個歷史。其中最晚出生的隊列剛剛開啟他們的職業生涯，而最早出生的已經退休，因此我們能觀察到貫穿整個生命週期的關鍵財政外部效益。 我們利用一個基於美國各地的重大改革並經過充分測試的工具變量策略，來分離出教育支出的因果效應。異常詳細的行政數據也讓我們能通過控制不可觀察因素，解決已知的測量誤差來源，並分析不同兒童群體間的異質性（這種分析亦能使我們了解政策應針對的人群），從而提高估計的可信度。 我們的證據將是及時的。在美國，拜登政府提議把聯邦教育支出擴大40%，這是半個世紀以來最大的擴張。在中國，中央資助的教育擴張是“十四五”規劃的首要目標之一。 在後續工作中，我們可以在州和地方層面上研究財政外部性和資助教育的激勵措施。

17501022.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17501022.value: 對醫生診症效率隨輪班時間變化的研究及其在急診室等候時間管理中的應用

17501022.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501022.value: Motivated by an intriguing observation on the time-varying physician productivity (measured by the number of new patients seen per hour, or PPH) in hospital emergency departments (EDs), we investigate the transient behavior of individual physicians within their shifts by a continuous-time optimal control framework. We believe that the transient behavior is intrinsic, mainly induced by shift-based scheduling. We demonstrate through a simulation study that it is important to explicitly consider time-varying physician productivity rates to obtain accurate and valuable models for ED operations. Further more, we propose a queueing framework that incorporate the shift-hour dependent PPH rates and time-varying number of physicians, where the essence of analyzing the model would be dimension reduction by state aggregation. As a result, it will also allow system transient analysis through the uniformization of a continuous-time Markov chain, which can be integrated with off-the-shelf algorithms for physician staffing. Validated using data from two Canadian EDs, the simulation of our proposed queueing model can accurately capture the time-of-day-dependent patient waiting times with a simple parameter estimation procedure, which is among the first in the ED literature. In this proposed work, we first unveil the mechanism under the time-varying physician productivity. Then, we analyze the transient behavior of the proposed ED queueing framework that incorporates the observation of the time-varying productivity, and integrate the analysis with the physician scheduling problem. Finally, we plan to conduct a case study and propose better physician scheduling policies based on real data. This project requires more research work for both academic and practical contributions. First, we need to provide more analytical characterization of the optimization model and develop staffing policies based on our analysis. Secondly, we also need to demonstrate how our analysis of the stylized mathematical model could be extended to more complicated real systems. Finally, we would like to collaborate with our medical collaborators to analyze the feasibility and evaluate the performance of proposed policies in practice. 醫院急診室里通常將醫生每小時診治的新病人數量視為醫生診症效率。 從我們合作醫院中，我們觀察到一個有意思的現象：醫生的診症效率是隨著輪班時間變化的。 通過建立連續時間最佳控制模型，我們研究了醫生個體在輪班期間的行為。 我們認為這種行為是內在的，主要是由輪班工作安排引起。 通過對急診室進行模擬建模，我們發現在安排急診室醫生班次時結合考慮醫生 診症效率對於建模的準確性非常重要。 另外，我們提出了一個排隊系統模型，結合了隨時間變化的醫生效率和醫生數量，通過聚合多維狀態來降維。 我們通過連續時間瑪律可夫鏈的均勻化進行系統瞬態分析，並與現成的演算法集成，將此模型用於醫生排班優化。 我們使用來自兩個加拿大醫院急診室的數據，驗證了基於我們提出的排隊模型的模擬建模可以通過簡單的參數估計準確 反映一天中不同時間的患者等待時間。 在這個研究專案中，我們首先研究展示醫生診症效率隨時間變化的理論依據。 然後，我們研究比較了急診室排隊模型和實際模型的瞬態行為，並將此排隊模型的分析與醫生排班問題相結合。 最後，我們計劃進行案例研究，根據真實數據提出更好的醫生排班策略。 這個課題仍需要更多的工作來做出學術和實踐貢獻。 首先，我們需要對醫生個體輪班期間行為的優化模型進行更具體的分析。 其次，我們還需要證明我們對排隊模型的數學分析如何擴展到更複雜的真實系統。 最後，我們希望通過與我們合作的醫療機構的醫生，分析我們所優化提出的排班策略的可行性並評估該策略在實踐中的表現。

17501322.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501322.value: The food delivery industry has experienced significant growth in recent years, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic, which drives many consumers to choose food delivery over in-restaurant dining. The rapidly increasing demand and the huge competitive pressure to satisfy customers have led to a shortage of food delivery riders, longer working hours, and unrealistic target delivery time. As a result, many riders need to drive faster or sometimes even break traffic rules to deliver the food on time and avoid late penalty. With increasing news reports on the deaths or injuries of food delivery riders due to traffic incidents all over the world, governments and regulators have openly urged food delivery platforms to improve the safety and work conditions of riders. To seek a balance between rider work pressure and customer satisfaction, we collaborate with the largest online food delivery platform in China and propose to run three randomized field experiments to quantify both the short-term and long-term impact of different delivery time requirements on rider job performance and customer outcomes. Delivery time requirements are manipulated through either more strict or more lenient estimated time of arrival (ETA) for food delivery. The findings from this proposed research can help food delivery platforms design better algorithms in defining delivery time requirements to protect the interests of riders and at the same time maintain customer satisfaction and loyalty. 近年來，外賣配送行業經歷了顯著增長，尤其是在 COVID-19 大流行期間，這促使許多消費者選擇外賣而不是餐廳內用餐。快速增長的需求和滿足客戶的巨大競爭壓力導致外賣騎手短缺，工作時間延長，目標交付時間緊張。因此，許多騎手需要開得更快，甚至有時違反交通規則才能準時送餐，避免遲到罰款。隨著世界各地因交通事故導致外賣騎手死亡或受傷的新聞報導越來越多，各國政府和監管機構公開敦促外賣平台改善外賣騎手的安全和工作條件。為了在騎手的工作壓力和客戶滿意度之間尋求平衡，我們與某在線外賣平台合作，通過進行隨機現場實驗，使用更嚴格或更寬鬆的預計送餐時間 (ETA) 來控制送餐時間要求，以量化不同的外賣時間要求如何影響騎手的短期和長期工作績效和客戶滿意度。這項研究的結果可以幫助外賣配送平台設計更好的算法來定義配送時間要求，以保護騎手的利益，同時保持客戶滿意度和忠誠度。

17501322.label: Realisation of objectives
17501322.value: This research project set out to examine the effects of varying delivery time requirements on food delivery rider performance, efficiency, customer satisfaction, and platform dynamics. Through a combination of field experimentation, regression discontinuity design (RDD), and survey analysis, the project has successfully achieved its core objectives, generating robust empirical insights into the behavioral and economic consequences of conservative ETA algorithms. Objective 1: Quantify the short-term effect of different delivery time requirements on food delivery riders’ job performance and customer satisfaction This objective was fully realized through a six-day field experiment conducted in a major Chinese city. By extending the ETA by five minutes in selected delivery zones, the study observed significant improvements in rider job performance. Riders strategically adapted by batching more orders, which led to a 15% increase in daily income and improved hourly earnings. Importantly, these changes did not compromise service quality—consumer ratings showed a statistically significant improvement, albeit with a modest effect size. The RDD analysis further confirmed that moderate ETA extensions reduced delivery delays and penalties, while increasing rider responsiveness and per-order income. These findings demonstrate that conservative ETA policies can enhance rider performance without diminishing customer satisfaction. Objective 2: Quantify the effect of different delivery time requirements on rider work efficiency, work pressure, and retention This objective was addressed through both experimental and survey data. The field experiment revealed that riders worked fewer total hours but increased their active working time, indicating improved work efficiency. The absence of significant changes in penalty rates and delivery delays suggests that riders were able to maintain service standards while reducing idle time. Survey responses corroborated these findings: 88% of riders reported a willingness to batch more orders when ETAs were extended, and 76% experienced income increases. Riders also reported reduced time pressure and greater flexibility, aligning with the autonomy-enhancing goals of conservative ETA design. While long-term retention was not directly measured, the observed income-targeting behavior and improved working conditions suggest potential positive effects on rider retention. Objective 3: Quantify the effect of different delivery time requirements on customer purchase tendency, purchase frequency, and retention A pre-experiment pilot study tested consumer reactions to ETA extensions of varying lengths. Results showed that extensions beyond five minutes significantly reduced purchase likelihood, with a six-minute extension leading to a measurable drop in conversion rates. These findings informed the design of the main experiment, which capped ETA extensions at five minutes to preserve consumer demand. While the main study did not directly measure purchase frequency or long-term retention, the RDD analysis showed that conservative ETAs reduced complaints, dissatisfaction, and urgency behaviors, indicating improved alignment between consumer expectations and service delivery. These outcomes suggest that moderate ETA adjustments can enhance consumer experience without harming short-term purchasing behavior. In summary, the project has successfully met its primary objectives, offering actionable insights into how algorithmic design can balance operational efficiency with human welfare in the gig economy. The findings have implications for platform governance, labor policy, and the future of algorithmic management.

17501322.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501322.value: This research project investigated the impact of varying delivery time requirements on food delivery platforms, focusing on rider performance, efficiency, and customer behavior. Using a mixed-methods approach—including a field experiment, regression discontinuity design (RDD), and a rider survey—the project successfully achieved its core objectives. First, the short-term effects of conservative ETA algorithms were quantified through a six-day field experiment in a major Chinese city. A five-minute extension in delivery time led to a significant increase in rider income (over 15%) without compromising delivery punctuality or customer satisfaction. Riders adapted by batching more orders and optimizing active working hours, demonstrating strategic behavior in response to algorithmic changes. Second, the project assessed rider work efficiency and pressure. The extended ETA reduced idle time and increased active delivery hours, improving overall productivity. Survey results confirmed that riders perceived reduced time pressure and greater autonomy. Experienced riders benefited most, showing higher earnings and better batching efficiency, while higher-educated riders were less responsive to algorithmic adjustments, likely due to differing motivations. Third, the project examined customer behavior. A pre-experiment pilot revealed that ETA extensions beyond five minutes negatively affected purchase likelihood, guiding the design of the main experiment. The RDD analysis showed that moderate ETA extensions reduced complaints, dissatisfaction, and urgency behaviors, indicating improved alignment between customer expectations and actual delivery performance. The research has been recognized academically, receiving a Major Revision at Information Systems Research (ISR) and is currently under second-round review. It has also been accepted for presentation at three prestigious conferences: the Workshop on Information Systems and Economics (WISE 2024), the 21st Annual Symposium on Statistical Challenges in eCommerce Research (SCECR 2025), and the Conference on Information Systems and Technology (CIST 2025). Additionally, the project contributed to capacity building by training one PhD student, who was actively involved in data analysis, field experiment design, and survey implementation. In summary, the project has delivered strong empirical evidence on how algorithmic design can balance operational efficiency with rider welfare and customer satisfaction. These findings offer actionable insights for platform governance and gig economy policy, with broader implications for ethical algorithmic management.

17501322.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501322.value: This project has laid a strong empirical foundation for understanding how algorithmic delivery time adjustments affect rider behavior and customer experience. Building on these findings, future research can explore the long-term effects of conservative ETA algorithms on rider retention, customer loyalty, and platform profitability. Additionally, coordinating ETA adjustments with dispatch and routing algorithms may further enhance efficiency and reduce delivery costs.

17501322.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501322.value: This research project looked at how changing the estimated delivery time for food orders affects delivery riders and customers. Most food delivery apps use very tight time estimates to make deliveries fast, but this can put a lot of pressure on riders, leading to stress and even accidents. To test a better approach, the researchers worked with a major food delivery platform in China and ran experiments where delivery times were slightly extended—by just five minutes. They found that this small change gave riders more flexibility, allowing them to group multiple orders together and earn more money, while also working fewer hours. Importantly, customers were still happy with the service, and there were fewer complaints and delays. The study also showed that experienced riders benefited the most from the extra time, while riders with higher education were less likely to adjust their strategies. Customers responded positively to the more relaxed delivery times, as it matched their expectations better. Overall, the findings show that small changes in delivery time can make a big difference for both riders and customers, helping create a fairer and more efficient gig economy.

17501622.value: 外賣平台與餐飲企業的合同機制研究與效率改進

17501622.label: Project Objectives
17501622.value: To solve the base model and compare three different contract schemes: commission plus membership fee, commission plus service fee, and service fee plus membership fee. We will obtain basic insights about the impact of each type of fee. To extend the base model to analyze cases in which the offline dining customers differ in their acceptable wait time. In these cases, accepting online orders may affect only some offline diners, so the opportunity costs for accepting small and large online orders may be different for the restaurant. To extend the base model to analyze cases in which the online dining customers are not infinitely cost sensitive. In these cases, the platform may choose to set the delivery fee differently and the restaurant may choose to set the online food price differently. Hence, how customer cost sensitivity affects the efficiency and effectiveness of the contract terms is not straightforward. To explore other extensions of the base model, such as incorporating limited dining capacity for the restaurant and considering a continuous distribution of acceptable wait time for the offline customers.

17501622.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501622.value: Online food delivery platforms are becoming a critical source of income for restaurants, but these platforms usually charge a high commission together with many fees, which deters many restaurant owners. Motivated by the recent appeals (during the pandemic) from restaurants to remove or reduce commissions for online food ordering and delivery services, we propose this project to study the contract design problem between a platform and a restaurant. We aim to answer three key questions. First, if the commission is waived and replaced by different fees, will the platform be better or worse off? Second, will the restaurant be better or worse off? Third, from a regulator's perspective, is there a way to increase the profits of both the platform and the restaurant by regulating the form of the contract? A key conflict between a platform and a restaurant is how to set the online minimum consumption value. When a commission contract is used, the platform loves large orders and hates small orders, because the commission is proportional to the order value, but the delivery cost is independent. Hence, the platform would ask the restaurant to set up a positive minimum consumption value. However, the restaurant would prefer smaller online orders to larger ones because (i) the set-up cost for each order can be ignored and (ii) for the same amount of increase in the kitchen utilization and revenue, smaller orders have a weaker impact on the offline diners' experience (i.e., the wait time for food preparation). Such a conflict may cause inefficiencies. To maintain a simple fee structure, we consider a platform that only charges two of the three fees: commission (which is proportional to the order value), service fee (a fixed fee for each order), and membership fee (a fixed fee for each restaurant). We plan to use a stylized game-theoretic model to compare the effectiveness and efficiency of three different contracts. 線上訂餐平台或外賣平台已經成為了餐飲企業一個非常重要的銷售渠道和收入來源。但是，外賣平台通常擁有巨大的市場權力並對餐飲企業收取很高的佣金，因此令很多餐館經營者叫苦連天或者望而卻步。近期，很多餐飲企業都呼籲平台降低或者取消佣金，以便這些企業能夠維持一定的利潤。本項目由此出發，研究平台究竟該如何與餐飲企業簽訂合約，是否能通過降低或取消佣金取得雙贏。 在平台和餐飲企業之間，一個主要的矛盾來自於如何設置最低消費金額。當平台以收取佣金為主時，平台很自然會偏愛大金額訂單，因為給定同樣的配送成本，訂單金額越大平台收入越高。然而，對於餐館來講，大訂單比一定比小訂單好，因為大訂單會造成廚房過度忙碌而影響線下食客體驗，反而廚房可以見縫插針處理小訂單。這個矛盾會使得雙方對最低消費金額的設置存在分歧進而影響雙方合作效率。 本項目將通過數學建模來比較幾種合同模式，分析每種合同模式下餐館對最低消費金額的設置以及平台的最優合同參數，最終得出各種合同模式的運營效率。

17501722.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501722.value: 創造力對於創造附加值和新價值至關重要，因此也是現代組織的競爭力所在。創造力在一定程度上是具自主性的，因為它來自於員工的思想，而且或許無法有效地通過威權主義的方式來強迫實現和分享。就過程和結果而言，創造力在一定程度上是有風險的，因為，失敗是過程的一部分，而創意的成果則是不確定的。由此可見，為了有效地管理創造力，必須同時考慮自主行為的誘因和創造力風險的緩衝。我們提出了一種針對員工創造力的誘因-風險緩衝方案，以針對創造力的自主性和風險性。在誘因方面，我們關注領導的創造力願景，這種願景主要着重在創造性的重要性和未來狀態。願景是當前管理學的一個重要主題，但相關研究仍不夠深入。我們認為，領導的創造力願景能夠誘導員工參與到創造的過程中，從而提高員工自身的創造力。我們在此基礎上提出兩種風險緩衝：其一為領導對失敗的容忍度，是創造過程中失敗的風險緩衝；其二為可感知的公平性，是對結果不確定性的風險緩衝。結合誘因和緩衝，我們提出了一個員工創造力的調節中介模型，其中員工參與創造的過程對領導的創造力願景和員工的創造力之間關係的中介作用，由領導對失敗的容忍度和員工對公平的感知共同調節。我們提出研究1，開發並驗證領導創造力願景的量表。我們進一步提出了研究2和研究3，利用員工的二波面板數據和主管提供的員工創造力數據進行實地研究。這一方案有望對創造力的理論化和實踐作出重要貢獻，亦為創造力的誘因-風險緩衝理論鋪平了道路。當中的理論和概念框架通過側重於創造力的自主性和風險性，為解決工作場所的創造力問題提供具體的指引。

17501722.label: Realisation of objectives
17501722.value: We developed, refined and validated the proposed conceptual model. Specifically, we established leader creativity vision as an important antecedent of employee creativity. We further found support for the relationship between leader creativity vision on vision recognition and territorial behavior. Vision must be recognized to be effective, as in the case that vision that is published on company website without employee recognition would have no effect on employee. We found an important form of employee engagement in creativity in the form of territorial behavior, which is representation by regarding behavioral indication that specific objects, target, entity and space as ‘mine’. This is consistent with the reasoning that inducement is needed for creativity, in that when one displays territorial behavior regarding one’s job territory, one would be motivated to mark, defend and expand this territory, thereby inducing job outcome, including creativity. To buffer against risk, we found that equity, or the perception that return is commensurate with one’s investment, was needed for employee creativity. We developed and validated a measure of leader creativity vision. Please see Study 1 in paper “LeaderCreativity”. We tested the model with two studies, one was a 3-wave matched supervisor-subordinate dyad field study and the other was a pre-registered experiment. Please see Study 2 and 3, respectively, in paper “LeaderCreativity”. We finished two papers, one was the “LeaderCreativity” paper. The other one was a review paper on leader vision, attached as “LeaderVision” to this report. Along the way of our exploration of the leader vision construct, we realized that vision as studies at different levels across different literature with different definitions. We decided to develop a deep understanding of this construct and ended up with a review paper. We have submitted the vision review paper to a journal but have withheld submission of the 3-study empirical paper before we plan to submit part of that paper to a conference. We hesitated to present part of this study in a conference because we would like to protect the research idea until we finish the entire study. Once part of the LeaderCreativity paper is submitted to a conference, we shall submit the attached completed manuscript to a journal.

17501722.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501722.value: We found convergent and discriminant validity for the leader creativity vision scale. In the LeaderVision review paper, we examined motivational effectives and communication dynamics of leader vision. In the empirical paper, we found the leader creativity vision will enhance employ recognition of the vision, thereby enhance employee territorial behavior for their job, which in turn enhance employee creativity. Specifically, of the three forms of territorial behavior, marking, defending and expanding, territorial expansion positively enhances creativity. The proposed reason for this is that when employees expand their territory, they will have more resources such as information to be creative. Further, perceived equity of their creative endeavor by employees moderated the relationship between territorial behavior and creativity. The direct relationship between territorial behavior and creativity, as well as the moderating effect of perceived equity on this relationship, yield support only from a 3-way matched supervisor-employee dyad field study, but also from a preregistered experiment. Overall, there was strong evidence that to enhance employee creativity, leader creativity vision is an important antecedent with both employee initiatives in the form of territorial behavior and perceived equity as a mediator and moderator, respectively.

17501722.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501722.value: We would like to continue the research on impact of leader creativity vision on employee territorial behavior and consequently employee creativity. While we proposed a relationship between territorial behavior and creativity, the explanations for this relationship have not been empirically tested. For example, territorial expansion may lead to additional resources. We would like to examine roles of specific resources such as information and social network in this relationship. Further, territorial expansion may have negative effects, especially when it is perceived to have intruded on other’s territory. It is interesting and important to examine territorial expansion as a double-edged sword and theorize how to leverage its advantages and counteract its negative effects.

17501722.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501722.value: Employee creativity is a rare but valuable output to organizations. To be creative, however, is difficult and requires significant leadership to achieve. We propose that leaders may provide creativity vision as a motivator. A vision provides a desirable and meaningful state for employees to achieve together. When such a vision is recognized by employees, they will take up the creative task as their territory, thereby motivating them to exert extraordinary effort to protect and enhance positive outcomes in their territory, thereby enhance creativity. As creativity is difficult and requires extraordinary effort, employees may perceive the reward for creativity as commensurate to their input into creativity. Overall, leaders who provides vision and equity reward will be more effective in enhance employee creativity.

17501922.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501922.value: We propose to study whether and how the accounting quality of licensee and licensor in a product market affects the design of payment provisions in licensing contracts. Prior literature provides evidence consistent with the contracting role of accounting in the product market. Payment provisions are a key feature of business contracts (Lafontaine and Slade, 2012). Contracting parties negotiate according to the trade-off between precise contracts (i.e., fixed-price contracts) and accounting-based arrangements, such as revenue-sharing contracts (e.g., Joskow, 1988, 1990; Crocker and Masten, 1991; Crocker and Reynolds, 1993). However, there is no clear understanding of whether and how accounting attributes affect the design of product-market contract terms in general (fixed payment versus performance sharing). Nor is there evidence on the design of payment provisions regarding how accounting information would be used (e.g., revenue, gross profit or net profit) in specific. Our proposed research aims to fill this void. We predict that when the licensee’s accounting quality is low, fixed pricing is more likely to be used so that opportunism by the licensee may be avoided. When the licensor’s accounting quality is low, contingent pricing may be preferred, as the licensor has low-quality information to determine pricing for the license and may rely on the licensee’s performance to determine a proper value of the contract. Empirically, we plan to collect a large sample of license contract from SEC Edgar and hand collect the price provisions and other terms from each license contract. We will explore the associated between payment provisions and the accounting quality proxies of both the licensor and the licensee. Regarding payment provisions, we will investigate both the choice between fixed-price and royalties payment, and the choice of accounting metrics for royalty base when contracts use royalty-payment terms. We further plan to establish the causal impact by exploiting the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 as an exogenous shock to the accounting quality. We then conduct cross-sectional tests exploring uncertainties regarding the estimation of transaction value, the concern of opportunism and the availability of alternative monitoring mechanisms. In summary, contributing to the accounting literature, this evidence is expected to enrich the growing mass of literature on the real economic consequences of accounting information. The project is expected to not only yield important insights for academicians on better understanding of contracting theories under the context of accounting, but also to practitioners and regulators on the design of product market contracts. 我們建議研究，被許可人和許可人的會計質量是否影響產品市場許可合同中付款條款的設計。已有的文獻提供會計在產品市場中作用的證據。特別是，付款條款是商業合同的一個關鍵特徵。締約雙方根據相互之間的取捨，基於會計的安排進行合同談判，例如收益分享合同。 但是，對於會計屬性是否影響產品市場合同條款的設計（固定付款與業績分享）並沒有清晰的認識。也沒有證據表明，如何使用會計信息設計付款條款（例如，收入、毛利或淨額利潤分享）。我們提出的研究旨在填補這一空白。 我們預測，當被許可人的會計質量較低時，更有可能採用固定定價，以避免被許可人的機會主義。當許可方會計質量低，局部定價可能是首選，因為許可人有低質量信息來確定許可的定價，並且可能依賴被許可人的盈利，來確定合同的適當價值。 在數據分析上，我們計劃從 SEC Edgar 和手工收集每個許可合同中的價格條款和其他條款。我們探討支付準備金與許可人和被許可人會計質量之間的關聯。關於付款規定，我們將調查固定價格和特許權使用費之間的選擇，以及會計選擇在作爲，合同使用特許權，使用費支付條款，和特許權使用費基礎的指標。 我們進一步計劃利用 2002 年的薩班斯-奧克斯利法案，作爲會計質量的外生衝擊，確定因果關係。然後我們測試有關交易價值估計的不確定性，機會主義和替代監測機制的可用性對於結果的影響。 總之，關於會計的實際經濟後果的文獻越來越多，這一證據有望豐富為會計文獻做出貢獻。該項目預計不僅為更好地理解契約理論的背景，產生重要的見解，也給從業者和監管者關於產品市場的設計合同。

17501922.label: Realisation of objectives
17501922.value: The objectives have been successfully accomplished, and the paper has been completed. We have received feedback from the conferences and journal submissions, and further revisions are being made to meet the publication requirements. To achieve the objectives, we use a sample of 1,165 material licensing contracts from U.S. public firms over the period 1986–2020. We manually read the assignment section of each licensing contract to classify the assignment restrictions of the license to a potential acquirer of the licensee. We find that approximately half (57.4%) of the contracts explicitly permit the licensee to assign the agreement without any restrictions, suggesting considerable variation in assignability. Our primary measure of assignment restrictiveness is an indicator variable that equals one if a contract has any form of restriction on assignability and zero if the clause allows the licensee to assign the agreement freely. Following prior studies (e.g., Agrawal and Knoeber, 1998; Schilingemann et al., 2002; Phillips and Zhdanov, 2013), we measure licensee takeover likelihood based on the frequency of M&As involving target firms from the licensee firm’s industry in a three-year window preceding the commencement of the license agreement. We find a robust positive association between licensee takeover likelihood and the use of assignment restrictions. A one standard deviation increase in the probability of licensee takeover is associated with a 12.0% increase in the probability of stipulating a restrictive contract, representing a 28.2% increase in the proportion of the overall sample. This finding suggests that, on average, when there is a high possibility of licensee takeover, licensors’ concern regarding protecting their proprietary information dominates over other financial and strategic concerns; consequently, the assignment of the licensing contract is more restrictive. The result is robust to a host of sensitivity tests, including controlling for industry and year fixed effects, using alternative time windows to measure takeover probability, and using alternative outcome variables that allow for richer variations in assignment restrictiveness. To lend credence to our attribution of the findings to licensee takeover likelihood rather than other unobservable factors correlated with industry-level takeover frequency, we examine the interaction effect of state anti-takeover laws and licensee takeover likelihood on the adoption of restrictive assignment clauses. The adoption of anti-takeover laws in a state reduces licensors’ concerns regarding the takeover of licensees, thus inducing exogenous variations across different states. If the documented positive association is driven by heightened takeover likelihood rather than confounding factors, we expect that following a state’s adoption of anti-takeover laws, the positive association between licensee takeover likelihood and the assignment restrictiveness will be mitigated. We find the result to be consistent with this expectation. This result implies that contractual provisions and state laws are complementary mechanisms for governing the dissemination of knowledge across firm boundaries. Next, we conduct cross-sectional analyses to further illuminate the underlying mechanisms of the observed effects. Our first set of analyses explores licensors’ proprietary cost concerns. We use two measures to evaluate licensors’ proprietary cost concerns. The first measure explores the nature of a licensing transaction. Compared with patents, a licensor’s know-how and trade secrets are more vulnerable to misappropriation (e.g., Glaeser, 2018). We thus expect proprietary cost concerns to be greater when the licensing transaction involves know-how and trade secrets. The second measure of proprietary cost concerns is the occurrence of competition-related words in a licensing contract, which captures licensors’ concerns about information leakage to competitors (Li et al., 2013). Compared with other types of M&As, the acquisition of a licensee by a competitor of the licensor is likely to result in a greater risk of undesirable knowledge diffusion (Shapiro, 1985; Katz and Shapiro, 1987). We find robust evidence in both tests that the positive effect of licensee takeover likelihood on the assignment restrictiveness increases with licensors’ proprietary cost concerns. We then examine whether the documented positive association between the assignment restrictiveness and licensee takeover likelihood changes with the expected commercialization benefits due to licensee takeover. We use variations in payment provisions as a proxy for the expected benefits. When licensors are entitled to higher royalty shares, they are likely to derive greater benefits by assigning the license to a potential acquirer who has enhanced capacities for commercializing the technology, thereby resulting in higher royalty revenue. Consistent with this notion, we find that licensee takeover likelihood has a smaller positive impact on the assignment restrictiveness among contracts with higher royalty rates, suggesting that licensors’ incentives to stipulate restrictive assignment provisions are moderated by the commercialization benefits expected from licensee takeovers. Finally, we examine the consequences of assignment restrictiveness in two ways. First, we test the effect on licensees’ (realized) future takeover probabilities. We find that assignment restrictions are associated with a lower likelihood of future licensee takeover in industries with high takeover likelihood. This finding supports the notion that an ex-ante restrictive assignment design helps prevent undesirable ex-post knowledge diffusion by reducing licensee takeovers. Second, we test the relationship between assignment restrictiveness and market reaction to quantify the net economic effects of assignability on licensees. As assignment restrictions limit cash-out opportunities and disincentivize investment by licensees, we expect them to reduce the value creation resulting from licensing agreements for licensees. Consistent with this prediction, we find that while the 3-day cumulative abnormal return (CAR) around the contract date of a license agreement is on average positive for licensees, it is 2.1% smaller for restrictive licensing contracts than for those with lax assignment clauses. These results reinforce the argument that lax assignment clauses are valuable to licensees, whereas the protection of proprietary costs through assignment restrictions may compromise the value of the collaboration.

17501922.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501922.value: Our study investigates the relationship between knowledge diffusion, proxied by licensee takeover likelihood, and the restrictiveness of assignment clauses in licensing contracts. Despite the importance of contracts in governing the information flow between collaborative partners, little is known about the use of contract provisions to ex ante control the boundaries of knowledge diffusion. An assignment clause pertains to the allocation of decision rights regarding the diffusion of innovation, specifying the conditions under which a licensee may assign the license and related know-how to a successor in the event of a takeover (Braeger, 2001; Ziff, 2002; Newman, 2013). Our study enriches the literature on innovation by demonstrating how firms utilize contract clauses, such as the assignment clause, to mitigate proprietary information leakage without hampering knowledge diffusion. Additionally, the research expands the understanding of technology-driven M&As beyond the characteristics of acquirers and target firms, emphasizing the importance of contractual mechanisms in shaping the outcome of technology-driven M&As. Grounded in incomplete contract theory, this research provides empirical evidence of how decision rights allocations in licensing contracts help mitigate hold-up problems between licensors and licensees. The findings further elucidate strategies for innovation management by examining the interplay among financial management, proprietary cost concerns, and contract designs, offering valuable insights into the dynamics of knowledge diffusion across firm boundaries.

17501922.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501922.value: The project can be further enhanced by conducting additional tests on the legal implications of the assignment clause in licensing contracts. Specifically, we aim to examine how courts interpret various forms of the assignment clause to protect the intellectual property (IP) of licensors. This analysis will include an investigation of relevant regulations, encompassing both statutory and case law, that influence the enforceability of these provisions. Furthermore, it is essential to assess the effectiveness of the assignment clause in preventing mergers and acquisitions (M&As) of rival firms from gaining access to the licensed IP. To implement this proposed direction, we plan to conduct more comprehensive cross-sectional tests focusing on the characteristics of different jurisdictions and regulatory regimes. This will allow us to determine whether the factors influencing the restrictiveness of assignment clauses vary across different legal environments. Additionally, we will perform outcome tests that correlate with the cross-sectional variables identified, assessing whether the actual outcomes of M&As differ based on the contract's characteristics and the legal context. By broadening our empirical analysis in these areas, we aim to provide deeper insights into the interplay between legal interpretations, regulatory frameworks, and the effectiveness of contractual provisions in safeguarding licensors’ interests. These findings could significantly contribute to a more robust understanding of how well-designed assignment clauses can mitigate risks associated with knowledge diffusion and enhance innovation management strategies.

17501922.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501922.value: This research studies whether and how inventors use contractual design to govern the boundaries of knowledge diffusion in licensing transactions. While the takeover of licensees by third-party firms—a key conduit for knowledge diffusion that is unforeseeable when a licensing agreement is drafted—may bolster licensing value due to acquirers’ superior capacity, it arouses licensors’ concerns about the exposure of proprietary cost. The licensor weighs these costs and benefits to define the boundaries of knowledge diffusion through assignment clauses. We find that the possibility of licensee takeover increases the assignment restrictiveness, suggesting the dominance of proprietary cost concerns. The effect is stronger when licensors have greater concerns about proprietary cost but weakens when the commercialization benefits expected from licensee takeovers are greater. Further analyses reveal that restrictive assignment clauses effectively reduce licensees’ future takeovers when their takeover probability is high. Finally, we find evidence that constraining knowledge diffusion to safeguard proprietary information may compromise collaboration value.

17502822.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502822.value: Jump risk is one of the leading explanations to the excess returns of currencies. Theoretically, introducing jumps in an incomplete financial market can potentially solve several exchange rate puzzles. However, it is hard to obtain direct empirical evidence about jumps in exchange rates mainly due to the low-frequency occurrence of jumps. We introduce a novel model-free and non-parametric approach to quantify common jump risks in FX and stock markets that overcomes the difficulty in the literature. We identify a tradable portfolio that only loads on jump risks, and is not exposed to any diffusion risks. Accordingly, any variation in the portfolio value originates from realized jumps in exchange rates and stock prices, and the average return of the portfolio quantifies the jump risk premium. We can estimate the jump risk premium even if no jump is realized within our sample as the jump risk is priced in the portfolio value. Thus, our approach does not suffer from the well-know peso problem. Finally, our approach allows for any stochastic process in diffusion risk loadings of exchange rates and stocks as all diffusion risk loadings of the portfolio cancel out. We apply the framework to quantify the jump risk premia in popular currency trading strategies, and compare with jumps and jump risk premia obtained using other approaches. 跳跃风险是货币超额收益的重要解释之一。理论上，在不完全金融市场模型中引入跳跃风险可以解释数个汇率谜题。然而，由于跳跃的低频率发生，获得直接的汇率跳跃风险的经验证据十分困难。我们介绍了一种全新的，不依赖模型的非参数方法来量化汇率和股票市场中的共同的跳跃风险，克服了文献中寻找跳跃风险证据的难题。我们构造了一个可交易的资产组合，它只有跳跃风险，而没有其他扩散风险。所以，任何资产组合价值的变化都来源于汇率和股票价格中实现的跳跃风险，而这个资产组合的平均收益即是跳跃风险的风险溢价。即使在样本中没有观测到跳跃，我们依然可以估计跳跃风险的风险溢价。因此，我们的方法不受限于广为人知的比索问题。最后，我们的方法允许任意扩散过程的汇率风险，因为所有的扩散风险都会相互抵消。我们把这一方法用于量化流行的汇率交易策略中的跳跃风险溢价，以及与其他方法估计得到的结果加以比较。

17502822.label: Realisation of objectives
17502822.value: We have realized the majority of objectives listed above. First, we have successfully proposed a model-free new approach to measure the common jump risk premia in currency market and construct portfolios to measure it in the data (we call it cojump portfolio). The portfolio is only exposed to the cojump risk. This achieves objective 1 and 2. Second, we use econometric methods to identify realized jumps in the sample, which achieves objective 3. Third, we compute the average return of the cojump portfolio measure the cojump risk premia and we measure such risk premia currency by currency in the cross-section and time series. We examine the cojump risk premia for high- and low-interest-rate currencies, which is related to the carry trade portfolios. This step achieves objective 5 and part of 6. As for momentum and value strategies, jump risks are not particularly relevant for them, so we drop this part. We compare the computed average jump risk premia to the ones implied by standard rare disaster models and find a tension. This finding gives us new ways to discipline such models and quantify the contribution of jump risk premia in overall currency risk premia. We choose not to compare to the high-frequency-data implied jumps after trial because we figure out the use of high frequency data that we have access to is not sufficient to identify jumps anyway. Similarly, term structure models impose strong assumptions on identifying jumps and thus is not directly comparable to our strategy. That explains why objective 4 and 7 is not fully achieved.

17502822.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502822.value: We develop a novel model-free, ex ante measure of risk premia compensation for the risk of common jump in equity price the exchange rate. Utilizing the quanto forward prices, we construct a selffinancing portfolio that is only exposed to the risk of equity price and exchange rate cojump, but not to diffusive risks or idiosyncratic jump risks in equity price and exchange rate. The average return of this portfolio, excluding infrequent realized jumps, equals the cojump risk premia (CJP). The CJP exhibit moderate cross-sectional heterogeneity and common time-series fluctuations. The difference of CJP between high- and low-interest-rate currencies implies that jump risk premia only accounts for 38% of the overall currency risk premia. In the meantime, we measure the reverse cojump risk premia (reverse CJP) constructed with quanto forwards for foreign equity market index in USD, which is informative about the relative importance of country-specific jumps.

17502822.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17502822.value: The project outcome can be used in real time as an ex ante measure of jump risk premia that can guide risk management, portfolio managers and policy makers. To achieve that, we need real-time updates of quanto forward prices. In principle, we can create a website, maintain and update our measure in real time.

17502822.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502822.value: International investors particularly concern about large stock market crash or exchange rate depreciations. If they have to bear such risk, they require higher returns. In the literature, there lacks a good quantification of risk premia specific to these large risks (jump risk). We use the price of relatively new derivative contracts, quanto forwards, to construct a self-financing portfolio that only exposes investors to these large risks. The average return of this portfolio is a measure of the associated compensation. We find that this risk premia is higher for high-interest-rate currencies than low-interest-rate ones, but the magnitude difference is small compared to the implication of standard models. In this way, our finding serves as a useful discipline on macro-financial modeling of exchange rate and stock markets.

17502922.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502922.value: Company managers are often rewarded with company stocks and options so that they have incentives to maximize shareholder value and have ‘skin in the game’. However, in practice, managers who have significant amounts of personal wealth tied to their companies often engage in the over-the-counter derivatives transactions to hedge the economic loss risk arising from a decline in share price. Such personal (or compensation) hedging is not true sale of the stock owned by a manager and so are not required to be disclosed, but the hedging can undo the intended effect of incentive-based compensation, and can make the publicly disclosed stock ownership information misleading to investors. Not surprisingly, proxy advisors such as Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) and Glass Lewis who advise institutional investors to vote in shareholder meetings regard such hedging as a ‘bad’ practice, and recommend to vote against directors hedge their stock ownership. On the other hand, permitting hedging of stock ownership could be desirable under some circumstances (e.g., when corporate risk-taking via R&D is essential) as it helps mitigate a CEO’s concern over making risky but positive-net present value investment, reduce the incentive of a CEO in an overvalued firm to engage in opportunistic behaviors to maintain the high stock price, and lower the amount of risk premium paid by the company to the CEO. As a result, there is a longstanding debate over the pros and cons of compensation hedging, let alone over the disclosure requirement of personal hedging. Regulatory efforts in the U.S. to increase the transparency of compensation hedging started in the SEC’s rule that allows firms to judge whether the disclosure is material and necessary in 2006 and culminated in the 2018 SEC disclosure mandate requiring a firm to disclose its policy on whether to permit executive compensation hedging or not. The 2018 disclosure mandate applies to companies whose fiscal years begin on or after July 1, 2019. The current project aims to provide a timely study to understand the real effects of the mandatory disclosure of a firm’s hedging policy on executive compensation, firms’ risk-taking and valuation. The study not only helps add to the limited research on disclosure regulation in general, but also helps investors better assess a firm’s efficacy of incentive compensation and the risk of investing in the firm. Our research also has important implications for regulators and has relevance to Hong Kong, an international financial center. 公司通常会授予股票和期权给公司管理层旨在使其利益与股东的利益保持一致。在实践中，因为管理层的大量个人财富和公司股价捆绑在一起，他们通常会进行场外衍生品交易来对冲股价下跌带来的经济损失风险。因为这种个人的对冲行为不是管理者真实出售所持有的股票，所以不需要按内幕交易的要求进行披露，但这种对冲行为削弱甚至抵消了薪酬激励的预期效果，并使公开披露的管理者持股信息对投资者产生误导。自然地，为机构投资者在股东大会上进行投票提供意见的顾问公司Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) 和 Glass Lewis等将这种对冲行为视为一种“不好的”做法，并建议机构投资者在董事选举时向对冲自身所持股票的董事投出反对票。另一方面，允许管理者对冲其所持股票可能也是有益的，因为对冲有助于减轻CEO对进行高风险但净现值为正的投资项目（如研发活动）的担忧，削弱高估值公司CEO为维持高股价做出的盈余操纵的动机，降低公司支付给CEO的风险溢价金额。因此，关于薪酬对冲利弊的争论由来已久，更不用说关于个人对冲行为披露要求的争论了。 为提高薪酬对冲的透明度，美国SEC于2006年发布了一项政策，允许公司判断对冲披露是否重要和必要；随后SEC在2018年发布的披露措施中强制要求公司披露其是否允许高管对薪酬进行对冲的政策。2018年的这项强制披露要求适用于会计年度开始于2019年7月1日或之后的公司。 本项目旨在及时研究公司对冲政策的强制披露的经济后果包括对高管薪酬、公司风险承担和公司估值的影响。这个项目不仅可以丰富目前披露监管领域的有限研究，也有助于投资者更好地评估公司薪酬激励的有效性和投资于该公司的风险。我们的研究对监管机构也有重要启示，作为国际金融中心的香港也可以得到借鉴。

17503022.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503022.value: 燃烧化石燃料会排放出大量的碳和空气污染物。前者是改变气候的全球外部性，而后者则是主要影响附近居民的局部外部性。为了将这些外部性内部化，世界各地的政策制定者已经设计了各类工具来改善当地的空气质量和缓解全球气候变化。然而，虽然这两套政策在许多国家都存在，但它们通常是分开的，往往由不同的当局管理，并且没有考虑空气污染和碳排放之间的相互关系。例如，气候政策通常只关注碳减排，几乎不考虑其对空气质量的影响，反之亦然。 在拟议的研究中，我们研究了在考虑到碳排放和空气污染之间的相互关系后，分析用于缓解气候变化的碳交易系统将如何影响社会福利。我们把重点放在中国，因为中国是世界上最大的碳和许多其他污染物的排放者。同时，中国的许多政策举措仍处于试验阶段，因此，拟议的研究将具有直接的政策影响。 我们假设，如果碳的边际减排成本高的地区比较富裕，人口密度大，那么允许他们从比较贫穷和人口密度小的地区购买碳排放许可证，将使比较富裕和人口密度大的地区的空气质量恶化（假设没有为控制空气污染做出额外努力）。这将导致一个意想不到的健康成本，抵消了碳交易带来的潜在利益。因此，根据健康成本的大小，引入国家碳交易体系可能会也可能不会改善社会福利。 为了说明这一观点，我们将分五个步骤进行拟议的研究。首先，我们将建立一个理论框架，以了解如何同时对这两类外部性进行最佳监管。值得注意的是，我们将分析碳交易在考虑到其对空气污染的外部性之后，将如何影响社会福利。第二，我们将收集中国的能源消耗、二氧化碳排放、生产投入和产出的数据，这些数据将被用来估计中国不同地区的碳边际减排成本。第三，我们将根据估计的各地区边际减排成本来模拟碳交易。第四，我们将估计碳交易在不同地区造成的空气污染的变化，并计算污染分布造成的潜在健康成本（或效益）。最后，我们将讨论我们的研究结果的含义并提供政策建议。 拟议的研究将在两个重要方面对文献作出贡献。首先，我们将提供一个理论基础，以了解如何监管具有不同范围的相互关联的外部性。第二，我们将强调全国碳市场的一个关键局限，这与所有已经建立或计划建立碳市场的国家有关。

17503022.label: Realisation of objectives
17503022.value: This project set out to address four ambitious objectives, all of which have been comprehensively realized. First, we assembled a unique and extensive dataset covering 30 Chinese provinces from 2000 to 2021. This dataset includes detailed information on energy consumption, CO₂ emissions, production inputs such as capital and labor, and economic outputs including industrial output and GDP. Air quality data, covering pollutants like PM2.5, SO₂, and NOₓ, were collected from over 1,600 monitoring stations and augmented with satellite data where necessary to ensure completeness and consistency across provinces and years. The second objective was to estimate the marginal abatement cost (MAC) of carbon for each province. Using the Directional Distance Function (DDF) approach, which is widely recognized in the literature for its robustness in modeling productivity under environmental constraints, we constructed province-specific MAC curves. Our findings reveal significant heterogeneity across different provinces. We further quantified the uncertainty in these estimates using an extensive bootstrapping procedure, providing confidence intervals for policy applications. Third, we simulated carbon trading across provinces using both theoretical and empirical models. The analysis demonstrates that a national carbon market reduces expected welfare losses compared to a purely planned allocation of abatement targets, but also highlights the limitations of market mechanisms in the presence of heterogeneous local externalities. Through a series of simulations, we showed that hybrid schemes—combining planning for provinces where information is relatively complete with market mechanisms for others—can substantially improve welfare outcomes. For example, a hybrid scheme with ten provinces under planning and twenty in a market reduces welfare losses by over 60% compared to a national market alone. Finally, we addressed the redistribution of air pollution and associated health impacts resulting from carbon trading. By estimating the elasticity between CO₂ emissions and air pollutant concentrations, we found that a 1% increase in CO₂ emissions leads to a 0.36% increase in PM2.5 levels. Monetizing the health impacts using the value of statistical life (VSL) approach, we estimate that each additional million tons of CO₂ emissions results in an average of 75.75 premature deaths and $60.73 million in health-related costs per province annually. These results provide the first province-level, monetized assessment of the health costs and benefits associated with carbon abatement and pollution redistribution in China. No objectives remain unfulfilled, and the project has generated a comprehensive empirical foundation for policy analysis and future research.

17503022.label: Major findings and research outcome
17503022.value: This research delivers several key findings with direct implications for climate policy in China and beyond. We demonstrate that while a national carbon market is more efficient than a purely planned approach—reducing expected welfare losses from $28.65 billion to $18.55 billion per year—it does not fully address the problem of heterogeneous local externalities. In other words, market-based trading can inadvertently shift pollution from less populated to more densely populated provinces, resulting in significant health costs. Our analysis shows that the welfare loss from ignoring information asymmetry (as in planning) is generally greater than the loss from ignoring externality heterogeneity (as in markets), but both are substantial. The optimal policy, therefore, is not an exclusive reliance on either market or planning, but a carefully designed hybrid. By assigning provinces with well-understood abatement costs to a planning regime and grouping others into regional carbon markets based on the magnitude of their pollution externalities, welfare losses can be reduced by up to 63% compared to a national market. This hybrid approach provides a practical blueprint for reconciling economic efficiency with public health protection. The project also produces the first comprehensive mapping of marginal abatement costs and local pollution externalities at the provincial level in China. These results reveal that provinces with complex industrial structures and higher levels of corruption tend to have greater information asymmetry, while provinces with larger populations face higher local externalities from carbon emissions. The strong empirical link between CO₂ emissions and air pollution further underscores the need for integrated policy design. Overall, our findings offer robust, data-driven guidance for the ongoing expansion of China’s carbon market and for similar policy debates in other large, heterogeneous economies.

17503022.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17503022.value: Building on the foundation established in this project, several avenues for further research are immediately apparent. First, future work should incorporate dynamic models of firm and population mobility, as the current analysis assumes static provincial boundaries and immobile firms. This extension would provide a more nuanced understanding of the long-term impacts of carbon trading and planning schemes. Second, the methodology can be refined by applying machine learning techniques to estimate marginal abatement costs, potentially reducing prediction error and capturing non-linearities in the data. Sectoral analyses, particularly in industries such as power generation and cement, would also enhance the policy relevance of the findings as China’s national Emissions Trading System (ETS) expands. Finally, the hybrid policy framework developed here should be piloted to test its effectiveness in real-world settings. There is also scope to adapt the model for application in other countries or regions, including Southeast Asia, where cross-border pollution and data heterogeneity present similar challenges.

17503022.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17503022.value: This project explored the best way for China to reduce carbon emissions by comparing two main strategies: a national carbon trading market, where provinces can buy and sell the right to emit, and a government-led plan that sets strict limits for each province. We found that while carbon trading is generally more cost-effective, it can unintentionally shift pollution to provinces with more people, causing greater health risks. To solve this, we propose a mixed approach: let provinces where the government has good information follow a planned system, and group the others into regional markets based on how much pollution affects local health. This hybrid solution saves more money and better protects people’s health than either strategy alone. Our research provides the first detailed map of carbon abatement costs and pollution impacts for all Chinese provinces, giving policymakers the tools they need to design smarter climate policies. These findings help China move closer to its goal of becoming carbon neutral by 2060, while minimizing the hidden costs of pollution for its citizens.

17503122.label: Project Objectives
17503122.value: Enriching the literature on the role of sleepiness in consumer behavior: Much research has been done to uncover the impacts of sleepiness on our physical and mental health and their implications for organizational behavior. However, scant research exists on how sleepiness influences consumer behavior. This research investigates how and why sleepiness affects consumers’ price sensitivity, which will add to our understanding of the role of sleepiness in consumer behavior. At a higher level, this research also sheds light on the emerging line of research on how consumer behavior is affected by physiologically-related factors. Contributing to the literature on price sensitivity: The existing literature has yielded rich insights about how price sensitivity is affected by various components of a marketing program and consumers’ psychological states. In this research, we test how a physiologically-related factor that is commonly experienced by consumers, sleepiness, might also influence price sensitivity in a counterintuitive way. Testing the mechanism by which sleepiness affects price sensitivity: We predict that sleepiness increases price sensitivity because sleepy consumers are more attentive to negative information and price is often considered as a negative attribute in product evaluation. Such a prediction receives preliminary support from the exploratory studies, but the planned studies will test this mechanism in a more systematic manner using not only mediation analysis but also examination of moderators that are closely related to this process. Uncovering boundary conditions of the effect: Testing the moderations related to the proposed process will also reveal boundary conditions of the effect. For example, we predict that if the proposed mechanism indeed holds, then the effect of sleepiness on price sensitivity will be weakened when consumers are led to have a more positive mood, when they are choosing among hedonic rather than utilitarian products, and when the price-quality heuristic is made salient. Offering practical implications: In this research, we will examine the impacts of sleepiness by not only directly measuring sleepiness but also using various well-established proxies of sleepiness, such as sunset time and time of day. The results generated in these studies will thus offer implications for marketing practitioners to better estimate consumers’ price sensitivity, taking into consideration those factors that may affect consumers’ sleepiness.

17503122.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503122.value: Sleepiness is a frequent experience for many people. Despite our rich understanding of how sleepiness influences health and its implications for organizational behavior, only a limited number of research findings directly shed light on its role in consumer behavior. In this research, we aim to enrich this literature by examining how and why sleepiness affects consumers’ price sensitivity. We propose that sleepiness increases price sensitivity and that such an effect occurs because sleepy consumers pay more attention to negative information and price is often considered to be a negative attribute in product evaluation. Boundary conditions that shed light on this mechanism are also tested. For instance, we predict that the effect of sleepiness on increased price sensitivity will be lessened when consumers are led to experience a more positive mood, when they are choosing among hedonic rather than utilitarian products, and when the price-quality heuristic is made salient. The effects will be examined using mixed methods, including lab and online experiments, as well as analysis of a large secondary dataset. The findings will also offer important theoretical and practical implications. They will enrich our understanding of the role of sleepiness in consumer behavior and uncover how price sensitivity might be influenced by a physiologically-related factor, sleepiness, which is commonly experienced by consumers. Marketing practitioners can draw on the findings generated in this research to better estimate consumers’ price sensitivity by taking into account various factors that may affect people’s sleepiness, such as sunset time, time of day, and the changeover to daylight saving time. 人們日常經常體驗到困倦感。雖然目前已經有不少研究發現困倦感如何影響我們的健康和組織行為，但是我們對於困倦感如何影響消費者行為的認知卻十分有限。本項目旨在研究困倦感如何影響消費者的價格敏感度。我們預測困倦感會增加價格敏感度。我們判斷這一效應的發生是由於困倦的消費者更容易留意到負面信息，而價格信息通常在產品評估的過程當中會被視為負面信息。

17503222.label: Project Objectives
17503222.value: We propose a sentiment-based view on examining investment returns of cryptocurrencies. Cryptocurrency sentiment refers to the emotions and opinions expressed in cryptocurrency-related texts. We use a proprietary set of 54 sentiment scores, retrieved by a natural language processing engine from global media outlets, including press, blogs, forums, and social media, to construct our sentiment measures. Probing into potential underlying mechanisms by using exogenous sentiment shocks that affect user growth and testing if such effect, in turn, contrasts or reinforces the user base feedback effect that underpins blockchain network theories. Employing three common machine learning methods, i.e., gradient boosted regression trees, random forest, and neural networks, to improve the measurement of the sentiment premium in the cryptocurrency market. These methods deliver more accurate sentiment-based strategy returns predictions than traditional linear regression models commonly used in the asset pricing literature.

17503222.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503222.value: Merriam-Webster (2021), one prominent English dictionary, describes cryptocurrencies as “any form of currency that only exists digitally, that usually has no central issuing or regulating authority but instead uses a decentralized system to record transactions and manage the issuance of new units, and that relies on cryptography to prevent counterfeiting and fraudulent transactions.” In this study, we propose a sentiment-based view on examining investment returns of cryptocurrencies. Cryptocurrency sentiment refers to the emotions and opinions expressed in cryptocurrency-related texts. We use a proprietary set of 54 sentiment scores, retrieved by a natural language processing engine from global media outlets, including press, blogs, forums, and social media, to construct our sentiment measures. We investigate whether sentiment-based strategies, especially from social media, generate economically sizable and statistically significant returns, which are not explained by the emerging factor models in the cryptocurrency market. Probing into potential underlying mechanisms, we explore whether exogenous sentiment shocks affect user growth and if such effect, in turn, contrasts or reinforces the user base feedback effect that underpins blockchain network theories. Blockchain network theories broadly suggest that user network growth positively reinforces itself as existing users are motivated to promote the network and benefit from its growth. We investigate the role of sentiment in the flywheel of user growth and examine if sentiment affects cryptocurrency returns via the channel of user growth. To improve the measurement of the sentiment premium in the cryptocurrency market, we employ three common machine learning methods: gradient boosted regression trees, random forest, and neural networks. These methods deliver more accurate sentiment-based strategy returns predictions than traditional linear regression models commonly used in the asset pricing literature. In particular, these machine learning methods allow us to capture the complicated dependence between different sentiments, which sheds more light on our understanding of how various sentiments affect the cryptocurrency market. Overall, our project aims to provide the first evidence on the nexus between cryptocurrency markets, machine learning methods, and behavioral finance insights. 著名的韋氏詞典將加密貨幣描述為 “任何只以數位形式存在的貨幣，特性是通常沒有中央發行或監管機構，而是使用一個分散的系統來記錄交易和管理新貨幣的發行，並依靠密碼學來防止偽造和欺詐性交易。”在這項研究中，我們從市場情緒的觀點出發來研究加密貨幣的投資收益。加密貨幣情緒指的是加密貨幣相關文本中，所表達的情緒和意見。為了構建我們的加密貨幣情緒指標，我們使用一套由自然語言處理引擎，從全球各類媒體（包括新聞、博客、論壇和社交媒體）中檢索分析出來的54個情緒分數。我們特別關注來自社交媒體的文本分析指標，是否產生了經濟上可觀的、統計上顯著的回報，而這些回報是加密貨幣市場上已經的因素模型所不能解釋的。 在探究潛在經濟機制時，我們將探討外生的情緒沖擊是否影響用戶增長，以及這種影響是否反過來影響區塊鏈網絡理論中的用戶基礎反饋效應。區塊鏈網絡理論一般認為，用戶網絡的增長會積極地自我加強，因為現有的用戶被激勵去推廣網絡並從其增長中受益。我們研究情緒在用戶增長的飛輪中的作用，並考察情緒是否通過用戶增長的渠道影響加密貨幣的回報。 為了改善對加密貨幣市場的情緒溢價的測量，我們采用了三種常見的機器學習方法：梯度提升回歸樹、隨機森林和神經網絡。與資產定價文獻中常用的傳統線性回歸模型相比，這些方法能提供更準確的基於情緒的策略收益預測。特別是，這些機器學習方法使我們能夠捕捉到不同情緒之間的複雜的相互依賴性，這為我們了解各種情緒如何影響加密貨幣市場提供了更多的啟示。總的來說，我們的項目旨在提供關於加密貨幣市場、機器學習方法和行為金融見解之間關系的新證據。

17503722.label: Project Objectives
17503722.value: We will conduct an extensive review of the prior and concurrent research that is related to our project. These include the literature of corporate finance and environmental economics with a particular focus on carbon emission and green investment. It will help us understand the theoretical background of the topic of interest as well as the existing empirical evidence. Based on the literature, we will conduct a series of revisions on our current model that captures the key points of the research. We will carefully study the meaning and computation of each variable in the prior and concurrent literature. In addition to the data that we have already collected, we will use other datasets to refine and complete carbon emission and green investment data. We will conduct an intensive structural estimation based on the model. We will modify the model if the estimated parameters have larger-than-expected standard errors or when the differences between the model moments and data moments are too large. After estimating the parameters, we will conduct impulse response analyses as well as counterfactual analyses to further understand the mechanism of green investment and carbon emission as well as their relationship with other firm behaviors such as capital investment and cash holding. We will write a paper to clearly report our model and estimation results, and present it at conferences and research institutions.
