To investigate the diverse waste management methods that have been implemented and refined by local communities in Hong Kong’s Big Northwest.

To develop an integrated framework for sustainable waste management that harnesses social mobilisation in the form of a community economy for food waste, so as to develop a more sustainable relationship between humans and waste in a rural-urban nexus of Hong Kong.

23602622.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23602622.value: The amount of food waste generated daily in Hong Kong greatly exceeds that of other densely populated cities, reaching 44% of the city’s total municipal solid waste since 2011. Meanwhile, disposal at landfills, as the main solution of waste treatment, is expected to reach saturation point by the 2030s. The longstanding problem of food waste is now posing a threat to the public health of the city, and becoming an environmental crisis. Although the environmental authorities of Hong Kong have mandated various attempts to reduce food waste, as of 2021, the results of these mandates remain far lower than initial expectations, due to the lack of social mobilisation. A practical and integrated approach to recycling Hong Kong’s enormous amount of daily putrescible waste is urgently needed. This project aims to shift societal attention towards some alternative models for waste management that are currently operating in the Northwest area of Hong Kong’s New Territories. The project focuses on the area known colloquially as the “Big Northwest,” where farming activities continue despite rapid urbanisation. In this area, diverse, tailor-made recycling practices are adopted to turn food waste into eco-friendly products or fertilisers. These practices are collectively instituted and maintained by residents and farmers who live around the area’s light rail loop. Such recycling practices not only address the issue of food waste but also connect rural and urban communities. This project proposes to explore the emerging and diverse community-based practices for recycling food waste along the light rail loop in the Big Northwest area in order to develop a solution to the problem of food waste in Hong Kong. The project also introduces and develops the concept waste commons, the idea of a shared ownership or responsibility for waste. The framework for studying the material and spatial characteristics of recycling food waste takes into account the need to maintain sustainable urban life, and fosters negotiation between diverse actors. Therefore, the project applies the method of participatory action research (PAR) to question how the practices of recycling food waste can construct multiple routes for metabolic connections between humans and land, producers and consumers, and rural and urban communities. It aims to ultimately develop an integrated framework for sustainable waste management that harnesses social mobilisation in the form of a community economy for food waste, so as to develop a more sustainable relationship between humans and waste in a rural-urban nexus of Hong Kong. 自2011年，香港每日生產的廚餘已超越其他擁有近似人口密度同的城市，佔了整個城市的固體垃圾總額的百十之四十四；這些廚餘的主要處理方式是堆填，而香港的堆填區預計在2030年間抵達飽和。廚餘，這個存在已久的課題現正危及本港的公共衛生並成為環境危機。雖然香港環保政策已試過許多方法來減少廚餘，由於缺乏社會動員，迄今，許多嘗試仍未收到相對應的回應。香港確實迫切需要實際又能整合的方法來回收每日產生的大量易腐垃圾。本計劃欲將在香港新界「大西北」社區處理廢棄物的替代性模式轉介給社會大眾，此地的在快速的都市化下仍保有農業活力。因此，在此區域有不少客製化的回收實踐將廚餘轉化為環境友善的產品或肥料，即「轉廢為寶」。這些實踐是由輕鐵沿線的居民與當地農夫制定與維持，這些回收實踐不僅回應了減廢問題也連結了城鄉發展。 以「大西北」地區輕軌沿線社區為本發展出了不同的的廚餘回收實踐，本計畫將研究這些實踐並探究處理香港廚餘問題的方法，同時，也引介與發展一個分享廢物的所有權與責任心的「餘之共」(waste commons)的概念。將回收廚餘的物質與空間特性納入本研究的框架去考量維持永續性的都市生活所需，並鼓勵不同行動者之間的協商關係。因此，本計畫使用參與式行動研究為方法探問回收廚餘是如何為人類與土地、生產者與消費者、城鄉社區之間的代謝連結打造多重的路徑，本計畫最終的目的要發展出一個具整合性的框架，在此框架中的永續廢物管理會以社區經濟的樣貌動員社會，並在香港的城鄉樞紐處發展出人類與垃圾間更持續的關係。

23602722.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23602722.value: 香港移民決策與轉化中的代際照顧關係：比較和代際研究方法

23602722.label: Project Objectives
23602722.value: Hong Kong is believed to be experiencing a new wave of migration. This study aims to explore how adult children and ageing parents in Hong Kong make migration decisions in the pre-migration context. To contribute to the ongoing intellectual debate about the changing intergenerational contract by collecting empirical data to investigate how migration decision-making shapes and is shaped by intergenerational care relations. To develop a multi-dimensional conceptual framework for examining how adult children and ageing parents make migration decisions based on considerations of intergenerational care. To achieve a more comprehensive and robust understanding of the dynamic relationship between migration decision-making and intergenerational care by comparing the migration decision-making of both the movers (those who plan to migrate) and the stayers (those who plan to stay). To examine whether and how adult children involve their ageing parents in making migration decisions, whether there are discrepancies between the migration views and care expectations of the generations, and how they manage such discrepancies by conducting in-depth interviews with adult children and ageing parents from the same family. To capture how older and younger generations envisage the present and future care arrangements for the ageing parents by using an innovative mix of qualitative in-depth interviews and the visual method of care mapping. By developing a protocol for using the visual technique of care mapping to generate multi-dimensional data on older people’s care networks, this study aims to make methodological contributions to qualitative research and ageing and care studies. To make suggestions for social and migration policies as well as family and elderly service provision, so that ageing parents and adult children can be better supported to maintain intergenerational care relations locally and transnationally.

23602722.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23602722.value: International migration has become a ubiquitous phenomenon. Not only does it affect people who are migrating, it also affects their family members, especially ageing parents. Since a migration decision will affect the extent to which ageing parents and their adult children can provide and receive care, migration decision-making between the generations is critical for the wellbeing of ageing parents. While some adult children migrate without involving and arranging care for their ageing parents, others may decide to stay or migrate with their ageing parents, given considerations of intergenerational care. In this regard, migration and intergenerational care are intimately linked. Across Asia, there has been an increasing concern that social changes such as migration may lead to a weakening of the intergenerational contract, thus hampering elderly support and security. Against this background, migration decision-making within the intergenerational care context becomes an important social and research topic. In migration scholarship, growing attention has been paid to how migrants have readjusted care practices in the post-migration context. However, few have scrutinized how older and younger generations negotiate migration decisions and make intergenerational care plans in the pre-migration context. In particular, very few studies have examined the views of both generations side by side. Questions as to whether and how adult children involve their ageing parents in making migration decisions, whether there are discrepancies between the views of the generations, and how they manage such discrepancies remain understudied. To fill these gaps, this study aims to examine the migration decision-making process between ageing parents and adult children in Hong Kong from four aspects: consensus or discrepancies in care expectations, intergenerational intimacy, resources and constraints, and power dynamics. It adopts a comparative and intergenerational approach to examine the intergenerational migration decision-making process of the following three groups: (1) both adult children and ageing parents moving, (2) moving adult children with staying parents, and (3) both adult children and ageing parents staying (90 respondents in total). An innovative mix of qualitative in-depth interviews and visual care mapping will be used. Theoretically, this study will contribute to the ongoing intellectual debate about the changing intergenerational contract and shed light on the dynamic relationship between migration and intergenerational care. Methodologically, it will illustrate how care mapping is a useful tool for generating multi-dimensional data on older people for data triangulation. The findings will also inform social and migration policies and elderly service provision in both migrant-sending and receiving societies. 國際移民已成為一種普遍現象。移民不僅影響移民本人，也會影響到其家人，尤其是年長父母。由於移民決定將影響年長父母及其成年子女可提供和接受照顧的程度，代際之間的移民決策對年長父母的福祉至關重要。雖然有成年子女在未曾讓年長父母參與移民決策和未有作出照顧父母安排的情況下移居外地，但亦有部分人考慮到其年長父母的照顧需要決而定留下。由此可見，移民和代際照顧息息相關。亞洲各地越來越關注社會轉變因素，例如遷移等，會否減低代際契約的重要性，繼而影響長者獲得的支援和保障。在此背景下，代際之間如何作出移民決策成為一個重要的社會和研究課題。 在與移民相關的學術文獻中，越來越多研究關注移民人士如何在遷移後調整其履行照顧責任的模式。然而，過往研究少有探討老一代和年輕一代如何在移民前協商移民決定和制定代際照顧計劃；同時了解兩代觀點的研究則更少。因此，有關成年子女如何將年長父母納入移民決策商議過程，兩代之間是否存在觀點差異，以及他們如何處理這些差異仍有待探討。 為了填補這些理解上的不足，本研究旨在從代際照顧期望的共識或差異、代際關係、資源與局限，以及代際權力關係四方面，探討香港年長父母與成年子女之間的移民決策過程。本研究採用比較和代際研究方法，以合併質性深度訪談和視覺照顧圖的創新組合方式，探討以下三類人士的代際移民決策過程：(1)兩代共同遷移者，(2)成年移民子女與留港父母，以及 (3)兩代共同留港者(合共 90 名受訪者)。 從理論層面而言，此研究有助推進有關代際契約轉變的學術辯論，並闡明移民和代際照顧之間的動態關係。於研究方法層面而言，此研究將說明視覺照顧圖作為一種質性研究工具，能如何就有關長者的議題產生多維度數據，以作研究數據多重檢核之用。研究結果亦能促進移民輸出社會和移民接收社會於社會、移民以及長者服務等方面的政策建議。

23602922.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23602922.value: This proposed project seeks to develop a theoretical understanding of the relation between corporate arrangements and epistemic injustice. Epistemic injustice is defined as injustice that happens at the cognitive and social level. According to an influential conceptualization of epistemic injustice, there are two types of epistemic injustice: one is a person being perceived as less credible simply because of the social prejudice against his/her identity (e.g., a racial minority not being trusted by others simply because of the social bias towards his/her racial identity); the other is a gap in collective interpretative resources, resulting in the inability of certain groups or members in a society being unable to make sense of their experience (e.g., women had difficulties in making sense of workplace sexual harassment before the concept of sexual harassment was invented by a group of feminists to capture such experience). There are three main objectives of the study. First, it aims to develop an epistemic theory of the corporation. Despite the growing literature in (a) epistemic injustice, (b) workplace justice, and (c) political theory of the corporation, an explicit theory which articulates the relationship between the three is largely absent. The proposed study aims to fill this gap in the literature. Second, the study aims to intervene debates concerning workplace justice through the lens of epistemic injustice. Specifically, the study evaluates, from an epistemic point of view, debates between advocates of the institutionalization of the rights of contestation (e.g., workplace republicanism as exemplified in the German co-determination model) and advocates of the democratization of the workplace (e.g., workplace democracy in democratic firms such as Mondragon). Empirical cases in the German co-determination model, the bi-cameralism model, and the employee-ownership model, as well as practical examples of democratic firms in Spain, will be examined. Third, the study aims to extend the epistemic injustice literature to evaluating external corporate behaviors, with a particular focus on corporate outsourcing to the global south. Generally, the request for disclosing information and transferring knowledge of production cannot easily travel beyond the legal boundaries of companies. Thus, workers in the global south who actually work for parent companies in the global north, and yet are not formally recognized as employees of the same companies due to outsourcing, constitutes an important sphere for unjust epistemic relationships. 本研究計劃旨在發展一套理論以建構公司安排與知性不公義之間的關係。知性不公義在認知與社會關係層面中存在。根據一個相當具影響力的對知性不公義的概念化，知性不公義可以分為兩種：一種是當一個人僅因其身份上的社會偏見而被認為是較不可信（例如當一個少數族裔因其種族身份而不被相信）；另一種是指當在整體詮釋資源中存在著某些缺口而導致一些社會上的群體或成員無法有效地理解自己的經歷（例如在性騷擾這一概念被一群女性主義者發明並普及前，女性在職場上遇見類近行為或會無法很好地理解這種行為的問題所在）。本研究計劃有三個目標。首先，本研究旨在發展一個公司與認知的理論。儘管近年(1)知性不公義、(2)工作場所的正義理論、(3)公司的政治理論這三組文獻各自都有可觀的發展，卻沒有一個明確的理論將三組文獻的關係梳理。本研究旨在填補這一文獻上的缺口。其次，本研究旨在以知性不公義的角度介入現存工作場域公義的辯論。具體而言，本研究將從知性不公義的角度去審視工作場域辯論的兩個主要派別的辯論：亦即工作場域問責與反對權利的提倡者(如德國的公司共同治理制度)和工作場域民主化提倡者(如西班牙的蒙德拉貢模式)。本研究將研判有關德國的公司共同治理經驗、公司的兩院制、僱員擁有制，以及具體有關以民主模式治理的公司等等的相關實證研究的個案。再者，本研究旨在將知性不公義的文獻拓展至公司的外在行為，並聚焦於公司對全球南方的商業外判行為。一般而言，全球南方的工人在外判的工作關係中，即便他們是為處於全球北方的企業進行實際的工作，全球南方的工人卻很難向全球北方的企業要求透露相關生產與企業安排的資訊及知識，但這卻構成了一個重要的知性不公義的場域。

23603722.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23603722.value: Approaches to preservation and re-enactment of performance art have received much attention in museums and academia recently. Since the 2000s, Tate Modern and The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) have hired curators and researchers devoted to commissioning, documenting, preserving, and re-enacting performance art. Conferences and publications on liveness in Euroamerica have also proliferated. However, there is little research regarding those issues in Asian contexts. The main obstacle for performance art research in Asia is the lack of data and critical analysis of discourses generated in local contexts. This project seeks to fill such gaps. Since the 1990s, live art festivals experimenting with performance art have been a crucial platform across Asia, with the region experiencing another shift due to COVID-19. This project explores the collaboration and new aesthetics in live art practices through transregional exchange, and assesses the aesthetics that have shaped certain international styles, including indigenous philosophies, Asian rituals, and postcolonial conditions. The project will also contribute to the intersecting fields of contemporary art, performance art studies, and postcolonial studies in Asia. Here, “performance art” or “live art” refers to those created beyond theatrical narratives and staged situations in conventional art spaces, and often demands participants’ engagement at different levels. The research aims at expanding the current scholarly work on performance art history through predominately case studies in Euroamerica, as they are much better documented. Evaluating archives primarily in three locations: Beijing, Jogja, and Cologne, I will focus on three aspects: ritual, participation, and liveness. Two major tasks are envisioned: first, to acquire more comprehensive understanding of transnational live art histories as a result of interactions between artists from Europe and Asia. This will lay the foundation of a monograph exploring the live art networks. Second, to identify and compare available sources of various archives and develop approaches of curating and repairing documentation. The project continues from the PI’s 2019–2020 research project, funded by a Faculty Research Grant, to map out the communities of performance art in Hong Kong, Shanghai, and Beijing; particularly, the methods of documentation, intermedia, and audience engagement. The PI hopes to get more support to expand and publish the research. Proposed end-user engagement and impact include new understandings of how artistic exchanges impact performance art in postcolonial states, particularly in the Asia-Pacific context, which will benefit curatorial engagement and museum practice under transnational exchange. 自1990年代以來，各種國際現場藝術節一直是亞洲藝術交流的一個重要平台，而行為藝術的保存及重新表演的方法最近受到博物館和學術界的關注。然而，這些問題在亞洲背景下的研究很少，主要障礙是亞洲行為藝術研究缺乏第一手材料和理論的建立與分析。本計畫旨在填補這些空白，探討跨區域的交流在現場藝術實踐中所碰撞出的新美學，包括本土性、亞洲儀式和後殖民狀態。

23605322.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23605322.value: Perhaps the central aspect of our psychology is our sense of self, or our felt awareness of ourselves as a distinct and enduring subject or 'I'. This sense of self pervades our everyday experience. It ties our memories, imaginings, perceptions, emotions, sensations, and thoughts together as those that feel like they belong to a single subject. Due to its importance, the sense of self has received significant attention from both philosophers and scientists. Yet, despite this activity, the nature of the sense of self remains poorly understood. The chief difficulty in understanding the sense of self is that, unlike experiences of, say, color or fear, it lies at the periphery of our consciousness. As a result, it resists introspective access and requires a more indirect method of investigation. My aim in this project is to improve our understanding of the sense of self by overcoming this methodological hurdle using interdisciplinary methods, in particular, applying scientific research to philosophical questions. The strategy I use to develop a new account of the sense of self is undertaking a systematic review of disorders of the sense of self, or psychiatric and neurological conditions in which the sense of self is disrupted. These disorders constitute our richest source of data about the function of the sense of self. I first provide an analysis of what is going on with these disorders, which I then leverage into a novel account of the sense of self. On the view I develop, our sense of self primarily consists in a feeling of self-concern, or a distinctive type of affective engagement with states of our own mind and body. I then use this account to resolve a deep and recalcitrant puzzle raised by disorders of the sense of self, namely that subjects with these conditions seem to simultaneously have and lack a sense of self. 也許我們心理學的核心方面是我們的自我意識，或者我們對 我們自己是一個獨特而持久的主體或“我”。這種自我意識瀰漫在我們的 日常經驗。它把我們的記憶、想像、知覺、情感、感覺、 和想法在一起，因為那些感覺它們屬於一個主題。由於其 重要性，自我意識受到了兩位哲學家的極大關注 和科學家。然而，儘管有這種活動，自我意識的本質仍然很差 明白了。理解自我意識的主要困難在於，不像 例如，顏色或恐懼的體驗，它位於我們意識的外圍。因此， 它抵制內省訪問，需要更間接的調查方法。 我在這個項目中的目標是通過以下方式提高我們對自我意識的理解 使用跨學科方法克服這一方法障礙，特別是， 將科學研究應用於哲學問題。我用來開發的策略 對自我意識的新解釋正在對 自我意識，或自我意識受到影響的精神和神經疾病 打亂了。這些疾病構成了我們最豐富的關於神經系統功能的數據來源 自我感覺。我首先對這些疾病的情況進行分析，我 然後利用對自我意識的新穎描述。根據我發展的觀點，我們的感覺 自我的主要存在於一種自我關注的感覺，或一種獨特的情感類型 參與我們自己的身心狀態。然後我使用這個帳戶來解決一個 由自我意識障礙引發的深刻而頑固的謎題，即具有這些條件的受試者似乎同時擁有和缺乏自我意識。

23605322.label: Realisation of objectives
23605322.value: Objective 1: To produce at least two research papers to be submitted to top 10 academic philosophy journals. I have completed this objective. As of 26 Mar, 2024 (the date I am writing this), I have produced two research papers and submitted them to consensus 'top 10' journals in analytic philosophy (according to the field-standard 'Leiter Reports' journal rankings). One of these papers, 'Against the Pathology Argument for Self-Aquaintance' has been published open-access in the *Australasian Journal of Philosophy*, a 4* journal in our departmental rankings and a consensus 'top-10' journal in the field. The other paper, 'Depersonalization and the Immediacy of Affect', has recently been submitted to another top-10 journal, *Philosophers' Imprint* on 17 March, 2024. If the paper should happen to be rejected from that journal, I will promptly send it to another top-10 journal, likely *Philosophical Studies.* Objective 2: To deepen our understanding of the sense of self by developing a novel account of it informed by a thorough investigation of psychiatric and neurological disorders of the sense of self. I have completed this objective. This goal of the project was to deepen our understanding of the 'sense of self', or our basic experiential sense of ourselves as distinct entities, by examining psychiatric and neurological conditions in which it appears to be disrupted. My work in this project has met this goal. Each of the two papers I have written focuses on studying what pathologies of self-awareness can tell us about the nature of our sense of self, or self-awareness. The first paper, 'Against the Pathology Argument for Self-Acquaintance', is primarily negative, in the sense that it argues that we should not understand such disorders as supporting the controversial thesis of 'self-acquaintance', which holds that we have direct and unmediated experiential access to the self. The second paper, 'Depersonalization and the Immediacy of Affect' is 'positive', in the sense that it develops a novel account of self-awareness in terms of the immediacy of affective experience. Objective 3: To contribute to our understanding of the role of affective experience, in particular, self-concern, in grounding our sense of self. I have completed this objective. The second research paper produced in this project, 'Depersonalization and the Immediacy of Affect' is an investigation of the role of affective experience in generating our sense of self, or self-awareness. In it, I examine subjects suffering from depersonalization/derealization disorder, who complain of deficits in self-awareness, up to and including reports that they do not feel as if they exist. I explain such deficits by appealing to a loss in the immediacy of affective experience, or its direct influence on our thought and behavior. Subjects suffering from depersonalization, I argue, lack affective immediacy. Though they still have affective experiences such as pain and pleasure, these experiences do not directly influence their thoughts and behaviors in the normal ways. This fact results in a kind of felt alienation from their own affective experiences, which in turn explains the puzzling symptoms of depersonalization. This account implicates affective immediacy in our feeling of self-concern, or the primitive concern we feel for ourselves. Such self-concern, I argue at the end of 'Depersonalization and the Immediacy of Affect', is explained in terms of the unique affective immediacy that accompanies our experiences of ourselves. Objective 4: To shed light on disorders of the sense of self, particularly the affective deficits involved in them. I have completed this objective. Both of the research papers that I have written in this project shed light on disorders of the sense of self. In particular, the second paper, 'Depersonalization and the Immediacy of Affect', explains depersonalization---a prominent disorder of the sense of self---as consisting in a deficit in affective experience. In that paper, I develop the notion of 'affective immediacy'---the direct way in which our affective experiences motivate thoughts and behaviors---and then posit that depersonalization symptoms are explained in terms of a deficit in affective immediacy. Objective 5: To resolve a puzzle posed by disorders of the sense of self, namely that subjects with these disorders display a mixed set of symptoms, some of which point to a missing sense of self, others of which point to some retained sense of self. I have completed this objective. Both of the research papers produced in this project aim to make sense of the puzzling symptoms of disorders of the sense of self. In particular, towards the end of 'Depersonalization and the Immediacy of Affect' I directly address the most puzzling aspect of disorders of the sense of self, namely subjects' denials of their own existence. In particular, I explain how the affective immediacy deficit account that I originate can resolve this puzzle. Objective 6: To contribute to the project of empirically-informed philosophy of mind by engaging in thoroughly interdisciplinary research, using findings from the cognitive sciences to guide my philosophical theorizing. I have completed this objective. Both of the research papers that I have produced are thoroughly interdisciplinary, bringing in research from philosophy, cognitive science, neuroscience, psychology, and psychiatry in order to address foundational questions about the operation of the mind, and in particular to address questions about self-consciousness and the sense of self. This aspect of my project was greatly enabled by the funded research visit to Professor Hong Yu Wong's research group at the University of Tuebingen, Germany. Completing this project has deepened my understanding of the interconnections between these research areas and has enabled me to further develop myself as an expert in empirically-informed philosophy of mind.

23605322.label: Major findings and research outcome
23605322.value: The major findings of this research project are that (a) attempts to explain the sense of self in terms of primitive notions of self-acquaintance fail; (b) that the experiential deficits implicated in depersonalization/derealization disorder are best explained in terms of a deficit in the immediacy of affect, or affect's direct influence on thought and behavior; (c) and hence that the immediacy of affect is a central component of our ordinary sense of self. These research outcomes are embodied in the two research papers that were written as part of this project: (1) 'Against the Pathology Argument for Self-Acquiantance' which was recently published (2024) in the 4* and top-10 philosophy journal *Australasian Journal of Philosophy.* Further details are provided in Part C. (2) 'Depersonalization and the Immediacy of Affect', which was submitted (17 March 2024), to the 4* and top-10 philosophy journal *Philosophers' Imprint.* It is currently under review at this journal. If it should happen to be rejected, it will be sent to another leading venue, likely *Philosophical Studies.* Further details are provided in Part C. In (1), I address a recent argument ('The Pathology Argument') that purports to establish the thesis of self-acquaintance, or the view that we are directly acquainted with the self in experience. This self-acquaintance view is a direct competitor to my own view. I refute the Pathology Argument and instead suggest that disorders of the sense of self such are best explained in terms of deficits in specific aspects of cognition and phenomenology, including potentially deficits in affective experience. Paper (2) primarily accomplishes (b) and (c). In this paper I develop a novel 'affective immediacy deficit' account of depersonalization/derealization disorder. Subjects with depersonalization complain of a felt detachment from their mind and body as well as the external world. Many say that they no longer feel as if they exist. An adequate explanation of this puzzling condition would shed light on the sense of self, since subjects with this condition have an impaired sense of self. To this end, I articulate the notion of the immediacy of affect---affect's direct influence on our thought and behavior---and argue that a deficit in affective immediacy explains the puzzling symptoms of depersonalization. I conclude that this account locates affective experience at the core of our sense of self and explains our normal capacity for self-concern in terms of affective immediacy.

23605322.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23605322.value: There is great potential for further development of the research ideas developed in this project. I am hopeful that both the concept of the immediacy of affect and the explanation of disorders of the sense of terms of a deficit of the immediacy of affect will prove to be influential ideas in debates about affective experience and self-awareness. Some potential ideas for future exploration include: (1) A paper further exploring the phenomenological and rational role of the immediacy of affect. Affect's immediacy is a novel notion that I developed in this project. The idea derives from Mark Johnston's influential work on the authority of affect, but builds upon it by identifying a specific aspect of affective phenomenology. Affective immediacy, I suspect, plays a key role in many mental processes and deserves further exploration. (2) Papers applying the affective deficit account to other disorders of self-awareness. In 'Depersonalization and the Immediacy of Affect' I primarily apply the immediacy deficit account to one pathology of self-awareness in particular, namely depersonalization/derealization disorder. But I am hopeful that this account can be expanded on to explain a wide variety of disorders of the sense of self, which I hope to accomplish in future work.

23605322.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23605322.value: I have developed a novel account of the sense of self---our experience of ourselves---by studying pathologies of self-awareness such as depersonalization. In these conditions, subjects complain of startling deficits in their sense of self. Depersonalized subjects, for example, report feeling as if they do not exist. These symptoms are puzzling because, in other ways, subjects with these conditions retain some sense of self. For example, a depersonalized subject might say, paradoxically, 'I do not feel as if I exist.' To resolve this puzzle and explain what is going on disorders such as depersonalization, I developed the 'immediacy deficit account' of depersonalization. Affective immediacy is an aspect of ordinary affective---pleasurable or painful---experiences. Typically, affective experiences immediately prompt us to think and act in certain ways. But in depersonalized subjects, I argue, affective immediacy is lost. These subjects are therefore alienated from their own affective experiences, and is this felt alienation which prompts them to say they do not feel as if they exist. The idea is that our sense of self is ordinarily grounded in affect's immediacy. This research is significant both theoretically---in sharpening our understanding of the sense of self---and practically---in helping us understand the nature of these syndromes.

23605922.label: Project Title(Chinese)

23605922.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23605922.value: Since the 21st century, both the Chinese government and mainland Chinese universities have been exerting a massive effort to attract overseas-educated academics to return to reverse the brain drain trend and improve the internationalisation of the Chinese higher education sector. However, researchers have found that these academic returnees are differentiated from their domestic-educated peers and marginalised in their host universities in China for their cross-border-built cultural values and norms. Moreover, this decade's increasing number of policy reforms in the Chinese higher education sector makes the surrounding institutional context even more complicated for academic returnees. In this vein, return migration of academic returnees is no longer a ‘one-shot’ decision of permanent physical return; instead, it is an ongoing consideration of personal and family relocation plans, involving multiple pathways of cultural adaptation and integration such as compromise for survival, constructing a virtual transnational diaspora against marginalisation, and re-mobility as resistance. This proposed study aims to explore, from a longitudinal perspective, the complex and dynamic interactive process between academic returnees and their embedding universities in confronting, negotiating, and reforming the academic culture of the mainland Chinese higher education system and how institutional and individual factors further shape this process. A Bourdieusian lens of cultural capital theory and the segmented assimilation theory are adopted as two theoretical pillars underpinning the inquiry into how academic returnees actively reshape and construct their academic culture in their interactions with the embedding institutions. A longitudinal study with a qualitative research design will be conducted via three rounds of semi-structured individual interviews and a document review. Chinese academic returnees who obtained their PhD degree from overseas universities and currently work as full-time faculty members of well-known universities in five mainland Chinese cities (i.e., Beijing, Shanghai, Hangzhou, Shenzhen, and Guangzhou) within their first eight years of returning will be selected purposefully for this proposed study. In addition, policies related to faculty management, performance valuation, and staff recruitment and promotion will also be collected and reviewed. It is expected that this proposed study could unravel the dynamics and rationales of the ongoing mutual interactions between academic returnees and the Chinese higher education system in their cultural adaptation and integration process. The findings from this proposed study will also provide practical implications for the personnel management system, faculty evaluation and promotion policies, and faculty mobility management in cross-border collaborations for universities in mainland China, Hong Kong universities with cross-border campuses, and beyond. 自21世紀以來，中國政府和中國內地大學一直致力於吸引海外畢業的學術人才歸國以扭轉人才流失趨勢，進而提升中國高等教育領域的國際化水準。然而，研究人員發現，這些海歸學者在學術文化價值觀和學術規範等方面與本土培養的學者存在一定差異，因此在所任職的內地高校可能存在被邊緣化的現象。此外，近十年來中國高等教育體系在國際化影響下進行了多項的政策改革，這使得海歸學者回國後所面臨的制度環境更加複雜化。本項研究旨在採用追蹤研究的方法，探索海歸學術人才與其所嵌入內地高校的學術場域之間的動態互動過程，分析其在應對、協商和改革當下中國內地高校主流學術文化價值觀體系時採取的策略，進而探究中國內地高等教育領域中制度因素和個體因素是如何進一步塑造海歸學者的文化適應過程。

23606122.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23606122.value: Confucianism, a major focus in the field of comparative political philosophy, is widely regarded as a tradition which prizes ethics over politics. In this view, ‘politics’ is not an autonomous realm with independent rules and objectives, instead it is a mere means for materializing Confucian ethical principles. Similar to liberalism, Confucian politics is conventionally considered as an extension of ethics. My research project challenges this established view of Confucianism through retrieving the realist aspects of Confucian politics. Drawing inspiration from political realism’s challenge against liberalism in Western philosophy, my project demonstrates that Confucians do consider politics as an autonomous realm with independent rules and conditions, which requires a realist attitude to navigate successfully. While most contemporary scholars have tried to stay fact-sensitive in their formulation of Confucianism, realism as an explicit paradigm for understanding Confucianism is yet to be explored. Relevant issues such as hegemony, political order, and dirty hands politics have been studied sporadically, but not as a systematic program of realist Confucian political philosophy. My project is the first step towards such a systematic study through exploring three major components in three journal articles. Firstly, I will explore the issue of dirty hands politics in the tradition of Confucianism. One key feature of political moralism as opposed to realism is the primacy of moral principle over realistic concerns. I will investigate Confucianism’s attitude towards dirty hand politics (i.e. taking unethical means for greater common good). I will show that Confucians do take possibility of ‘dirty hands’ seriously and that their determining considerations are realist rather than ethical. Secondly, I will offer a realist reading of Confucian virtues. A moralistic reading usually considers virtues as primarily intrinsically valuable (i.e. one should be virtuous because it is ethically good). I challenge this reading and argue that Confucian virtues, though grounded on moral nature of humanity, are primarily advocated for good governance. This in turn helps revise our understanding of virtue’s role in modern democratic society. Thirdly, building on the first two articles, I will offer a realist account of Confucian leadership in democratic society. Rather than reducing statesmanship to a simple form of ethical leadership, I will explore the complex duty, authority and expectation of Confucian democratic leadership. With a realist account of virtues, I argue that Confucian political virtue of ‘faithfulness’ can help resolving some longstanding tension between the roles of citizens and the leaders in a democratic society. 現代比較政治哲學普遍認為傳統儒家重視「倫理」多於「政治」。此類儒家觀點認為「政治」從屬於「倫理」，本身並無獨立地位。「政治行動」目的只在實踐儒家倫理價值，而不在追求任何獨立「政治目標」或「政治價值」。本研究計劃，旨在反對並修正此類觀點。只要重新審視儒家經典，就會發現「政治現實主義」一直扎根於儒家傳統。正如當代「政治現實主義」反對「自由主義」以倫理壓到政治，本研究亦旨在證明儒家政治哲學同樣視「政治」為一獨立領域 ，「政治領域」有只屬於「政治領域」的考慮、價值和規則。政治上要成功，就必須正視其獨立地位。當代比較政治哲學似乎仍未留意到儒家內的「政治現實主義」傳統。話雖如此， 不少相關議題其實已頗受重視，例如儒家如何處理「政治霸權」、「政治秩序」、「不正手段」（dirty hands politics）等問題，已漸受關注。但這些討論仍未有系統地組成一套「儒家現實政治主義」，而本研究正期望有系統地開始建立此套觀點，要之以三篇學術論文開展。 首篇將重新審視儒家傳統如何看待政治中使用「不正手段」。以倫理壓到政治的做法，又稱「政治道德主義」，其要在視「道德原則」為至上考慮，就連「現實考慮」都不能凌駕其上，而與之背道而馳的，有所謂「不正手段政治」 （dirty hands politics），即主張基於現實需要，政治家有時必須以不正當手段確保重大公眾利益。對此，儒家立場又如何呢? 此篇將旨在證明儒家非常了解並重視「不正手段政治」在現實中可取之處，而儒家最終反對，主要仍是出於現實考量，而非盲目堅持道德原則。 次篇會探討儒家德行與政治現實主義的關係。「政治道德主義」多認為「德行」本身就有價值，追求德行只為成為有德之士。但此篇將提出另類觀點，儒門重德，固出於視德行為本然人性，但政治上重德，主要考量仍是為了良政美治。如是觀之，儒家德行對推動現代民主善治亦當有一番貢獻。 第三篇將以首兩篇為基礎，探討以「政治現實主義」為基調的儒家政治理論將如何理解「領袖」在民主社會中的角色。儒家政治領袖，絕不應被單純視為一種「道德領袖」，反而應細心考慮在民主社會中，政治領袖應如何處理「有效領袖」與「民主限制」的複雜關係。本篇主張以「忠」為本的儒家政治領袖想像，將有助解決民主社會與強勢領袖之間的緊張關係。

23606822.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23606822.value: In everyday life we often criticize reasoning or arguments as being irrelevant. In formal logic, however, which studies arguments in a regimented and symbolized form, finding an adequate theory of relevance has proven challenging. Since the 1970’s, the main approach to theorizing relevance in formal logic was the Anderson-Belnap tradition (named after its pioneers). Nevertheless, this approach has remained a niche topic and Anderson-Belnap systems of relevance logic never gained wide acceptance as alternatives to classical logic. Against this background, several authors have recently proposed new approaches to relevance in formal logic, specifically Makinson, Verdee, and myself. In contrast to much of the work in the Anderson-Belnap tradition, which advocated relevance logic as an alternative to classical logic, these new approaches see relevance as a topic of study within classical logic. This makes these approaches much more widely acceptable, as they do not presuppose a revisionary stance to classical logic. A second advantage is that, at least for Brauer and Verdée and arguably for Makinson, their logical theories of relevance are built on a clear philosophical conception of relevance; by contrast, one of the controversial elements of the Anderson-Belnap tradition was whether there was any clear conception of relevance behind their systems of formal logic. In this project, I will advance our understanding of these novel approaches to the theory of relevance, guided by three main research questions. The first question is what logical properties each of the new accounts of relevance enjoys. Do they have familiar proof-theoretic properties such as cut-admissibility, interpolation, or variable-sharing? The second question is how the three accounts of relevance relate to each other. Does one of them include the others, or do they cross-cut one another? Is there a common core to all three accounts? The third research question is how each of these three accounts of relevance relate to the background of classical logic. How much of classical logic is considered relevant or irrelevant on each account? Is there an independent characterization of the arguments in classical logic that are relevance on each account? 在日常生活中我們不時指責推理或論證不相干。 在形式邏輯中，一門把論證視為是有條理的可符號化的學問，找出一個恰當的相干性理論卻是一項已知的挑戰。自一九七零年代起，安達臣貝爾傳統(以此理論的開拓者們而命名)是形式邏輯中建立相干性理論的主流方法。儘管如此，這個方法卻不是大眾的關注，而安達臣貝爾的相干邏輯系統亦從未如其他古典邏輯的替代一樣受到廣泛的接納。 在此背景下，近來數名作者，尤其是麥金森、華迪和我本人，對形式邏輯中的相干性提出了多個新的方法。與大部分安達臣貝爾傳統中意圖把相干邏輯作為古典邏輯的替代的工作不同，這些新的方法視相干性為一個於古典邏輯中的研究課題。由於這些方法不會預設一個修正古典邏輯的立場，這使它們更廣為接受。這些方法的第二個優勢是它們的相干性邏輯理論是建基於一個清晰的相干性哲學概念。這優勢對布勞爾和華迪的方法而言是無疑的，麥金森的方法也許有此優勢。與之相反，在安達臣貝爾傳統中其中一項有爭議的元素就是不確定是否有任何清晰的相干性概念於它的形式邏輯系統之中。 在三個研究問題的引導下，我將會在此計劃中增進我們對上述那些相干性理論的新方法的認知。第一個問題是有什麼邏輯屬性是每一個新方法各自擁有的。這些新方法有沒有相似的證明理論屬性，例如：切減可採性、插值、變量共享？第二個問題是上述三個新方法如何互相關聯。會否有一種方法含括另一種？它們會否與彼此重疊？這三個方法會否有一共通的基點？第三個問題是這三個新的相干性理論如何與古典邏輯的背景相關聯。對每個新的理論來說，有多少古典邏輯的內容能夠視之與它相關或不相關？對每個新的理論來說，有沒有一個對古典邏輯中的論證的獨立描述是跟它相應的？

23607022.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23607022.value: This project aims to advance an important step towards writing a cultural history of translating, publishing, and reading classical Chinese poetry in the late nineteenth and early twentieth-century English literary world. I will focus on two vital vehicles in which translations of classical Chinese poetry were brought to the readers of the time: 1) the modernist “little magazine”, which was marked by the independence from market concerns enabled by developments in the publishing industry and the emergence of new readerships, and 2) the translation anthology, the chief form in which classical Chinese poetry was introduced to the general reading public. These two vehicles served as the site of convergence for a wide range of intellectual activities related to translation and a dynamic ensemble of writers, translators, and commentators on Chinese culture. I use the term “cultural formation” to describe the complex networks of ideas, discourses, agents, and institutions brought into view by the modernist little magazine and the translation anthology. Returning to these historical sites will challenge our modern-day conceptions about the boundaries and norms of translation. The modernist little magazine and the translation anthology present diverse modes of translating Chinese poetry – sinological translations that emphasize philological competence, indirect translations made by poet-translators who professed strong affinity with the poetic spirit of Cathay despite the lack of direct knowledge of the Chinese language, collaborative translations, imitations, adaptations, and pseudotranslations. The richness and complexity of this landscape of translation require a different analytic framework than the normative principles of correct interpretation and fidelity to the source text. I develop the idea of translational sinography to reconceptualize translation as a process of meaning-making across cultures and, more specifically, as a medium through which knowledge about China is constructed and disseminated. This reconceptualization will restore translation to a wider continuum of kindred modes of rewriting and highlight the mediating and constructive roles of translation in the formation of transcultural knowledge, thus enriching our understanding of what translation can mean and do. Furthermore, I employ a triangulation method of analysis that correlates the discursive, transtextual, and sociological networks of translational sinography, aiming to illustrate how translation constitutes a kind of transcultural heuristics, whereby extended thought experiments on larger cultural questions about language, history, subjectivity, and aesthetic form are carried out. 本項目聚焦現代主義雜誌及翻譯選集，考察中國古典詩歌在十九世紀末至二十世紀初英文世界的翻譯、出版与接受。現代主義雜誌依託出版界的革新，相對獨立於市場、銷量方面的考量。翻譯選集則是中國古典詩歌進入英文世界讀者視域的主要形式。這兩種文化載體既是聯結眾多譯者、作家、批評家的文化生產網絡，亦是有关漢詩英譯各種觀點、話語和模式交匯的場域。將翻譯視作跨文化詮釋和知識生產的媒介，重绘这一紛繁複雜的翻譯圖景，有助于拓寬翻譯的邊界，探究翻譯與其他改寫模式的接續性，並展現當時各類譯者對中國的想象與書寫，以及他們在翻譯/書寫中國的同時所進行的關於語言、歷史、美學形式等論題的思想實驗。

23607022.label: Realisation of objectives
23607022.value: This project examines two vital vehicles for presenting English translations of classical Chinese poetry to early twentieth-century readers – the modernist little magazine and the translation anthology. Its objectives are defined along historical, conceptual, and methodological lines. I have conducted archival research, looking into historical periodicals, editorial and publishing records, and personal papers. The diverse materials in little magazines enable me to examine various modes of translating and rewriting classical Chinese poetry, including translations direct and indirect, imitations, adaptations, pseudotranslations, and chinoiserie poems. I have further examined how these translations and rewritings interact with other texts like reviews, editorial comments, reader correspondence, and promotional materials in the textual ecology of the periodical space. With regard to translation anthologies, I have studied the works of both well-known translators and overlooked figures. By incorporating archival materials and proposing new theoretical perspectives, I try to revise and enrich current understanding about the widely noted anthologies of Herbert Giles, Ezra Pound, and Arthur Waley. I have also tried to recover the voices of figures who, though receiving scanty scholarly attention today, were active interlocutors along better-known translators and played crucial roles in shaping the culture of translating classical Chinese poetry. One of the guiding questions of this project is how Chinese poetry, and the idea of China more generally, are integrated into the transcultural imaginary of literary modernism. My work in this project addresses this question from multiple perspectives. Studying the archives of modernist little magazines and translation anthologies reveals a complex genealogy of Chinese influence in literary modernism, featuring an eclectic ensemble of translators, poets, reviewers, editors, and patrons, and spanning various geographical locations and social spaces. That Chinese poetry became an object of avid interest and poetic experiment for modernist poets is not only the result of the influential works of sinologists; it is also facilitated by developments in turn-of-the-century publishing, notably the proliferation of the little magazines and small presses. They are the dynamic medium for transcultural experiment and present a micro-sociology of modernist innovation. In this project, I have attended to this sociological dimension and considered the interactions between agents in the networks of modernist publishing, the resources of print culture brought into play in promoting particular methods of translation and visions of Chinese poetry, and the travels of these multiple articulations of Chinese poetry across the varied landscape of transatlantic modernist publishing. Furthermore, I examine the little magazines and translation anthologies as discursive spaces for practising divergent modes of translation and constructing transcultural knowledge. I have looked into how translators engage in discussions about the principles, methods, and philosophies of translation, how intertextual connections are created between Chinese poetry and modernist intertexts like vers libre, Imagism, Vorticism, Eastern spiritualism and the occult, and transtextual experimentalism, and how processes of translating and reinventing Chinese poetry are intertwined with various strands of modernism. This project also aims to expand our conceptualization of translation, firstly by setting translation within a wider spectrum of transtextual modes, and secondly by examining the mediating and constructive roles of translation in the formation of knowledge about China. The translation anthologies studied in this project encompass different types of translations, ranging from translations made directly from Chinese texts, indirect (re)translations, and collaborative translations. The modernist little magazines, as noted above, present a diverse transtextual landscape characterized by experimental energy and creative transtextual modes that blur the boundary between translation and original composition and conflate the real and the imaginary. By studying translation anthologies and the little magazines, this project thus opens up and pluralizes the idea of translation. I have considered how translators experiment with various modes of translating and rewriting Chinese poetry, how different methods and principles of translation are formulated and debated, and how the dialogic interplay between these transtextual modes renders the idea of translation fluid and relational, thus offering a historically nuanced account of the multiple meanings and forms of translation, and the manifold cultural work it performs. This project further conceptualizes translation as a medium for constructing and disseminating transcultural knowledge. I have developed the term “translational sinography” to elaborate on how translation participates in the history of “sinographies”, or the discursive archive of images, motifs, themes, and conceptions formed through the West’s history of contact with China. I have examined the ways in which translations and rewritings of Chinese poetry engage with recurrent sinographic tropes – through reiteration, transformation, creative inversion, and via intertextual connections with discursive currents in the target cultural field. These processes of sinographic engagement shed light on how translation contributes to the formation of knowledge about China. The methodological goal of this project is to develop a triangulation method that integrates three dimensions of analysis: the discursive dimension of how translation, as a form of sinography, constructs and disseminates knowledge about China, the transtextual dimension of multiple modes of translating and rewriting Chinese poetry, and the sociological dimension of agents in the field of cultural production. This triangulation method has been employed in conference presentations and articles, where I bring together different sets of materials and experiment with various configurations of the three analytic dimensions. For example, I study the little magazines as multilayered constructs of interlocking spaces: the discursive space where divergent discourses are woven into intertextual networks, the social space of actors, agents, and institutions, and the periodical space, inscribed with particular periodical codes, expanding across pages, issues, and titles, where diverse voices and transtextual modes coexist and interact. This project has contributed to four conference presentations, four articles, and a few ongoing pieces of work. More details are given in the following sections of this report.

23607022.label: Major findings and research outcome
23607022.value: The main findings of this project are detailed in four articles. The first article focuses on Ezra Pound’s Cathay, an anthology of Chinese poetry reworked from the notebooks of Ernest Fenollosa. This article explicates Pound’s methods of reworking the Fenollosa notes and reconstructs the multiple processes of mediation. I develop two analytical concepts: transcultural imitation, which describes the sources and techniques with which Pound signals a certain form of “Chineseness” and mediates the experience of the foreign; and the palimpsest of translation, which delineates the multilayered richness of Cathay by unpacking the diverse sets of intertexts out of which it is woven. The second article discusses Edwardian poet-translators’ anthologies of Chinese poetry. I use the terminological compound of indirect retranslation to illustrate their hybrid transtextual features, showing how, in contradistinction to common conceptions of dependence and deficiency, indirectness can also be characterized by divergence and distinction vis-à-vis the mediating texts/agents. Indirect translation can thus be reconceptualized as the transformative medium for generating new transcultural knowledge in various ways, from the (para)textual means of creating interpretative frameworks and validating translational approaches, to the revision of established ideas about China through the textual particulars of translation, and the relocation to new discursive-sociological fields, whereby translation contributes to cultural change. The third article focuses on translations and rewritings of Chinese poetry in early twentieth-century transatlantic modernist little magazines. Examining a broad spectrum of practices ranging from translations direct and indirect, imitations and the pseudotranslational, to editorial comments, reviews, and promotional materials, I study the formation of sinophilic modernisms in the heterogeneous, dialogic, and densely networked spaces of the little magazines. The fourth article examines reviews, rewritings, and retranslations of Herbert Giles’s works on Chinese literature, focusing on a group of writers and poets who, without sufficient knowledge of Chinese, read Chinese poetry indirectly through Giles’s mediation. Contrary to modern-day criticisms that Giles’s translations are misleadingly ‘domesticating’ and obscures the foreignness of Chinese poetry, this group of readers derive from Giles’s translations an appealing experience of aesthetic difference. Their discovery of Chinese aesthetic alterity brings about a range of readerly, writerly, and translatorly engagement, published in anthologies and little magazines. I illustrate how these engagements turn Giles’s texts into generative nexuses and thereby pluralize the meaning of Chinese poetry and enable various cultural work.

23607022.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23607022.value: I envisage several directions for further development. Firstly, the chronological scope can be expanded, reaching back to the 1870s and extending further into the 1930s. While this project includes discussions of prominent sinologists like Giles and Waley, the emphasis has been placed on poet-translators and indirect modes of translation. Further examination of sinologist-translators and the sinological sphere of translation is therefore necessary. A more in-depth understanding would also require delving deeper into other aspects of the culture of translation, notably publishing and reading. Finally, longer-term research can be directed towards accentuating the diverse transnational currents that shape the translation and reception of Chinese literature. Initial work has begun in exploring these lines of further enquiry, which includes a GRF proposal that aims to offer a holistic view of translating, publishing, and reading Chinese poetry in late Victorian and modernist print culture, a new project that focuses on the reception of sinological translation in the literary periodical press, an article that examines sinological translations and the interaction between the sinological and literary spheres of translation, and another article that discusses practices of comparison in translations and reviews of Chinese literature in the Victorian periodical press.

23607022.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23607022.value: This project looks into various forms of translating classical Chinese poetry in the English literary world during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. It examines two media: modernist little magazine, which was marked by the independence from market concerns and functioned as the vital vehicle for modernist experiment; and the translation anthology, the chief form in which Chinese poetry was introduced to the reading public. They facilitated a rich interplay of ideas among writers, translators, and cultural critics, revealing a spectrum of translation approaches ranging from scholarly efforts to creative rewritings by poets without direct knowledge of Chinese. This project conceptualizes translation as a process of cross-cultural knowledge production that shapes ideas about China. The main findings are set out in several articles: the first focuses on Ezra Pound’s Cathay, unpacking how his reworking of intermediary texts create a composite work of transcultural imitation; the second examines Edwardian poet-translators’ anthologies as indirect retranslations that yield new interpretations of Chinese poetry; the third discusses the emergence of sinophilic modernisms in transatlantic little magazines; and the fourth considers how writers and poets transformed Herbert Giles’s translations into sources of literary experiment through reviewing, rewriting, and retranslation.

23607522.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23607522.value: 從性別角度看非正規住房：交織性不平等與劏房家庭的韌性

23607522.label: Project Objectives
23607522.value: To investigate how SDUs, as a material condition, directly or indirectly shape gender relations within the family and reinforce gender inequality through, for example, the gendered division of labour, family practices and access to domestic and public spaces. To examine how different forms of inequality, arising from factors such as gender, class and migration status, are intertwined with informal housing by analysing the multifaceted marginalisation encountered by SDU tenants. To document the various coping strategies deployed by SDU tenants, including spatial, emotional, relational, digital and collective strategies, to navigate socio-spatial constraints and household dynamics, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic. To analyse the role of neighbourhood attributes, such as public and social spaces, recreational and commercial areas, community facilities and infrastructure, in enabling or constraining SDU tenants to improvise their everyday lives.

23607522.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23607522.value: Background: While a growing body of literature has drawn attention to the emergence of informal housing, a form of accommodation that exists beyond formal regulations, few studies in Hong Kong have explicated how women, usually the primary homemakers, are disproportionately affected by housing informality. Additionally, in general, few studies have shed light on the agency of tenants, thus failing to acknowledge their resilience. Focusing on families living in subdivided units (SDUs) in Hong Kong, this study examines the intersections of gender and other forms of marginalisation in the context of informal housing and documents how SDU tenants negotiate spatial and structural constraints through everyday practices. Study aims: Building on the PI’s pilot study, the project will 1) investigate the ways in which informal housing in Hong Kong shapes gender relations and reproduces gender inequality; 2) examine how different forms of inequality, such as class and migration status, are intertwined with and reinforced by informal housing; 3) document the agency of SDU tenants and the strategies they deploy to navigate socio-spatial constraints and family dynamics; and 4) analyse the role of the neighbourhood in enabling or restraining SDU tenants to improvise their everyday lives. Method of analysis: The study will use qualitative methods, including in-depth interviews and ethnographic observation. A total of 40 families, including low-income, middle-income, local and migrant families, will be interviewed. Ethnographic observation will be conducted in two neighbourhoods in Hong Kong where SDUs are highly concentrated. The study will adopt an intersectional framework to examine the impact of gender, class and migration on the lives of SDU tenants at the individual, familial and community levels. The themes to be investigated will include the housing trajectories of SDU tenants, the domestic division of labour, family relations and practices, spatial strategies, the uses of domestic and public spaces, and the interactions between neighbourhood attributes and SDU tenants’ daily lives. Significance: The study has the potential to advance theories of gender, space, family and housing informality by highlighting the interplay of gender and spatial injustice and delineating the structural pathways that reproduce intersectional inequalities within the housing and spatial domain. It will also contribute to the conceptualisation of the everyday resilience of marginalised groups. Practically, the study will provide substantive and nuanced information to support the formulation, implementation and evaluation of social policies and offer directions for developing service programmes and community initiatives to improve the lives of SDU tenants. 背景：近年，不少研究均指出非正規住房──一種存在於正規制度之外的房屋，在世界各地愈益普遍，包括香港的劏房現象。本地研究主要集中在劏房的法規、租務和住房條件，卻缺乏性別視覺，因而忽略了作為主要家務勞動者和照顧者的女性在住房的非正規化下所受的影響。同時，現有的研究亦少有分析劏房住戶的主體性，因而令住戶的韌性和能動性未被足夠的肯定和闡述。此研究聚焦於劏房家庭，以分析非正規住房如何強化和再製性別及交織性不平等，並記錄劏房住戶如何透過日常策略以應對空間和制度性的限制。 研究目的：在前導研究的基礎上，此研究將進一步1）分析香港的非正規住房如何塑造性別關係和再製性別不平等；2）疏理交織性不平等，如階級和移民身份，如何透過非正規住房現象互為強化；3）記錄劏房住戶的主體性及其應對社會性的空間限制和家庭需求所採取的策略；4）檢視社區如何賦能或限制劏房住戶湊合日常生活。 研究方法：此調查採用質性研究方法，包括深入訪談和民族誌觀察。調查將採訪40個不同收入及移民背景的家庭，並在劏房高度集中的兩個社區進行民族誌觀察。本研究將採用交織性理論框架來闡釋性別、階級和移民身份的不平等對劏房住戶在個人、家庭和社區層面的生活所產生的影響。研究的主題包括劏房住戶的住房經歷、家庭分工、家庭關係和實踐、空間策略、對家庭和公共空間的使用，以及社區和劏房住戶的日常生活之間的互動。 研究貢獻：透過分析交織性不平等如何透過性別和空間強化和再製，並疏理多面向壓迫的結構性途徑，本研究能深化對性別、空間、家庭和非正式住房的理論探討，並有助發展弱勢群體的主體性和日常韌性的理論建構。同時，本研究能反映劏房住戶的實際生活經歷和需要，以促進社會政策的制訂、實施和評估，並為服務發展和社區倡議提供可行方向，以改善劏房家庭的生活水平。

23608222.label: Project Title(Chinese)
23608222.value: 以培養可持續發展能力為目標的高校教學轉型——基於香港公立大學的整體框架探索

23608222.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23608222.value: Higher education has been increasingly regarded as a critical venue for achieving the United Nations’ 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). More importantly, higher education institutions (HEIs) are taking responsibility for promoting sustainability ideas and practices to the young generations through teaching and learning and the general society through their service and impact to the communities and societies. The efforts of the Hong Kong public higher education sector in integrating sustainability into institutional strategies and practices have received recognition. The Hong Kong Sustainable Campus Consortium (HKSCC) has successfully coordinated the efforts of eight University Grants Committee (UGC)-funded institutions in promoting sustainability on campuses. However, HKSCC primarily focuses on environmental management at the institutional level. Also, the educational function of HKSCC practices is more based on informal education settings to enhance university students’ sustainability awareness. Therefore, much attention is needed to be paid to integrating sustainability into teaching and learning in both formal and informal contexts. To explore the ways of transforming higher education teaching and learning for sustainability, this study examines the relevant aspects of sustainability-related courses and extracurricular activities for students and professional development programs for faculty members at eight UGC-funded universities in Hong Kong. Through a mixed-methods approach by survey questionnaire and semi-structured in-depth interviews with students, faculty members, and administrators from eight UGC-funded universities, this study aims to investigate the current status, challenges, and good practices of integrating sustainability into teaching and learning at eight universities. Ultimately, based on collected quantitative and qualitative data and the review of the facilitating characteristics of Hong Kong higher education in promoting sustainability education, this study aims to propose a holistic framework as a pragmatic roadmap for eight UGC-universities to integrate sustainability into their teaching and learning practices to cultivate sustainability competencies for both students and faculty. 高等教育越來越被視為實現聯合國17項可持續發展目標(SDGs)的重要手段。更重要的是，高等教育機構正在承擔責任，通過教學向年輕一代推廣可持續發展的理念和實踐，並通過社會服務向廣大的社區推廣可持續發展教育。香港公立高等教育界將可持續發展納入機構策略和實踐的努力已獲得認可。香港可持續校園聯盟(HKSCC)的建立成功協調了八間教資委(UGC)資助大學在促進校園可持續發展方面的努力。然而，各所院校主要關注機構層面的環境管理。此外，香港可持續校園聯盟實踐的教育功能更多基於非正式教育環境，以提高大學生的可持續發展意識。因此，將可持續發展教育融入正式和非正式的教學值得關注。為探討通過大學的教學轉型來促進可持續發展教育的方法，本研究調查了八所教資會資助大學與可持續發展相關的課程、課外活動以及教師的專業發展計劃。本研究通過問卷調查和半結構化深度訪談，對八所大學的學生、教職員工和行政人員進行深入調查，旨在探討將可持續發展教育融入正式教學的現狀、挑戰和良好實踐。最終，基於收集到的定量和定性數據，以及梳理香港高等教育在促進可持續發展教育方面的特點，本研究旨在提出一個整體框架，作為八所大學將可持續發展教育有效融入教學的務實路線圖，以培養學生和教師的可持續發展能力。

24106022.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24106022.value: 多發性硬化症 (Multiple Sclerosis, MS) 是最常見的中樞神經系統脫髓鞘疾病，也是導致年輕人神經性殘障的主要成因之一。雖然疾病活躍度具有可逆轉性，但也會造成不可逆轉的後遺症。因此早期治療的重要目標是儘量減少進一步的組織損傷。早期識別和治療活躍性疾病可以降低殘疾的風險。 磁力共振成像 (MRI) 通過識別活躍性脫髓鞘斑塊，在評估疾病活躍度中發揮了核心作用。注射含釓造影劑後的病變信號增強是活躍性炎症和活躍性疾病的關鍵成像特徵。儘管許多常規 MS MRI 協議包括釓造影劑成像，但是造影劑的使用會有帶來不良後果的風險。相對而言，使用無造影劑的常規序列和功能性技術（如彌散成像）檢測活躍性疾病的診斷準確性低很多。最近有研究用 T1 或 T2 弛豫時間的定量技術來評估活躍性疾病。但這些定量技術存在固有的局限性。迄今為止，現有的非增強 MRI 方法檢測活躍性疾病仍具有明顯的局限性。 T1rho 成像是一種新的 MRI 技術，在檢測活躍性炎症和 MS 斑塊成像方面具有顯著潛力。該技術不需要外源性造影劑且具有高空間分辨率。T1rho成像的潛在用途是能夠準確評估活躍性 MS 患者，從而進行適當治療和降低致殘率。 我們在 T1rho 技術上的顯著進展使得該技術能夠可靠地用於臨床實踐。我們從研究表明，我們的方法在定量腦組織方面可靠性非常高。在一組試驗組患者中，我們觀察到活躍性和非活躍性 MS 病變的 T1rho 值存在差異。對此我們假設這是由於急性炎症、炎性細胞浸潤和蛋白表達導致急性病變的 T1rho 值延長所致。為了驗證這一觀察結果，擬定的研究將招募復發緩解型多發性硬化症患者，並獲得活躍性和非活躍性 MS 病變的定量 T1rho 測量值。該研究將比較活躍性和非活躍性 MS 腦部病變的 T1rho 值，並確定 T1rho 在多發性硬化症非侵入性評估中的診斷價值。

24107022.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24107022.value: 新冠疫苗與誘發腦神經疾病的關係

24107022.label: Project Objectives
24107022.value: To determine the risk of radiological strokes and neurodegeneration in community-dwelling individuals who received CoronaVac or Pfizer-BioNTech Comirnaty. To determine the risk factors that contribute to the above complications in individuals who received CoronaVac or Comirnaty. To explore the protective factors that may prevent the above complications from CoronaVac or Comirnaty use.
rows: To determine the risk of radiological strokes and neurodegeneration in community-dwelling individuals who received CoronaVac or Pfizer-BioNTech Comirnaty.
To determine the risk factors that contribute to the above complications in individuals who received CoronaVac or Comirnaty.
To explore the protective factors that may prevent the above complications from CoronaVac or Comirnaty use.

24107022.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24107022.value: As of 31st August 2021, the Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic had globally infected more than 200 million people and caused more than 4.5 million deaths. Strong evidence suggested that brain-related complications occurred in up to one-third of COVID-19 patients during both acute and convalescence phase, which may further attribute to stroke and cognitive decline in the long run. The emergency use authorization of COVID-19 vaccinations instilled hope for better control of the global pandemic. Media coverage raised safety concerns about COVID-19 vaccinations, including CoronaVac and Pfizer-BioNTech Comirnaty, that are in use in Hong Kong. Emerging evidence also reported an increased stroke risk following vaccination. Whether the neurological damages caused by COVID-19 can happen with vaccination must be elucidated through scientific research. In the proposed prospective cohort study, we aim to longitudinally compare the pre- and post-vaccination clinical, neuroimaging and immunologic profiles with unvaccinated controls. We shall recruit 500 consecutive citizens from a prospective community-based cohort from the Chinese University of Hong Kong Brain Health Research Centre, which consists of community-dwelling individuals who are free of neurological diseases. The cohort had undergone baseline cognitive assessment, blood tests and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) before the global pandemic. We shall dichotomize the study participants into the vaccinated and unvaccinated group. Vaccinated participants will receive cognitive assessment, blood tests and MRI brain 16 ± 4 weeks after the completion of the 2nd dose of either CoronaVac or Comirnaty. Levels of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein neutralizing antibody and cytokines will also be measured. The control group, i.e. unvaccinated individuals, will also undergo the above assessments. With expert clinical assessment and artificial-intelligence assisted brain imaging assessment, we shall identify and compare brain pathologies such as incident strokes, cognitive decline, radiological infarcts, microhemorrhages, small vessel disease, intracranial large artery atherosclerosis, and brain volumes among individuals with different vaccination status. Preliminary analyses of 15 participants revealed no significant differences in changes in brain volumes and white matter hyperintensities with different vaccination status. Our study may reveal the effect of COVID-19 vaccination on brain health and identify risk factors associated with neurological events following COVID-19 vaccines. Results of this study may impact on vaccination strategies amidst the global health emergency. 2019冠狀病毒病（COVID-19）疫情持續肆虐，為全球帶來沉重的疾病負擔。為減低新型冠狀病毒對公共衞生及社會的影響，2019冠狀病毒病疫苗（新冠疫苗）被視為一項減低傳播率及透過增加人群免疫以達致控制疫情的中長期重要公共衞生措施。隨着疫苗接種覆蓋率於全球各地上升，對於新冠疫苗與誘發腦神經疾病的關係，目前仍存在較大爭議。了解疫苗的安全及副作用，將可減低市民對接種疫苗的疑慮。我們希望透過是次研究來探索及闡釋新冠疫苗對腦神經系統的影響，使社會大眾能更掌握疫苗接種的風險及副作用。

24107022.label: Realisation of objectives
24107022.value: We have realised all project objectives. We recruited 415 subjects in the funded project, of which190 received BNT162b2, 152 received CoronaVac, and 73 remained unvaccinated. A total of 60 (14.4%) had COVID-19 infection before follow-up MRI, and 109 (26.3%) developed the primary outcome of radiological cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) progression. Firstly, regarding our objective to determine the risk of radiological strokes and neurodegeneration in community-dwelling individuals who received CoronaVac or Comirnaty. We found that neither BNT162b2 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.61, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.30-1.26, P = 0.179) nor CoronaVac (aOR 0.71, 95% CI 0.34-1.47, P = 0.349) was associated with cSVD progression. Secondly, regarding our objective to determine the risk factors that contribute to the above complications in individuals who received CoronaVac or Comirnaty, we found among the BNT162b2 recipients, a higher surrogate virus neutralization test was associated (aOR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95-0.99, P = 0.002) with a lower risk of cSVD progression. Thirdly, regarding our objective to explore the protective factors that may prevent the above complications from CoronaVac or Comirnaty use. We found that dyslipidemia and increase in white cell count were risk factors of cSVD progression in our study, which reflects that long-term stringent control of cardiovascular risks, such as hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and systemic inflammation, is, overall, more important than short-term predispositions, if any, by SARS-CoV-2 vaccination.

24107022.label: Major findings and research outcome
24107022.value: Objectives The association between SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and cerebrovascular diseases raised a concern of cerebrovascular safety of COVID-19 vaccines. We aimed to determine the risk of radiologic cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) progression with BNT162b2 and CoronaVac. Methods In this community-based prospective cohort study, community-dwelling subjects underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) before and 4 months after vaccination with BNT162b2 or CoronaVac. Unvaccinated subjects received serial brain MRI over a comparable interval. The primary outcome was progression of a composite of six standard cSVD biomarkers. We compared the risk of cSVD progression between vaccinated and unvaccinated subjects and identified predictors of primary outcome within each vaccine subgroup. Results Of the 415 subjects recruited, 190 received BNT162b2, 152 received CoronaVac, and 73 remained unvaccinated. A total of 60 (14.4%) had COVID-19 infection before follow-up MRI, and 109 (26.3%) developed the primary outcome. Neither BNT162b2 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.61, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.30-1.26, P = 0.179) nor CoronaVac (aOR 0.71, 95% CI 0.34-1.47, P = 0.349) was associated with cSVD progression. Among the BNT162b2 recipients, a higher surrogate virus neutralization test was associated (aOR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95-0.99, P = 0.002) with a lower risk of cSVD progression. Conclusions BNT162b2 and CoronaVac did not increase cSVD burden in community-dwelling citizens. The association between surrogate virus neutralization test and cSVD progression among BNT162b2 recipients requires further investigation.

24107022.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24107022.value: Our project has established a prospective cohort of patients who received a live attenuated or mRNA COVID-19 vaccination. Our project did not reveal a medium-term effect by these vaccinations on cerebral small vessel disease and neurodegeneration. The cohort established in the study will undergo follow-up with longitudinal assessment of clinical outcomes (e.g. stroke, dementia) and interval cognitive assessment to reveal possible long term effect of COVID-19 vaccination. The data generated from the study also created a solid foundation for future longitudinal studies related to brain health.

24107022.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24107022.value: The risk of cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) with COVID-19 vaccines was unknown. In our study, we demonstrated reassuring results that BNT162b2 and CoronaVac were not associated with radiologic cSVD progression. However, in patients who received BNT162b2 and did not mount an appropriate immune response may have an increased risk of cSVD progression, which necessitates further studies in this group of patients.
